### 216

**pi** `94346–97674`
Rūpakkhandho abyākato. Cattāro khandhā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Dve khandhā na vattabbā – "sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi, "dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi, "adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi. Tayo khandhā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Rūpakkhandho nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Cattāro khandhā siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Rūpakkhandho siyā upādinnupādāniyo, siyā anupādinnupādāniyo . Cattāro khandhā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. ⤵ Rūpakkhandho asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko. Cattāro khandhā siyā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Rūpakkhandho avitakkaavicāro. Tayo khandhā siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā savitakkasavicāro, siyā avitakkavicāramatto, siyā avitakkaavicāro, siyā na vattabbo – "savitakkasavicāro"tipi, "avitakkavicāramatto"tipi, "avitakkaavicāro"tipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – "pītisahagato"tipi, "sukhasahagato"tipi, "upekkhāsahagato"tipi. Vedanākkhandho siyā pītisahagato na sukhasahagato na upekkhāsahagato, siyā na vattabbo – "pītisahagato"ti. Tayo khandhā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na vattabbā – "pītisahagatā"tipi, "sukhasahagatā"tipi, "upekkhāsahagatā"tipi. ⤵ Rūpakkhandho neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Cattāro khandhā siyā dassanena pahātabbā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Rūpakkhandho neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Cattāro khandhā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Rūpakkhandho nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī. Cattāro khandhā siyā ācayagāmino, siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Rūpakkhandho nevasekkhanāsekkho. Cattāro khandhā siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā, siyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Rūpakkhandho paritto. Cattāro khandhā siyā parittā, siyā mahaggatā, siyā appamāṇā. Rūpakkhandho anārammaṇo. Cattāro khandhā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – "parittārammaṇā"tipi , "mahaggatārammaṇā"tipi, "appamāṇārammaṇā"tipi. Rūpakkhandho majjhimo. Cattāro khandhā siyā hīnā, siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Rūpakkhandho aniyato . Cattāro khandhā siyā micchattaniyatā, siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. ⤵ Rūpakkhandho anārammaṇo. Cattāro khandhā siyā maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā – "maggārammaṇā"tipi, "maggahetukā"tipi , "maggādhipatino"tipi; siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino; siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Rūpakkhandho anārammaṇo. Cattāro khandhā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – "atītārammaṇā"tipi, "anāgatārammaṇā"tipi, "paccuppannārammaṇā"tipi; siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Rūpakkhandho anārammaṇo. Cattāro khandhā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – "ajjhattārammaṇā"tipi, "bahiddhārammaṇā"tipi, "ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā"tipi. Cattāro khandhā anidassanaappaṭighā. Rūpakkhandho siyā sanidassanasappaṭigho, siyā anidassanasappaṭigho, siyā anidassanaappaṭigho.

**en** `151144–155364`
The aggregate of material form is neutral. The other four aggregates may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. Two aggregates cannot be described as joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. Three aggregates may be joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The aggregate of material form is neither a result nor something that produces results. The other four aggregates may be results, may produce results, or may be neither. The aggregate of material form may be taken up at birth and able to be clung to, or not taken up but able to be clung to. The other four aggregates may be taken up and able to be clung to, not taken up but able to be clung to, or neither taken up nor able to be clung to. ⤵ The aggregate of material form is undefiled yet open to defilement. The other four aggregates may be defiled and open to defilement, undefiled yet open to defilement, or neither defiled nor open to defilement. The aggregate of material form is without thought and examination. Three aggregates may have both thought and examination, may have examination only, or may have neither. The aggregate of mental formations may have both thought and examination, may have examination only, may have neither, or may not be describable as any of these. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as accompanied by joy, accompanied by happiness, or accompanied by equanimity. The aggregate of feeling may be accompanied by joy but is not accompanied by happiness or equanimity, or it may not be describable as accompanied by joy. Three aggregates may be accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity, or may not be describable as accompanied by any of these. ⤵ The aggregate of material form is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. The other four aggregates may be abandoned by seeing, may be abandoned by development, or may be abandoned by neither. The aggregate of material form has root causes to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. The other four aggregates may have root causes to be abandoned by seeing, root causes to be abandoned by development, or root causes to be abandoned by neither. The aggregate of material form neither leads to further accumulation nor to dismantling. The other four aggregates may lead to accumulation, may lead to dismantling, or may lead to neither. The aggregate of material form belongs neither to trainees nor to those beyond training. The other four aggregates may belong to trainees, to those beyond training, or to neither. The aggregate of material form is limited. The other four aggregates may be limited, expanded, or measureless. The aggregate of material form has no object. The other four aggregates may have a limited object, an expanded object, or a measureless object, or may not be describable as having any of these. The aggregate of material form is middling. The other four aggregates may be inferior, middling, or superior. The aggregate of material form is not fixed in its outcome. The other four aggregates may be fixed in wrongness, fixed in rightness, or not fixed. ⤵ The aggregate of material form has no object. The other four aggregates may have the path as their object, the path as their cause, or the path as their dominant factor, or may not be describable as any of these; they may have arisen, may not have arisen, or may be bound to arise; they may be past, future, or present. The aggregate of material form has no object. The other four aggregates may have a past object, a future object, or a present object, or may not be describable as having any of these; they may be internal, external, or both internal and external. The aggregate of material form has no object. The other four aggregates may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external, or may not be describable as having any of these. Four aggregates are invisible and offer no resistance. The aggregate of material form may be visible and offer resistance, may be invisible and offer resistance, or may be invisible and offer no resistance.

### 217

**pi** `97675–97692`
<h2>2. Dukaṃ</h2>

**en** `155365–155386`

### 218

**pi** `97693–98940`
Cattāro khandhā na hetū. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā hetu, siyā na hetu. Rūpakkhandho ahetuko. Cattāro khandhā siyā sahetukā, siyā ahetukā. Rūpakkhandho hetuvippayutto. Cattāro khandhā siyā hetusampayuttā, siyā hetuvippayuttā. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – "hetu ceva sahetuko cā"tipi, "sahetuko ceva na ca hetū"tipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – "hetū ceva sahetukā cā"ti, siyā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū, siyā na vattabbā – "sahetukā ceva na ca hetū"ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā hetu ceva sahetuko ca, siyā sahetuko ceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbo – "hetu ceva sahetuko cā"tipi, "sahetuko ceva na ca hetū"tipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – "hetu ceva hetusampayutto cā"tipi, "hetusampayutto ceva na ca hetū"tipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – "hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cā"ti, siyā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū, siyā na vattabbā – "hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū"ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, siyā hetusampayutto ceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbo – "hetu ceva hetusampayutto cā"tipi, "hetusampayutto ceva na ca hetū"tipi. Rūpakkhandho na hetu ahetuko . Tayo khandhā siyā na hetū sahetukā, siyā na hetū ahetukā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā na hetu sahetuko, siyā na hetu ahetuko, siyā na vattabbo – "na hetu sahetuko"tipi, "na hetu ahetuko"tipi.

**en** `155387–157031`
Four aggregates are not root causes. The aggregate of mental formations may be a root cause or not. The aggregate of material form is without root causes. The other four aggregates may have root causes or not. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from root causes. The other four aggregates may be joined with root causes or dissociated from them. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "a root cause with root causes" or as "having root causes without being a root cause". Three aggregates cannot be described as "root causes with root causes"; they may have root causes without being root causes, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be a root cause with root causes, may have root causes without being a root cause, or may not be describable as either. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "a root cause joined with root causes" or as "joined with root causes without being a root cause". Three aggregates cannot be described as "root causes joined with root causes"; they may be joined with root causes without being root causes, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be a root cause joined with root causes, may be joined with root causes without being a root cause, or may not be describable as either. The aggregate of material form is not a root cause and is without root causes. Three aggregates may be not root causes with root causes, or not root causes without root causes. The aggregate of mental formations may be not a root cause with root causes, not a root cause without root causes, or not describable as either.

### 219

**pi** `98941–98962`
Sappaccayā, saṅkhatā.

**en** `157032–157076`
All five have conditions and are compounded.

### 220

**pi** `98963–99257`
Cattāro khandhā anidassanā. Rūpakkhandho siyā sanidassano, siyā anidassano. Cattāro khandhā appaṭighā. Rūpakkhandho siyā sappaṭigho, siyā appaṭigho. Rūpakkhandho rūpaṃ. Cattāro khandhā arūpā. Rūpakkhandho lokiyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā; kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.

**en** `157077–157531`
Four aggregates are invisible. The aggregate of material form may be visible or invisible. Four aggregates offer no resistance. The aggregate of material form may offer resistance or not. The aggregate of material form is material. The other four aggregates are immaterial. The aggregate of material form is worldly. The other four aggregates may be worldly or beyond the world; all are knowable by some kinds of consciousness and not knowable by others.

### 221

**pi** `99258–100479`
Cattāro khandhā no āsavā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā āsavo, siyā no āsavo. Rūpakkhandho sāsavo. Cattāro khandhā siyā sāsavā, siyā anāsavā. Rūpakkhandho āsavavippayutto. Cattāro khandhā siyā āsavasampayuttā, siyā āsavavippayuttā. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – "āsavo ceva sāsavo cā"ti, sāsavo ceva no ca āsavo. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – "āsavā ceva sāsavā cā"ti, siyā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā, siyā na vattabbā – "sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā"ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā āsavo ceva sāsavo ca, siyā sāsavo ceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbo – "āsavo ceva sāsavo cā"tipi, "sāsavo ceva no ca āsavo"tipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – "āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto cā"tipi, "āsavasampayutto ceva no ca āsavo"tipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – "āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cā"ti, siyā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā, siyā na vattabbā – "āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā"ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, siyā āsavasampayutto ceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbo – "āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto cā"tipi, "āsavasampayutto ceva no ca āsavo"tipi. Rūpakkhandho āsavavippayuttasāsavo. Cattāro khandhā siyā āsavavippayuttasāsavā, siyā āsavavippayuttaanāsavā, siyā na vattabbā – "āsavavippayuttasāsavā"tipi, "āsavavippayuttaanāsavā"tipi.

**en** `157532–159070`
Four aggregates are not mental taints. The aggregate of mental formations may be a taint or not. The aggregate of material form is subject to the taints. The other four aggregates may be subject to the taints or free of them. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from the taints. The other four aggregates may be joined with the taints or dissociated from them. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "a taint subject to the taints"; it is subject to the taints without being a taint. Three aggregates cannot be described as "taints subject to the taints"; they may be subject to the taints without being taints, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be a taint subject to the taints, may be subject to the taints without being a taint, or may not be describable as either. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "a taint joined with the taints" or as "joined with the taints without being a taint". Three aggregates cannot be described as "taints joined with the taints"; they may be joined with the taints without being taints, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be a taint joined with the taints, may be joined with the taints without being a taint, or may not be describable as either. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from the taints yet subject to them. The other four aggregates may be dissociated from the taints yet subject to them, dissociated from them and free of them, or not describable as either.

### 222

**pi** `100480–101948`
Cattāro khandhā no saṃyojanā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā saṃyojanaṃ, siyā no saṃyojanaṃ. Rūpakkhandho saṃyojaniyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā saṃyojaniyā, siyā asaṃyojaniyā. Rūpakkhandho saṃyojanavippayutto. Cattāro khandhā siyā saṃyojanasampayuttā, siyā saṃyojanavippayuttā. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – "saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyo cā"ti, "saṃyojaniyo ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ". Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – "saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā cā"ti, siyā saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā, siyā na vattabbā – "saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā"ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyo ca, siyā saṃyojaniyo ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbo – "saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyo cā"tipi, "saṃyojaniyo ceva no ca saṃyojana"ntipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – "saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayutto cā"tipi, "saṃyojanasampayutto ceva no ca saṃyojana"ntipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – "saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā cā"ti, siyā saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā, siyā na vattabbā – "saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā"ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayutto ca, siyā saṃyojanasampayutto ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbo – "saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayutto cā"tipi, "saṃyojanasampayutto ceva no ca saṃyojana"ntipi. Rūpakkhandho saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā, siyā saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā, siyā na vattabbā – "saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā"tipi, "saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā"tipi.

**en** `159071–160589`
Four aggregates are not fetters. The aggregate of mental formations may be a fetter or not. The aggregate of material form can be bound by the fetters. The other four aggregates may be able to be bound or not. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from the fetters. The other four aggregates may be joined with the fetters or dissociated from them. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "a fetter that can be bound"; it can be bound without being a fetter. Three aggregates cannot be described as "fetters that can be bound"; they may be able to be bound without being fetters, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be a fetter that can be bound, may be able to be bound without being a fetter, or may not be describable as either. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "a fetter joined with the fetters" or as "joined with the fetters without being a fetter". Three aggregates cannot be described as "fetters joined with the fetters"; they may be joined with the fetters without being fetters, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be a fetter joined with the fetters, may be joined with the fetters without being a fetter, or may not be describable as either. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from the fetters yet able to be bound. The other four aggregates may be dissociated from the fetters yet able to be bound, dissociated from them and unable to be bound, or not describable as either.

### 223

Cattāro khandhā no ganthā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā gantho, siyā no gantho. Rūpakkhandho ganthaniyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā ganthaniyā, siyā aganthaniyā. Rūpakkhandho ganthavippayutto. Four aggregates are not ties. The aggregate of mental formations may be a tie or not. The aggregate of material form can be tied. The other four aggregates may be able to be tied or not. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from the ties. The other four aggregates may be joined with the ties or dissociated from them. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "a tie that can be tied"; it can be tied without being a tie. Three aggregates cannot be described as "ties that can be tied"; they may be able to be tied without being ties, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be a tie joined with the ties, may be joined with the ties without being a tie, or may not be describable as either. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from the ties yet able to be tied. The other four aggregates may be dissociated from the ties yet able to be tied, dissociated from them and unable to be tied, or not describable as either.

### 224

There are twelve sense-fields – the eye sense-field, the sense-field of sights, the ear sense-field, the sense-field of sounds, the nose sense-field, the sense-field of smells, the tongue sense-field, the sense-field of tastes, the body sense-field, the sense-field of things touched, the mind sense-field, and the sense-field of mental objects. ⤵ The eye is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Sights are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. The ear is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Sounds are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. The nose is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Smells are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. The tongue is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Tastes are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. The body is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Things touched are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. The mind is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Mental objects are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change.

### 237

**pi** `112633–112652`
Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

**en** `174176–174235`
The Classification According to the Discourses is finished.

### 238

**pi** `112653–112685`
<h1>2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ</h1>

**en** `174236–174290`
<h1>2. Classification According to the Abhidhamma</h1>

### 239

**pi** `112686–112874`
Dvādasāyatanāni – cakkhāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ.

**en** `174291–174636`
There are twelve sense-fields – the eye sense-field, the ear sense-field, the nose sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the body sense-field, the mind sense-field, the sense-field of sights, the sense-field of sounds, the sense-field of smells, the sense-field of tastes, the sense-field of things touched, and the sense-field of mental objects.

### 240

**pi** `112875–113381`
Tattha katamaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ cakkhu [cakkhuṃ (sī. syā. ka.) dha. sa. 596-599] catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo attabhāvapariyāpanno anidassano sappaṭigho, yena cakkhunā anidassanena sappaṭighena rūpaṃ sanidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ passi vā passati vā passissati vā passe vā, cakkhumpetaṃ cakkhāyatanampetaṃ cakkhudhātupesā cakkhundriyampetaṃ lokopeso dvārāpesā samuddopeso paṇḍarampetaṃ khettampetaṃ vatthumpetaṃ nettampetaṃ nayanampetaṃ orimaṃ tīrampetaṃ suñño gāmopeso. Idaṃ vuccati "cakkhāyatanaṃ" .

**en** `174637–175291`
Therein, what is the eye sense-field? The eye that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements, included in one's own body, invisible, and offering resistance; the eye – itself invisible and offering resistance – by which one has seen, sees, will see, or may see a sight that is visible and offers resistance: this is the eye, this is the eye sense-field, this is the eye element, this is the eye faculty; this is a world, this is a door, this is an ocean; this is the bright surface, this is a field, this is a base; this is a guide, this is an eye; this is the near shore, this is an empty village. This is called "the eye sense-field".

### 241

**pi** `113382–113801`
Tattha katamaṃ sotāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ sotaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo attabhāvapariyāpanno anidassano sappaṭigho, yena sotena anidassanena sappaṭighena saddaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ suṇi vā suṇāti vā suṇissati vā suṇe vā, sotampetaṃ sotāyatanampetaṃ sotadhātupesā sotindriyampetaṃ lokopeso dvārāpesā samuddopeso paṇḍarampetaṃ khettampetaṃ vatthumpetaṃ orimaṃ tīrampetaṃ suñño gāmopeso. Idaṃ vuccati "sotāyatanaṃ".

**en** `175292–175919`
Therein, what is the ear sense-field? The ear that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements, included in one's own body, invisible, and offering resistance; the ear – itself invisible and offering resistance – by which one has heard, hears, will hear, or may hear a sound that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the ear, this is the ear sense-field, this is the ear element, this is the ear faculty; this is a world, this is a door, this is an ocean; this is the bright surface, this is a field, this is a base; this is the near shore, this is an empty village. This is called "the ear sense-field".

### 242

**pi** `113802–114234`
Tattha katamaṃ ghānāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ ghānaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo attabhāvapariyāpanno anidassano sappaṭigho, yena ghānena anidassanena sappaṭighena gandhaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ ghāyi vā ghāyati vā ghāyissati vā ghāye vā, ghānampetaṃ ghānāyatanampetaṃ ghānadhātupesā ghānindriyampetaṃ lokopeso dvārāpesā samuddopeso paṇḍarampetaṃ khettampetaṃ vatthumpetaṃ orimaṃ tīrampetaṃ suñño gāmopeso. Idaṃ vuccati "ghānāyatanaṃ".

**en** `175920–176560`
Therein, what is the nose sense-field? The nose that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements, included in one's own body, invisible, and offering resistance; the nose – itself invisible and offering resistance – by which one has smelled, smells, will smell, or may smell a smell that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the nose, this is the nose sense-field, this is the nose element, this is the nose faculty; this is a world, this is a door, this is an ocean; this is the bright surface, this is a field, this is a base; this is the near shore, this is an empty village. This is called "the nose sense-field".

### 243

**pi** `114235–114657`
Tattha katamaṃ jivhāyatanaṃ? Yā jivhā catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo attabhāvapariyāpanno anidassano sappaṭigho, yāya jivhāya anidassanāya sappaṭighāya rasaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ sāyi vā sāyati vā sāyissati vā sāye vā, jivhāpesā jivhāyatanampetaṃ jivhādhātupesā jīvhindriyampetaṃ lokopeso dvārāpesā samuddopeso paṇḍarampetaṃ khettampetaṃ vatthumpetaṃ orimaṃ tīrampetaṃ suñño gāmopeso. Idaṃ vuccati "jivhāyatanaṃ".

**en** `176561–177216`
Therein, what is the tongue sense-field? The tongue that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements, included in one's own body, invisible, and offering resistance; the tongue – itself invisible and offering resistance – by which one has tasted, tastes, will taste, or may taste a taste that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the tongue, this is the tongue sense-field, this is the tongue element, this is the tongue faculty; this is a world, this is a door, this is an ocean; this is the bright surface, this is a field, this is a base; this is the near shore, this is an empty village. This is called "the tongue sense-field".

### 244

**pi** `114658–115082`
Tattha katamaṃ kāyāyatanaṃ? Yo kāyo catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo attabhāvapariyāpanno anidassano sappaṭigho, yena kāyena anidassanena sappaṭighena phoṭṭhabbaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ phusi vā phusati vā phusissati vā phuse vā, kāyopeso kāyāyatanampetaṃ kāyadhātupesā kāyindriyampetaṃ lokopeso dvārāpesā samuddopeso paṇḍarampetaṃ khettampetaṃ vatthumpetaṃ orimaṃ tīrampetaṃ suñño gāmopeso. Idaṃ vuccati "kāyāyatanaṃ".

**en** `177217–177870`
Therein, what is the body sense-field? The body that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements, included in one's own body, invisible, and offering resistance; the body – itself invisible and offering resistance – by which one has touched, touches, will touch, or may touch something touchable that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the body, this is the body sense-field, this is the body element, this is the body faculty; this is a world, this is a door, this is an ocean; this is the bright surface, this is a field, this is a base; this is the near shore, this is an empty village. This is called "the body sense-field".

### 245

**pi** `115083–116872`
Tattha katamaṃ manāyatanaṃ? Ekavidhena manāyatanaṃ – phassasampayuttaṃ. ⤵ Duvidhena manāyatanaṃ – atthi sahetukaṃ, atthi ahetukaṃ. ⤵ Tividhena manāyatanaṃ – atthi kusalaṃ, atthi akusalaṃ, atthi abyākataṃ. ⤵ Catubbidhena manāyatanaṃ – atthi kāmāvacaraṃ, atthi rūpāvacaraṃ, atthi arūpāvacaraṃ, atthi apariyāpannaṃ. ⤵ Pañcavidhena manāyatanaṃ – atthi sukhindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi dukkhindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi somanassindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi domanassindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi upekkhindriyasampayuttaṃ. ⤵ Chabbidhena manāyatanaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ. Evaṃ chabbidhena manāyatanaṃ. ⤵ Sattavidhena manāyatanaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu. Evaṃ sattavidhena manāyatanaṃ. ⤵ Aṭṭhavidhena manāyatanaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ atthi sukhasahagataṃ, atthi dukkhasahagataṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena manāyatanaṃ. ⤵ Navavidhena manāyatanaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu atthi kusalaṃ, atthi akusalaṃ, atthi abyākataṃ. Evaṃ navavidhena manāyatanaṃ. ⤵ Dasavidhena manāyatanaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ atthi sukhasahagataṃ, atthi dukkhasahagataṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu atthi kusalaṃ, atthi akusalaṃ, atthi abyākataṃ. Evaṃ dasavidhena manāyatanaṃ. ⤵ Ekavidhena manāyatanaṃ – phassasampayuttaṃ. ⤵ Duvidhena manāyatanaṃ – atthi sahetukaṃ, atthi ahetukaṃ. ⤵ Tividhena manāyatanaṃ – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ…pe…. Evaṃ bahuvidhena manāyatanaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati "manāyatanaṃ".

**en** `177871–180319`
Therein, what is the mind sense-field? As a single class, the mind sense-field is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is mind with a root cause, and mind without a root cause. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is wholesome mind, unwholesome mind, and neutral mind. ⤵ As a fourfold class: there is mind belonging to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, and mind not included in any sphere. ⤵ As a fivefold class: there is mind joined with the faculty of pleasure, joined with the faculty of pain, joined with the faculty of gladness, joined with the faculty of sadness, and joined with the faculty of equanimity. ⤵ As a sixfold class: there is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. This is the mind sense-field as a sixfold class. ⤵ As a sevenfold class: there is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element. This is the mind sense-field as a sevenfold class. ⤵ As an eightfold class: there is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness – which may be accompanied by pleasure or by pain – the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element. This is the mind sense-field as an eightfold class. ⤵ As a ninefold class: there is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the mind sense-field as a ninefold class. ⤵ As a tenfold class: there is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness – which may be accompanied by pleasure or by pain – the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the mind sense-field as a tenfold class. ⤵ As a single class, the mind sense-field is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is mind with a root cause, and mind without a root cause. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is mind joined with pleasant feeling, mind joined with painful feeling, and mind joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant… Thus the mind sense-field is classified in many ways. This is called "the mind sense-field".

### 246

**pi** `116873–117754`
Tattha katamaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya vaṇṇanibhā sanidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ nīlaṃ pītakaṃ lohitakaṃ [pītaṃ lohitaṃ (sī.)] odātaṃ kāḷakaṃ mañjiṭṭhakaṃ [mañjeṭṭhakaṃ (sī. syā.)] hari harivaṇṇaṃ ambaṅkuravaṇṇaṃ dīghaṃ rassaṃ aṇuṃ thūlaṃ vaṭṭaṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ caturassaṃ chaḷaṃsaṃ aṭṭhaṃsaṃ soḷasaṃsaṃ ninnaṃ thalaṃ chāyā ātapo āloko andhakāro abbhā mahikā dhūmo rajo candamaṇḍalassa vaṇṇanibhā sūriyamaṇḍalassa [suriyamaṇḍalassa (sī. syā. kaṃ.)] vaṇṇanibhā tārakarūpānaṃ vaṇṇanibhā ādāsamaṇḍalassa vaṇṇanibhā maṇisaṅkhamuttaveḷuriyassa vaṇṇanibhā jātarūparajatassa vaṇṇanibhā, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi rūpaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya vaṇṇanibhā sanidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ, yaṃ rūpaṃ sanidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ cakkhunā anidassanena sappaṭighena passi vā passati vā passissati vā passe vā, rūpampetaṃ rūpāyatanampetaṃ rūpadhātupesā. Idaṃ vuccati "rūpāyatanaṃ".

**en** `180320–181395`
Therein, what is the sense-field of sights? The sight that is the shining of colour derived from the four great elements, visible and offering resistance – blue, yellow, red, white, black, crimson, leaf-green, greenish, the colour of a mango shoot; long, short, small, large, round, circular, square, six-sided, eight-sided, sixteen-sided; low, high; shade and sunshine; light and darkness; cloud, mist, smoke, and dust; the shining colour of the moon's disc, the shining colour of the sun's disc, the shining colour of the stars, the shining colour of a mirror's disc, the shining colour of gems, conch shells, pearls, and cat's-eye, the shining colour of gold and silver; or whatever other sight there is, derived from the four great elements, the shining of colour, visible and offering resistance; the sight – visible and offering resistance – which one has seen, sees, will see, or may see with the eye that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a sight, this is the sense-field of sights, this is the element of sights. This is called "the sense-field of sights".

### 247

**pi** `117755–118316`
Tattha katamaṃ saddāyatanaṃ? Yo saddo catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho bherisaddo mudiṅgasaddo [mutiṅgasaddho (sī.)] saṅkhasaddo paṇavasaddo gītasaddo vāditasaddo sammasaddo pāṇisaddo sattānaṃ nigghosasaddo dhātūnaṃ sannighātasaddo vātasaddo udakasaddo manussasaddo amanussasaddo, yo vā panaññopi atthi saddo catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho, yaṃ saddaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ sotena anidassanena sappaṭighena suṇi vā suṇāti vā suṇissati vā suṇe vā, saddopeso saddāyatanampetaṃ saddadhātupesā. Idaṃ vuccati "saddāyatanaṃ".

**en** `181396–182254`
Therein, what is the sense-field of sounds? The sound that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance – the sound of drums, the sound of small drums, the sound of conches, the sound of tom-toms, the sound of singing, the sound of instruments, the sound of cymbals, the sound of clapping hands, the cries of living beings, the sound of elements colliding, the sound of wind, the sound of water, the sound of humans, the sound of non-humans; or whatever other sound there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance; the sound – invisible and offering resistance – which one has heard, hears, will hear, or may hear with the ear that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a sound, this is the sense-field of sounds, this is the element of sounds. This is called "the sense-field of sounds".

### 248

**pi** `118317–118794`
Tattha katamaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ? Yo gandho catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho mūlagandho sāragandho tacagandho pattagandho pupphagandho phalagandho āmagandho vissagandho sugandho duggandho, yo vā panaññopi atthi gandho catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho , yaṃ gandhaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ ghānena anidassanena sappaṭighena ghāyi vā ghāyati vā ghāyissati vā ghāye vā, gandhopeso gandhāyatanampetaṃ gandhadhātupesā. Idaṃ vuccati "gandhāyatanaṃ".

**en** `182255–182973`
Therein, what is the sense-field of smells? The smell that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance – the smell of roots, the smell of heartwood, the smell of bark, the smell of leaves, the smell of flowers, the smell of fruits, raw smells, putrid smells, pleasant smells, unpleasant smells; or whatever other smell there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance; the smell – invisible and offering resistance – which one has smelled, smells, will smell, or may smell with the nose that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a smell, this is the sense-field of smells, this is the element of smells. This is called "the sense-field of smells".

### 249

**pi** `118795–119317`
Tattha katamaṃ rasāyatanaṃ? Yo raso catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho mūlaraso khandharaso tacaraso pattaraso puppharaso phalaraso ambilaṃ madhuraṃ tittakaṃ kaṭukaṃ loṇikaṃ [lapilakaṃ (sī.), lampikaṃ (ka. sī.)] khārikaṃ lambikaṃ kasāvo sādu asādu, yo vā panaññopi atthi raso catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho, yaṃ rasaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ jivhāya anidassanāya sappaṭighāya sāyi vā sāyati vā sāyissati vā sāye vā, rasopeso rasāyatanampetaṃ rasadhātupesā. Idaṃ vuccati "rasāyatanaṃ".

**en** `182974–183713`
Therein, what is the sense-field of tastes? The taste that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance – the taste of roots, the taste of stems, the taste of bark, the taste of leaves, the taste of flowers, the taste of fruits; sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, salty, alkaline, acrid, astringent; tasty, unappetising; or whatever other taste there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance; the taste – invisible and offering resistance – which one has tasted, tastes, will taste, or may taste with the tongue that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a taste, this is the sense-field of tastes, this is the element of tastes. This is called "the sense-field of tastes".

### 250

**pi** `119318–119678`
Tattha katamaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ? Pathavīdhātu tejodhātu vāyodhātu kakkhaḷaṃ mudukaṃ saṇhaṃ pharusaṃ sukhasamphassaṃ dukkhasamphassaṃ garukaṃ lahukaṃ, yaṃ phoṭṭhabbaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ kāyena anidassanena sappaṭighena phusi vā phusati vā phusissati vā phuse vā, phoṭṭhabbopeso phoṭṭhabbāyatanampetaṃ phoṭṭhabbadhātupesā. Idaṃ vuccati "phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ".

**en** `183714–184236`
Therein, what is the sense-field of things touched? The earth element, the fire element, the air element; hard, soft, smooth, rough; pleasant to the touch, painful to the touch; heavy, light; the touchable thing – invisible and offering resistance – which one has touched, touches, will touch, or may touch with the body that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a touchable thing, this is the sense-field of things touched, this is the element of things touched. This is called "the sense-field of things touched".

### 251

**pi** `119679–121061`
Tattha katamaṃ dhammāyatanaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu. ⤵ Tattha katamo vedanākkhandho? Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto. Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho. Ayaṃ vuccati "vedanākkhandho". ⤵ Tattha katamo saññākkhandho? Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto. Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena saññākkhandho. Ayaṃ vuccati "saññākkhandho". ⤵ Tattha katamo saṅkhārakkhandho? Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi hetu, atthi na hetu. Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho. Ayaṃ vuccati "saṅkhārakkhandho". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ? Itthindriyaṃ purisindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. Idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ "anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamā asaṅkhatā dhātu? Rāgakkhayo , dosakkhayo, mohakkhayo – ayaṃ vuccati "asaṅkhatā dhātu".

**en** `184237–186459`
Therein, what is the sense-field of mental objects? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the material form that is invisible and offers no resistance and is included in the sense-field of mental objects, and the unconditioned element. ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of feeling? As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is joined with contact. As a twofold class: there is feeling with a root cause, and feeling without one. As a threefold class: there is wholesome feeling, unwholesome feeling, and neutral feeling… thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of feeling is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of feeling". ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of perception? As a single class, the aggregate of perception is joined with contact. As a twofold class: there is perception with a root cause, and perception without one. As a threefold class: there is wholesome perception, unwholesome perception, and neutral perception… thus the aggregate of perception is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of perception is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of perception". ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of mental formations? As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is joined with mind. As a twofold class: there are formations that are root causes, and formations that are not. As a threefold class: there are wholesome formations, unwholesome formations, and neutral formations… thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of mental formations". ⤵ Therein, what is the material form that is invisible, offers no resistance, and is included in the sense-field of mental objects? The faculty of femininity, the faculty of masculinity… physical food. This is called the material form that is "invisible, offers no resistance, and is included in the sense-field of mental objects". ⤵ Therein, what is the unconditioned element? The ending of desire, the ending of hatred, and the ending of delusion – this is called "the unconditioned element".

**en** `186619–186964`
There are twelve sense-fields – the eye sense-field, the sense-field of sights, the ear sense-field, the sense-field of sounds, the nose sense-field, the sense-field of smells, the tongue sense-field, the sense-field of tastes, the body sense-field, the sense-field of things touched, the mind sense-field, and the sense-field of mental objects.

**en** `186965–187116`
Of the twelve sense-fields, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral… how many involve conflict, how many are free from conflict?

Dasāyatanā abyākatā. Dvāyatanā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – "sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi, "dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi, "adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi. Manāyatanaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – "sukhāya vedanāya sampayutta"ntipi, "dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutta"ntipi, "adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutta"ntipi. Dasāyatanā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Dvāyatanā siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. ⤵ Pañcāyatanā upādinnupādāniyā. Saddāyatanaṃ anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Cattāro āyatanā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādāniyā. Dvāyatanā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Dasāyatanā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā. Dvāyatanā siyā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Dasāyatanā avitakkaavicārā. Manāyatanaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkavicāramattaṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkavicāramattaṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ , siyā na vattabbaṃ – "savitakkasavicāra"ntipi, "avitakkavicāramatta"ntipi, "avitakkaavicāra"ntipi. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – "pītisahagatā"tipi, "sukhasahagatā"tipi, "upekkhāsahagatā"tipi. Dvāyatanā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na vattabbā – "pītisahagatā"tipi, "sukhasahagatā"tipi, "upekkhāsahagatā"tipi. ⤵ Dasāyatanā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Dvāyatanā siyā dassanena pahātabbā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Dasāyatanā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Dvāyatanā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Dasāyatanā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Dvāyatanā siyā ācayagāmino, siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Dasāyatanā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Dvāyatanā siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā , siyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Dasāyatanā parittā. Dvāyatanā siyā parittā, siyā mahaggatā, siyā appamāṇā. Dasāyatanā anārammaṇā. Dvāyatanā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – "parittārammaṇā"tipi, "mahaggatārammaṇā"tipi, "appamāṇārammaṇā"tipi. Dasāyatanā majjhimā. Dvāyatanā siyā hīnā, siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Dasāyatanā aniyatā. Dvāyatanā siyā micchattaniyatā, siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. ⤵ Dasāyatanā anārammaṇā. Dvāyatanā siyā maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā – "maggārammaṇā"tipi, "maggahetukā"tipi, "maggādhipatino"tipi. Pañcāyatanā siyā uppannā, siyā uppādino, na vattabbā – "anuppannā"ti. Saddāyatanaṃ siyā uppannaṃ, siyā anuppannaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – "uppādī"ti. Pañcāyatanā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā uppannaṃ, siyā anuppannaṃ, siyā uppādi, siyā na vattabbaṃ – "uppanna"ntipi, "anuppanna"ntipi, "uppādī"tipi. Ekādasāyatanā siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā atītaṃ, siyā anāgataṃ, siyā paccuppannaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – "atīta"ntipi, "anāgata"ntipi, "paccuppanna"ntipi. Dasāyatanā anārammaṇā. Dvāyatanā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā , siyā paccuppannārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – "atītārammaṇā"tipi, "anāgatārammaṇā"tipi, "paccuppannārammaṇā"tipi; siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Dasāyatanā anārammaṇā. Dvāyatanā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – "ajjhattārammaṇā"tipi, "bahiddhārammaṇā"tipi, "ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā"tipi. Rūpāyatanaṃ sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ. Navāyatanā anidassanasappaṭighā. Dvāyatanā anidassanaappaṭighā.

**en** `187140–191491`
Ten sense-fields are neutral. Two sense-fields may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The mind sense-field may be joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The sense-field of mental objects may be joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant, or may not be describable as joined with any of these. Ten sense-fields are neither results nor things that produce results. Two sense-fields may be results, may produce results, or may be neither. ⤵ Five sense-fields are taken up at birth and able to be clung to. The sense-field of sounds is not taken up but able to be clung to. Four sense-fields may be taken up and able to be clung to, or not taken up but able to be clung to. Two sense-fields may be taken up and able to be clung to, not taken up but able to be clung to, or neither taken up nor able to be clung to. Ten sense-fields are undefiled yet open to defilement. Two sense-fields may be defiled and open to defilement, undefiled yet open to defilement, or neither defiled nor open to defilement. Ten sense-fields are without thought and examination. The mind sense-field may have both thought and examination, examination only, or neither. The sense-field of mental objects may have both thought and examination, examination only, or neither, or may not be describable as any of these. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity. Two sense-fields may be accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity, or may not be describable as accompanied by any of these. ⤵ Ten sense-fields are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Two sense-fields may be abandoned by seeing, by development, or by neither. Ten sense-fields have root causes to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Two sense-fields may have root causes to be abandoned by seeing, root causes to be abandoned by development, or root causes to be abandoned by neither. Ten sense-fields neither lead to further accumulation nor to dismantling. Two sense-fields may lead to accumulation, to dismantling, or to neither. Ten sense-fields belong neither to trainees nor to those beyond training. Two sense-fields may belong to trainees, to those beyond training, or to neither. Ten sense-fields are limited. Two sense-fields may be limited, expanded, or measureless. Ten sense-fields have no object. Two sense-fields may have a limited object, an expanded object, or a measureless object, or may not be describable as having any of these. Ten sense-fields are middling. Two sense-fields may be inferior, middling, or superior. Ten sense-fields are not fixed in their outcome. Two sense-fields may be fixed in wrongness, fixed in rightness, or not fixed. ⤵ Ten sense-fields have no object. Two sense-fields may have the path as their object, the path as their cause, or the path as their dominant factor, or may not be describable as any of these. Five sense-fields may be arisen or bound to arise; they cannot be described as "not arisen". The sense-field of sounds may be arisen or not arisen; it cannot be described as "bound to arise". Five sense-fields may be arisen, not arisen, or bound to arise. The sense-field of mental objects may be arisen, not arisen, or bound to arise, or may not be describable as any of these. Eleven sense-fields may be past, future, or present. The sense-field of mental objects may be past, future, or present, or may not be describable as past, future, or present. Ten sense-fields have no object. Two sense-fields may have a past object, a future object, or a present object, or may not be describable as having any of these; they may be internal, external, or both internal and external. Ten sense-fields have no object. Two sense-fields may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external, or may not be describable as having any of these. The sense-field of sights is visible and offers resistance. Nine sense-fields are invisible and offer resistance. Two sense-fields are invisible and offer no resistance.

Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "defilements that are defiled" or as "defiled without being defilements". The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a defilement that is defiled"; it may be defiled without being a defilement, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a defilement that is defiled, may be defiled without being a defilement, or may not be describable as either. ⤵ Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "defilements joined with the defilements" or as "joined with the defilements without being defilements". The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a defilement joined with the defilements"; it may be joined with the defilements without being a defilement, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a defilement joined with the defilements, may be joined with the defilements without being a defilement, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from the defilements yet open to defilement. Two sense-fields may be dissociated from the defilements yet open to defilement, dissociated from them and not open to defilement, or not describable as either. ⤵ Ten sense-fields are not to be abandoned by seeing. Two sense-fields may be abandoned by seeing or not. Ten sense-fields are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Two sense-fields may be abandoned by development or not. Ten sense-fields do not have root causes to be abandoned by seeing. Two sense-fields may have root causes to be abandoned by seeing or not. Ten sense-fields do not have root causes to be abandoned by development. Two sense-fields may have root causes to be abandoned by development or not. Ten sense-fields are without thought. Two sense-fields may have thought or not. Ten sense-fields are without examination. Two sense-fields may have examination or not. Ten sense-fields are without joy. Two sense-fields may have joy or not. Ten sense-fields are not accompanied by joy. Two sense-fields may be accompanied by joy or not. Ten sense-fields are not accompanied by happiness. Two sense-fields may be accompanied by happiness or not. Ten sense-fields are not accompanied by equanimity. Two sense-fields may be accompanied by equanimity or not. ⤵ Ten sense-fields belong to the sense sphere. Two sense-fields may belong to the sense sphere or not. Ten sense-fields do not belong to the fine-material sphere. Two sense-fields may belong to the fine-material sphere or not. Ten sense-fields do not belong to the immaterial sphere. Two sense-fields may belong to the immaterial sphere or not. Ten sense-fields are included in the round of existence. Two sense-fields may be included in the round of existence or outside it. Ten sense-fields do not lead out of the round. Two sense-fields may lead out of the round or not. Ten sense-fields are not fixed in their outcome. Two sense-fields may be fixed or not fixed. Ten sense-fields can be surpassed. Two sense-fields may be surpassable or unsurpassable. Ten sense-fields are free from conflict. Two sense-fields may involve conflict or be free from conflict.

### 265

**pi** `139395–139518`
Cha dhātuyo – pathavīdhātu [paṭhavīdhātu (sī. syā.) evamuparipi], āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu, ākāsadhātu, viññāṇadhātu.

**en** `208342–208489`
There are six elements – the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the air element, the space element, and the consciousness element.

### 266

**pi** `139519–140713`
Tattha katamā pathavīdhātu? Pathavīdhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru [nahāru (sī.)] aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ [aṭṭhimiñjā (sī.)] vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu’. ⤵ Tattha katamā bāhirā pathavīdhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – ayo lohaṃ tipu sīsaṃ sajjhaṃ [sajjhu (syā.)] muttā maṇi veḷuriyo saṅkho silā pavāḷaṃ rajataṃ jātarūpaṃ lohitaṅko [lohitaṅgo (syā. ka.), lohitako (?)] masāragallaṃ tiṇaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ sakkharā kaṭhalaṃ [kathalaṃ (ka.)] bhūmi pāsāṇo pabbato, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā pathavīdhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu yā ca bāhirā pathavīdhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati "pathavīdhātu".

**en** `208490–209727`
Therein, what is the earth element? The earth element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal earth element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, internal and taken up at birth – namely: head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, membranes, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach contents, and excrement; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal earth element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external earth element? Whatever externally is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, external and not taken up – namely: iron, copper, tin, lead, silver ore, pearl, gems, cat's-eye, conch shell, stone, coral, silver, gold, ruby, emerald, grass, wood, gravel, potsherds, earth, rock, and mountains; or whatever else externally is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external earth element'. The internal earth element and the external earth element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the earth element".

### 267

**pi** `140714–141735`
Tattha katamā āpodhātu? Āpodhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā āpodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ [sneho snehagataṃ (syā.)] bandhanattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā muttaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ bandhanattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā āpodhātu’. ⤵ Tattha katamā bāhirā āpodhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ bandhanattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – mūlaraso khandharaso tacaraso pattaraso puppharaso phalaraso khīraṃ dadhi sappi navanītaṃ telaṃ madhu phāṇitaṃ bhummāni vā udakāni antalikkhāni vā, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ bandhanattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā āpodhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā āpodhātu yā ca bāhirā āpodhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati "āpodhātu".

**en** `209728–210989`
Therein, what is the water element? The water element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal water element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, internal and taken up at birth – namely: bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, mucus, joint fluid, and urine; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal water element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external water element? Whatever externally is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, external and not taken up – namely: the juice of roots, the juice of stems, the juice of bark, the juice of leaves, the juice of flowers, the juice of fruits, milk, curds, ghee, butter, oil, honey, molasses, and the waters of the earth or of the sky; or whatever else externally is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external water element'. The internal water element and the external water element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the water element".

### 268

**pi** `141736–142815`
Tattha katamā tejodhātu? Tejodhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā tejodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – yena ca santappati yena ca jīrīyati yena ca pariḍayhati yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ sammā pariṇāmaṃ gacchati, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā tejodhātu’. ⤵ Tattha katamā bāhirā tejodhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kaṭṭhaggi palālaggi [sakalikaggi (sabbattha)] tiṇaggi gomayaggi thusaggi saṅkāraggi indaggi aggisantāpo sūriyasantāpo kaṭṭhasannicayasantāpo tiṇasannicayasantāpo dhaññasannicayasantāpo bhaṇḍasannicayasantāpo, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā tejodhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā tejodhātu yā ca bāhirā tejodhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati "tejodhātu".

**en** `210990–212287`
Therein, what is the fire element? The fire element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal fire element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, internal and taken up at birth – namely: that by which one is warmed, that by which one ages, that by which one is burned, and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is fully digested; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal fire element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external fire element? Whatever externally is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, external and not taken up – namely: fire of wood, fire of straw, fire of grass, fire of cow dung, fire of husks, fire of rubbish, lightning fire, the heat of fire, the heat of the sun, the heat of a heap of wood, the heat of a heap of grass, the heat of a heap of grain, the heat of a heap of goods; or whatever else externally is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external fire element'. The internal fire element and the external fire element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the fire element".

### 269

**pi** `142816–143899`
Tattha katamā vāyodhātu? Vāyodhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā vāyodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – uddhaṅgamā vātā adhogamā vātā kucchisayā vātā koṭṭhāsayā [koṭṭhasayā (sī. syā.)] vātā aṅgamaṅgānusārino vātā satthakavātā khurakavātā uppalakavātā assāso passāso iti vā, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā vāyodhātu’. ⤵ Tattha katamā bāhirā vāyodhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – puratthimā vātā pacchimā vātā uttarā vātā dakkhiṇā vātā sarajā vātā arajā vātā sītā vātā uṇhā vātā parittā vātā adhimattā vātā kāḷavātā verambhavātā pakkhavātā supaṇṇavātā tālavaṇṭavātā vidhūpanavātā, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā vāyodhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā vāyodhātu yā ca bāhirā vāyodhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati "vāyodhātu".

**en** `212288–213601`
Therein, what is the air element? The air element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal air element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is air, airy, the distension of material form, internal and taken up at birth – namely: winds going upward, winds going downward, winds in the belly, winds in the bowels, winds coursing through the limbs, cutting winds, piercing winds, throbbing winds, breathing in and breathing out; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is air, airy, the distension of material form, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal air element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external air element? Whatever externally is air, airy, the distension of material form, external and not taken up – namely: east winds, west winds, north winds, south winds, dusty winds, dust-free winds, cold winds, hot winds, gentle winds, strong winds, black winds, high-altitude winds, winds from birds' wings, winds from a supaṇṇa bird, winds from palm-leaf fans, winds from a winnowing fan; or whatever else externally is air, airy, the distension of material form, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external air element'. The internal air element and the external air element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the air element".

### 270

**pi** `143900–144834`
Tattha katamā ākāsadhātu? Ākāsadhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāso ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaro vivaragataṃ asamphuṭṭhaṃ maṃsalohitehi ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kaṇṇacchiddaṃ nāsacchiddaṃ mukhadvāraṃ, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ ajjhoharati, yattha ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ santiṭṭhati, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ adhobhāgaṃ nikkhamati, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāso ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaro vivaragataṃ asamphuṭṭhaṃ maṃsalohitehi ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu’. ⤵ Tattha katamā bāhirā ākāsadhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ ākāso ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaro vivaragataṃ asamphuṭṭhaṃ catūhi mahābhūtehi bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā ākāsadhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu yā ca bāhirā ākāsadhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati "ākāsadhātu".

**en** `213602–214764`
Therein, what is the space element? The space element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal space element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is space, spatial, a void, a hollow, an opening, a gap, not touched by flesh and blood, internal and taken up at birth – namely: the opening of the ear, the opening of the nose, the door of the mouth, that by which one swallows what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted, that in which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted stays, and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted passes out below; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is space, spatial, a void, a hollow, an opening, a gap, not touched by flesh and blood, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal space element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external space element? Whatever externally is space, spatial, a void, a hollow, an opening, a gap, not touched by the four great elements, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external space element'. The internal space element and the external space element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the space element".

### 271

**pi** `144835–145004`
Tattha katamā viññāṇadhātu? Cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhāviññāṇadhātu, kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati "viññāṇadhātu".

**en** `214765–215049`
Therein, what is the consciousness element? The eye-consciousness element, the ear-consciousness element, the nose-consciousness element, the tongue-consciousness element, the body-consciousness element, and the mind-consciousness element – this is called "the consciousness element".

### 273

**pi** `145022–145127`

There are another six elements – the pleasure element, the pain element, the gladness element, the sadness element, the equanimity element, and the ignorance element.

### 274

**pi** `145128–146334`
Tattha katamā sukhadhātu? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ sātaṃ kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "sukhadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā dukkhadhātu? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "dukkhadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā somanassadhātu? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "somanassadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā domanassadhātu? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "domanassadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā upekkhādhātu? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "upekkhādhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā avijjādhātu? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ anabhisamayo ananubodho asambodho appaṭivedho asaṅgāhaṇā apariyogāhaṇā asamapekkhanā apaccavekkhaṇā apaccakkhakammaṃ dummejjhaṃ bālyaṃ asampajaññaṃ moho pamoho sammoho avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "avijjādhātu".

**en** `215245–216996`
Therein, what is the pleasure element? Bodily comfort, bodily pleasure; the comfortable, pleasant experience born of body-contact; the comfortable, pleasant feeling born of body-contact – this is called "the pleasure element". ⤵ Therein, what is the pain element? Bodily discomfort, bodily pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of body-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of body-contact – this is called "the pain element". ⤵ Therein, what is the gladness element? Mental comfort, mental pleasure; the comfortable, pleasant experience born of mind-contact; the comfortable, pleasant feeling born of mind-contact – this is called "the gladness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the sadness element? Mental discomfort, mental pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of mind-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of mind-contact – this is called "the sadness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the equanimity element? What is mentally neither comfortable nor uncomfortable; the experience born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant; the feeling born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant – this is called "the equanimity element". ⤵ Therein, what is the ignorance element? Not knowing, not seeing, not comprehending, not awakening, not fully awakening, not penetrating, not grasping, not fathoming, not weighing evenly, not reflecting, not seeing directly; poor discernment, foolishness, lack of clear understanding; delusion, bewilderment, complete confusion; ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the barrier of ignorance; delusion, the root of the unwholesome – this is called "the ignorance element".

### 275

**pi** `146335–146351`
Imā cha dhātuyo.

**en** `216997–217024`
These are the six elements.

### 276

**pi** `146352–146458`
Aparāpi cha dhātuyo – kāmadhātu, byāpādadhātu, vihiṃsādhātu, nekkhammadhātu, abyāpādadhātu, avihiṃsādhātu.

**en** `217025–217222`
There are another six elements – the element of sense desire, the element of ill will, the element of cruelty, the element of renunciation, the element of goodwill, and the element of harmlessness.

### 277

**pi** `146459–148196`
Tattha katamā kāmadhātu? Kāmapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko saṅkappo appanā byappanā cetaso abhiniropanā micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati kāmadhātu. Heṭṭhato avīcinirayaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā uparito paranimmitavasavattī deve anto karitvā yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā khandhadhātuāyatanā rūpā [rūpaṃ (syā.)] vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "kāmadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā byāpādadhātu? Byāpādapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati "byāpādadhātu". Dasasu vā āghātavatthūsu cittassa āghāto paṭighāto paṭighaṃ paṭivirodho kopo pakopo sampakopo doso padoso sampadoso cittassa byāpatti manopadoso kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso dussanā dussitattaṃ byāpatti byāpajjanā virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati "byāpādadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā vihiṃsādhātu? Vihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati "vihiṃsādhātu". Idhekacco pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā rajjuyā vā aññataraññatarena satte viheṭheti, yā evarūpā heṭhanā viheṭhanā hiṃsanā vihiṃsanā rosanā virosanā parūpaghāto – ayaṃ vuccati "vihiṃsādhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā nekkhammadhātu? Nekkhammapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati "nekkhammadhātu". Sabbepi kusalā dhammā "nekkhammadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā abyāpādadhātu? Abyāpādapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati "abyāpādadhātu". Yā sattesu metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati "abyāpādadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā avihiṃsādhātu? Avihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko saṅkappo appanā byappanā cetaso abhiniropanā sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati "avihiṃsādhātu" . Yā sattesu karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati "avihiṃsādhātu".

**en** `217223–219623`
Therein, what is the element of sense desire? Thinking connected with sense desire – thought, intention, fixing, focusing, directing the mind, wrong intention – this is called the element of sense desire. Taking the Avīci hell as the lower limit and the gods who wield power over others' creations as the upper limit, whatever within this range moves here and is included here – the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields, material form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness – this is called "the element of sense desire". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of ill will? Thinking connected with ill will – thought… wrong intention – this is called "the element of ill will". Or the mind's irritation over the ten grounds for resentment: hostility, resistance, opposition; anger, rage, fury; hatred, ill feeling, malice; the mind's vexation, mental resentment; anger, being angry, the state of being angry; hatred, hating, the state of hating; vexation, being vexed; opposition, hostility; ferocity, harshness, and the mind's displeasure – this is called "the element of ill will". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of cruelty? Thinking connected with cruelty – thought… wrong intention – this is called "the element of cruelty". Here someone harms living beings with a hand, a clod, a stick, a knife, a rope, or with one thing or another; such tormenting, harassing, hurting, injuring, provoking, and attacking of others – this is called "the element of cruelty". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of renunciation? Thinking connected with renunciation – thought… right intention – this is called "the element of renunciation". Indeed, all wholesome states are "the element of renunciation". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of goodwill? Thinking connected with goodwill – thought… right intention – this is called "the element of goodwill". Loving-kindness towards living beings, the act of loving, the state of loving, the liberation of mind through loving-kindness – this is called "the element of goodwill". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of harmlessness? Thinking connected with harmlessness – thought, intention, fixing, focusing, directing the mind, right intention – this is called "the element of harmlessness". Compassion towards living beings, the act of compassion, the state of compassion, the liberation of mind through compassion – this is called "the element of harmlessness".

### 278

**pi** `148197–148213`

**en** `219624–219651`
These are the six elements.

### 279

**pi** `148214–148305`
Iti imāni tīṇi chakkāni tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo honti.

**en** `219652–219736`
Thus these three sets of six, gathered and grouped together, make eighteen elements.

### 280

**en** `219737–219796`
