### 347

**pi** `220884–226367`
Dasindriyā abyākatā. Domanassindriyaṃ akusalaṃ. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ kusalaṃ. Cattārindriyā siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Cha indriyā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. ⤵ Dvādasindriyā na vattabbā – "sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi, "dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi, "adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi. Cha indriyā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Tīṇindriyā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – "sukhāya vedanāya sampayutta"ntipi , "dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutta"ntipi, "adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutta"ntipi. ⤵ Sattindriyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Tīṇindriyā vipākā. Dvindriyā vipākadhammadhammā. Aññindriyaṃ siyā vipākaṃ, siyā vipākadhammadhammaṃ. Navindriyā siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Navindriyā upādinnupādāniyā . Domanassindriyaṃ anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Tīṇindriyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Navindriyā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. ⤵ Navindriyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā. Domanassindriyaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikaṃ. Tīṇindriyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Tīṇindriyā siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Cha indriyā siyā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Navindriyā avitakkaavicārā. Domanassindriyaṃ savitakkasavicāraṃ. Upekkhindriyaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ. Ekādasindriyā siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. ⤵ Ekādasindriyā na vattabbā – "pītisahagatā"tipi, "sukhasahagatā"tipi, "upekkhāsahagatā"tipi. Somanassindriyaṃ siyā pītisahagataṃ na sukhasahagataṃ na upekkhāsahagataṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – "pītisahagata"nti. Cha indriyā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Cattārindriyā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā , siyā na vattabbā – "pītisahagatā"tipi, "sukhasahagatā"tipi, "upekkhāsahagatā"tipi. ⤵ Pannarasindriyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Domanassindriyaṃ siyā dassanena pahātabbaṃ, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ. Cha indriyā siyā dassanena pahātabbā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Pannarasindriyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Domanassindriyaṃ siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ. Cha indriyā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. ⤵ Dasindriyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Domanassindriyaṃ ācayagāmi. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ apacayagāmi. Aññindriyaṃ siyā apacayagāmi, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmi . Navindriyā siyā ācayagāmino, siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Dasindriyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Dvindriyā sekkhā. Aññātāvindriyaṃ asekkhaṃ. Navindriyā siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā, siyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. ⤵ Dasindriyā parittā. Tīṇindriyā appamāṇā. Navindriyā siyā parittā, siyā mahaggatā, siyā appamāṇā. Sattindriyā anārammaṇā. Dvindriyā parittārammaṇā. Tīṇindriyā appamāṇārammaṇā. Domanassindriyaṃ siyā parittārammaṇaṃ siyā mahaggatārammaṇaṃ, na appamāṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – "parittārammaṇa"ntipi , "mahaggatārammaṇa"nti pi. Navindriyā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – "parittārammaṇā"tipi, "mahaggatārammaṇā"tipi, "appamāṇārammaṇā"tipi. ⤵ Navindriyā majjhimā. Domanassindriyaṃ hīnaṃ. Tīṇindriyā paṇītā. Tīṇindriyā siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Cha indriyā siyā hīnā, siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Dasindriyā aniyatā. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ sammattaniyataṃ. Cattārindriyā siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Domanassindriyaṃ siyā micchattaniyataṃ, siyā aniyataṃ . Cha indriyā siyā micchattaniyatā, siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Sattindriyā anārammaṇā. Cattārindriyā na vattabbā – "maggārammaṇā"tipi, "maggahetukā"tipi, "maggādhipatino"tipi. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ na maggārammaṇaṃ, siyā maggahetukaṃ, siyā maggādhipati, siyā na vattabbaṃ – "maggahetuka"ntipi, "maggādhipatī"tipi. Aññindriyaṃ na maggārammaṇaṃ, siyā maggahetukaṃ, siyā maggādhipati, siyā na vattabbaṃ – "maggahetuka"ntipi, "maggādhipatī"tipi. Navindriyā siyā maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā – "maggārammaṇā"tipi, "maggahetukā"tipi, "maggādhipatino"tipi. ⤵ Dasindriyā siyā uppannā, siyā uppādino, na vattabbā – "anuppannā"ti. Dvindriyā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā – "uppādino"ti. Dasindriyā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino ; siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Sattindriyā anārammaṇā. Dvindriyā paccuppannārammaṇā. Tīṇindriyā na vattabbā – "atītārammaṇā"tipi, "anāgatārammaṇā"tipi , "paccuppannārammaṇā"tipi. Dasindriyā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – "atītārammaṇā"tipi, "anāgatārammaṇā"tipi, "paccuppannārammaṇā"tipi; siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Sattindriyā anārammaṇā. Tīṇindriyā bahiddhārammaṇā. Cattārindriyā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā, aṭṭhindriyā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – "ajjhattārammaṇā"tipi, "bahiddhārammaṇā"tipi, "ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā"tipi. Pañcindriyā anidassanasappaṭighā. Sattarasindriyā anidassanaappaṭighā.

**en** `315865–322442`
Ten faculties are neutral. The faculty of sadness is unwholesome. The faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known" is wholesome. Four faculties may be wholesome or neutral. Six faculties may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. ⤵ Twelve faculties cannot be described as joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. Six faculties may be joined with pleasant feeling or with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. Three faculties may be joined with pleasant feeling, with painful feeling, or with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The life faculty may be joined with pleasant feeling, with painful feeling, or with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant, or may not be describable as joined with any of these. ⤵ Seven faculties are neither results nor things that produce results. Three faculties are results. Two faculties are things that produce results. The faculty of final knowledge may be a result or something that produces results. Nine faculties may be results, may produce results, or may be neither. Nine faculties are taken up at birth and able to be clung to. The faculty of sadness is not taken up but able to be clung to. Three faculties are neither taken up nor able to be clung to. Nine faculties may be taken up and able to be clung to, not taken up but able to be clung to, or neither taken up nor able to be clung to. ⤵ Nine faculties are undefiled yet open to defilement. The faculty of sadness is defiled and open to defilement. Three faculties are neither defiled nor open to defilement. Three faculties may be undefiled yet open to defilement, or neither defiled nor open to defilement. Six faculties may be defiled and open to defilement, undefiled yet open to defilement, or neither defiled nor open to defilement. Nine faculties are without thought and examination. The faculty of sadness has both thought and examination. The faculty of equanimity may have both thought and examination, or neither. Eleven faculties may have both thought and examination, examination only, or neither. ⤵ Eleven faculties cannot be described as accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity. The faculty of gladness may be accompanied by joy but not by happiness or equanimity, or may not be describable as accompanied by joy. Six faculties may be accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity. Four faculties may be accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity, or may not be describable as accompanied by any of these. ⤵ Fifteen faculties are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. The faculty of sadness may be abandoned by seeing or by development. Six faculties may be abandoned by seeing, by development, or by neither. Fifteen faculties have root causes to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. The faculty of sadness may have root causes to be abandoned by seeing or by development. Six faculties may have root causes to be abandoned by seeing, by development, or by neither. ⤵ Ten faculties neither lead to further accumulation nor to dismantling. The faculty of sadness leads to accumulation. The faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known" leads to dismantling. The faculty of final knowledge may lead to dismantling, or lead to neither. Nine faculties may lead to accumulation, to dismantling, or to neither. Ten faculties belong neither to trainees nor to those beyond training. Two faculties belong to trainees. The faculty of one who has fully known belongs to those beyond training. Nine faculties may belong to trainees, to those beyond training, or to neither. ⤵ Ten faculties are limited. Three faculties are measureless. Nine faculties may be limited, expanded, or measureless. Seven faculties have no object. Two faculties have a limited object. Three faculties have a measureless object. The faculty of sadness may have a limited object or an expanded object but not a measureless object, or may not be describable as having a limited or an expanded object. Nine faculties may have a limited object, an expanded object, or a measureless object, or may not be describable as having any of these. ⤵ Nine faculties are middling. The faculty of sadness is inferior. Three faculties are superior. Three faculties may be middling or superior. Six faculties may be inferior, middling, or superior. Ten faculties are not fixed in their outcome. The faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known" is fixed in rightness. Four faculties may be fixed in rightness or not fixed. The faculty of sadness may be fixed in wrongness or not fixed. Six faculties may be fixed in wrongness, fixed in rightness, or not fixed. Seven faculties have no object. Four faculties cannot be described as having the path as their object, the path as their cause, or the path as their dominant factor. The faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known" does not have the path as its object; it may have the path as its cause, or the path as its dominant factor, or may not be describable as having the path as its cause or as its dominant factor. The faculty of final knowledge does not have the path as its object; it may have the path as its cause, or the path as its dominant factor, or may not be describable as having the path as its cause or as its dominant factor. Nine faculties may have the path as their object, the path as their cause, or the path as their dominant factor, or may not be describable as having any of these. ⤵ Ten faculties may be arisen or bound to arise; they cannot be described as "not arisen". Two faculties may be arisen or not arisen; they cannot be described as "bound to arise". Ten faculties may be arisen, not arisen, or bound to arise; they may be past, future, or present. Seven faculties have no object. Two faculties have a present object. Three faculties cannot be described as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. Ten faculties may have a past object, a future object, or a present object, or may not be describable as having any of these; they may be internal, external, or both internal and external. Seven faculties have no object. Three faculties have an external object. Four faculties may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external. Eight faculties may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external, or may not be describable as having any of these. Five faculties are invisible and offer resistance. Seventeen faculties are invisible and offer no resistance.

### 354

**pi** `240929–241291`
Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ, saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

**en** `341592–342200`
With ignorance as condition, formations; with formations as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality and material form; with mentality and material form as condition, the six sense-fields; with the six sense-fields as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come to be. Thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

### 355

**pi** `241292–242064`
Tattha katamā avijjā? Dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "avijjā". ⤵ Tattha katame avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā? Puññābhisaṅkhāro, apuññābhisaṅkhāro, āneñjābhisaṅkhāro, kāyasaṅkhāro, vacīsaṅkhāro, cittasaṅkhāro. ⤵ Tattha katamo puññābhisaṅkhāro? Kusalā cetanā kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarā dānamayā sīlamayā bhāvanāmayā – ayaṃ vuccati "puññābhisaṅkhāro". ⤵ Tattha katamo apuññābhisaṅkhāro? Akusalā cetanā kāmāvacarā – ayaṃ vuccati "apuññābhisaṅkhāro". ⤵ Tattha katamo āneñjābhisaṅkhāro? Kusalā cetanā arūpāvacarā – ayaṃ vuccati "āneñjābhisaṅkhāro". ⤵ Tattha katamo kāyasaṅkhāro? Kāyasañcetanā kāyasaṅkhāro, vacīsañcetanā vacīsaṅkhāro, manosañcetanā cittasaṅkhāro. Ime vuccanti "avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā".

**en** `342201–343404`
Therein, what is ignorance? Not knowing suffering, not knowing the origin of suffering, not knowing the cessation of suffering, not knowing the way leading to the cessation of suffering — this is called "ignorance". ⤵ Therein, what are the formations that have ignorance as condition? The meritorious formation, the demeritorious formation, the imperturbable formation, the bodily formation, the verbal formation, the mental formation. ⤵ Therein, what is the meritorious formation? Wholesome intention belonging to the sense sphere or the fine-material sphere, made of giving, made of virtue, made of meditative development — this is called "the meritorious formation". ⤵ Therein, what is the demeritorious formation? Unwholesome intention belonging to the sense sphere — this is called "the demeritorious formation". ⤵ Therein, what is the imperturbable formation? Wholesome intention belonging to the immaterial sphere — this is called "the imperturbable formation". ⤵ Therein, what is the bodily formation? Bodily intention is the bodily formation; verbal intention is the verbal formation; mental intention is the mental formation. These are called "the formations that have ignorance as condition".

### 356

**pi** `242065–242235`
Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ".

**en** `343405–343663`
Therein, what is the consciousness that has formations as condition? Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness — this is called "the consciousness that has formations as condition".

### 357

**pi** `242236–242573`
Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ? Atthi nāmaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ. Tattha katamaṃ nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati "nāmaṃ" . Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ? Cattāro mahābhūtā, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya rūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "rūpaṃ". Iti idañca nāmaṃ, idañca rūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati "viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ".

**en** `343664–344227`
Therein, what are the mentality and material form that have consciousness as condition? There is mentality, there is material form. Therein, what is mentality? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations — this is called "mentality". Therein, what is material form? The four great elements and the material form derived from the four great elements — this is called "material form". So this is mentality and this is material form. This is called "the mentality and material form that have consciousness as condition".

### 358

**pi** `242574–242744`
Tattha katamaṃ nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ? Cakkhāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ".

**en** `344228–344541`
Therein, what are the six sense-fields that have mentality and material form as condition? The eye sense-field, the ear sense-field, the nose sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the body sense-field, the mind sense-field — this is called "the six sense-fields that have mentality and material form as condition".

### 359

**pi** `242745–242915`
Tattha katamo saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso? Cakkhusamphasso sotasamphasso ghānasamphasso jivhāsamphasso kāyasamphasso manosamphasso – ayaṃ vuccati "saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso".

**en** `344542–344772`
Therein, what is the contact that has the six sense-fields as condition? Eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, mind-contact — this is called "the contact that has the six sense-fields as condition".

### 360

**pi** `242916–243137`
Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "phassapaccayā vedanā".

**en** `344773–345073`
Therein, what is the feeling that has contact as condition? Feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "the feeling that has contact as condition".

### 361

**pi** `243138–243286`
Tattha katamā vedanāpaccayā taṇhā? Rūpataṇhā, saddataṇhā, gandhataṇhā, rasataṇhā, phoṭṭhabbataṇhā, dhammataṇhā – ayaṃ vuccati "vedanāpaccayā taṇhā".

**en** `345074–345331`
Therein, what is the craving that has feeling as condition? Craving for sights, craving for sounds, craving for smells, craving for tastes, craving for tangible things, craving for mental objects — this is called "the craving that has feeling as condition".

### 362

**pi** `243287–243426`
Tattha katamaṃ taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ? Kāmupādānaṃ, diṭṭhupādānaṃ, sīlabbatupādānaṃ, attavādupādānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ".

**en** `345332–345569`
Therein, what is the clinging that has craving as condition? Clinging to sense pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, clinging to a doctrine of self — this is called "the clinging that has craving as condition".

### 363

**pi** `243427–243943`
Tattha katamo upādānapaccayā bhavo? Bhavo duvidhena – atthi kammabhavo, atthi upapattibhavo. Tattha katamo kammabhavo? Puññābhisaṅkhāro, apuññābhisaṅkhāro, āneñjābhisaṅkhāro – ayaṃ vuccati "kammabhavo". Sabbampi bhavagāmikammaṃ kammabhavo. ⤵ Tattha katamo upapattibhavo? Kāmabhavo, rūpabhavo, arūpabhavo, saññābhavo, asaññābhavo, nevasaññānāsaññābhavo, ekavokārabhavo, catuvokārabhavo, pañcavokārabhavo – ayaṃ vuccati "upapattibhavo". Iti ayañca kammabhavo, ayañca upapattibhavo. Ayaṃ vuccati "upādānapaccayā bhavo".

**en** `345570–346372`
Therein, what is the existence that has clinging as condition? Existence is twofold: there is action-existence and there is rebirth-existence. Therein, what is action-existence? The meritorious formation, the demeritorious formation, the imperturbable formation — this is called "action-existence". All action that leads to existence is action-existence. ⤵ Therein, what is rebirth-existence? Sense-sphere existence, fine-material existence, immaterial existence, percipient existence, non-percipient existence, neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient existence, one-constituent existence, four-constituent existence, five-constituent existence — this is called "rebirth-existence". So this is action-existence and this is rebirth-existence. This is called "the existence that has clinging as condition".

### 364

**pi** `243944–244139`
Tattha katamā bhavapaccayā jāti? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jāti sañjāti okkanti abhinibbatti, khandhānaṃ pātubhāvo , āyatanānaṃ paṭilābho – ayaṃ vuccati "bhavapaccayā jāti".

**en** `346373–346681`
Therein, what is the birth that has existence as condition? The birth of the various beings in the various classes of beings, their being born, their descent, their coming forth, the appearance of the aggregates, the obtaining of the sense-fields — this is called "the birth that has existence as condition".

### 365

**pi** `244140–244690`
Tattha katamaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ? Atthi jarā, atthi maraṇaṃ. Tattha katamā jarā? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jarā jīraṇatā khaṇḍiccaṃ pāliccaṃ valittacatā āyuno saṃhāni indriyānaṃ paripāko – ayaṃ vuccati "jarā". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ maraṇaṃ? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṃ maccu maraṇaṃ kālakiriyā [kālaṃkiriyā (ka.)] khandhānaṃ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo jīvitindriyassupacchedo – idaṃ vuccati "maraṇaṃ". Iti ayañca jarā, idañca maraṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati "jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ".

**en** `346682–347428`
Therein, what are the aging and death that have birth as condition? There is aging, there is death. Therein, what is aging? The aging of the various beings in the various classes of beings, their growing old, broken teeth, grey hair, wrinkled skin, the decline of the life span, the ripening of the faculties — this is called "aging". ⤵ Therein, what is death? The passing away of the various beings from the various classes of beings, their passing on, breakup, disappearance, dying, death, the completion of their time, the breakup of the aggregates, the laying down of the body, the cutting off of the life faculty — this is called "death". So this is aging and this is death. This is called "the aging and death that have birth as condition".

### 366

**pi** `244691–245056`
Tattha katamo soko? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa, aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa soko socanā socitattaṃ antosoko antoparisoko cetaso parijjhāyanā domanassaṃ sokasallaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "soko".

**en** `347429–347850`
Therein, what is sorrow? For one touched by loss of relatives, touched by loss of wealth, touched by loss through illness, touched by loss of virtue, or touched by loss of view; for one who meets with some misfortune or other, touched by some painful thing or other — the sorrow, sorrowing, state of sorrowing, inner sorrow, inner deep sorrow, the burning of the mind, grief, the dart of sorrow — this is called "sorrow".

### 367

**pi** `245057–245458`
Tattha katamo paridevo? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa , rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa, aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa ādevo paridevo ādevanā paridevanā ādevitattaṃ paridevitattaṃ vācā palāpo vippalāpo lālappo lālappanā lālappitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati paridevo".

**en** `347851–348320`
Therein, what is lamentation? For one touched by loss of relatives, touched by loss of wealth, touched by loss through illness, touched by loss of virtue, or touched by loss of view; for one who meets with some misfortune or other, touched by some painful thing or other — the crying, lamenting, act of crying, act of lamenting, state of crying, state of lamenting, wordy talk, babbling, wailing, the act of wailing, the state of wailing — this is called "lamentation".

### 368

**pi** `245459–245621`
Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "dukkhaṃ".

**en** `348321–348514`
Therein, what is pain? Bodily discomfort, bodily pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of body-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of body-contact — this is called "pain".

### 369

**pi** `245622–245797`
Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ, cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ, cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ, cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "domanassaṃ".

**en** `348515–348710`
Therein, what is grief? Mental discomfort, mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "grief".

### 370

**pi** `245798–246122`
Tattha katamo upāyāso? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa, aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa āyāso upāyāso āyāsitattaṃ upāyāsitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "upāyāso".

**en** `348711–349066`
Therein, what is despair? For one touched by loss of relatives, touched by loss of wealth, touched by loss through illness, touched by loss of virtue, or touched by loss of view; for one who meets with some misfortune or other, touched by some painful thing or other — the distress, despair, state of distress, state of despair — this is called "despair".

### 371

**pi** `246123–246350`
Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotīti, evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa saṅgati hoti, samāgamo hoti, samodhānaṃ hoti, pātubhāvo hoti. Tena vuccati "evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī"ti.

**en** `349067–349324`
"Thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering": thus there is the coming together of this entire mass of suffering, its meeting, its combination, its appearance. Therefore it is said, "thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering".

Which things are unwholesome? On the occasion when an unwholesome mind has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with a view, with a sight as its object, or a sound as its object, or a smell as its object, or a taste as its object, or a tangible thing as its object, or a mental object as its object, or based on whatever it may be — on that occasion, with ignorance as condition, a formation; with the formation as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense-field; with the sixth sense-field as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

### 391

**pi** `254560–257002`
Tattha katamā avijjā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "avijjā". ⤵ Tattha katamo avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ [cetayitattaṃ (sī. ka.)] – ayaṃ vuccati "avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati "saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati "viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati "nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamo chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso? Yo phasso phusanā samphusanā samphusitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso". ⤵ Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "phassapaccayā vedanā". ⤵ Tattha katamā vedanāpaccayā taṇhā? Yo rāgo sārāgo anunayo anurodho nandī nandirāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati "vedanāpaccayā taṇhā". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ? Yā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho patiṭṭhāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho [vipariyesaggāho (bahūsu)] – idaṃ vuccati "taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamo upādānapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā upādānaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati "upādānapaccayā bhavo". ⤵ Tattha katamā bhavapaccayā jāti? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ jāti sañjāti nibbatti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo – ayaṃ vuccati "bhavapaccayā jāti". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ? Atthi jarā, atthi maraṇaṃ. Tattha katamā jarā? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ jarā jīraṇatā āyuno saṃhāni – ayaṃ vuccati "jarā". Tattha katamaṃ maraṇaṃ? Yo tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ khayo vayo bhedo paribhedo aniccatā antaradhānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "maraṇaṃ". Iti ayañca jarā, idañca maraṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati "jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ". ⤵ Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotīti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa saṅgati hoti, samāgamo hoti, samodhānaṃ hoti, pātubhāvo hoti. Tena vuccati "evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī"ti.

**en** `363407–366987`
Therein, what is ignorance? The lack of knowledge, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "ignorance". ⤵ Therein, what is the formation that has ignorance as condition? The intention, intending, state of intending — this is called "the formation that has ignorance as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the consciousness that has the formation as condition? The mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the consciousness that has the formation as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the mentality that has consciousness as condition? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations — this is called "the mentality that has consciousness as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the sixth sense-field that has mentality as condition? The mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the sixth sense-field that has mentality as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition? The contact, touching, being in contact, state of being in contact — this is called "the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the feeling that has contact as condition? Mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "the feeling that has contact as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the craving that has feeling as condition? The lust, passion, compliance, attraction, delight, delight-and-lust, passion of the mind — this is called "the craving that has feeling as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the clinging that has craving as condition? The view, resort to views, thicket of views, wilderness of views, distortion of views, wavering of views, fetter of views, the grip, the hold, the insistence, the wrong grasping, the bad road, the wrong path, wrongness, the sectarian domain, the distorted grip — this is called "the clinging that has craving as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the existence that has clinging as condition? Setting aside clinging: the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness — this is called "the existence that has clinging as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the birth that has existence as condition? The birth of the various states, their being born, arising, coming forth, appearance — this is called "the birth that has existence as condition". ⤵ Therein, what are the aging and death that have birth as condition? There is aging, there is death. Therein, what is aging? The aging of the various states, their growing old, the decline of their life span — this is called "aging". Therein, what is death? The destruction of the various states, their vanishing, breakup, disintegration, impermanence, disappearance — this is called "death". So this is aging and this is death. This is called "the aging and death that have birth as condition". ⤵ "Thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering": thus there is the coming together of this entire mass of suffering, its meeting, its combination, its appearance. Therefore it is said, "thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering".

This is called "the mentality and material form that have consciousness as condition". ⤵ "With mentality and material form as condition, the sixth sense-field": there is mentality, there is material form. Therein, what is mentality? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations — this is called "mentality". Therein, what is material form? The material form depending on which the mind-consciousness element occurs — this is called "material form". So this is mentality and this is material form. This is called "mentality and material form". ⤵ Therein, what is the sixth sense-field that has mentality and material form as condition? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the sixth sense-field that has mentality and material form as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition? The contact, touching, being in contact, state of being in contact — this is called "the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition"… therefore it is said, "thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering".

Tattha katamā avijjā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "avijjā". ⤵ Tattha katamo avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro avijjāhetuko? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro avijjāhetuko". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārahetukaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati "saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārahetukaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ viññāṇahetukaṃ? Atthi nāmaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ. Tattha katamaṃ nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati "nāmaṃ". Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ? Cakkhāyatanassa upacayo, sotāyatanassa upacayo, ghānāyatanassa upacayo, jivhāyatanassa upacayo, kāyāyatanassa upacayo, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi rūpaṃ cittajaṃ cittahetukaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "rūpaṃ". Iti idañca nāmaṃ, idañca rūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati "viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ viññāṇahetukaṃ". ⤵ Nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ nāmarūpahetukanti. Atthi nāmaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ. Tattha katamaṃ nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho , saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati "nāmaṃ". Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ? Cattāro ca mahābhūtā, yañca rūpaṃ nissāya manoviññāṇadhātu vattati – idaṃ vuccati "rūpaṃ". Iti idañca nāmaṃ, idañca rūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati "nāmarūpaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ nāmarūpahetukaṃ? Cakkhāyatanaṃ , sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ , jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ nāmarūpahetukaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamo chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso chaṭṭhāyatanahetuko? Yo phasso phusanā samphusanā samphusitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso chaṭṭhāyatanahetuko". ⤵ Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā phassahetukā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "phassapaccayā vedanā phassahetukā". ⤵ Tattha katamā vedanāpaccayā taṇhā vedanāhetukā? Yo rāgo sārāgo…pe… cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati "vedanāpaccayā taṇhā vedanāhetukā". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ taṇhāhetukaṃ? Yā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati "taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ taṇhāhetukaṃ"…pe… tena vuccati "evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī"ti.

**en** `384803–388476`
Therein, what is ignorance? The lack of knowledge, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "ignorance". ⤵ Therein, what is the formation that has ignorance as condition, with ignorance as its cause? The intention, intending, state of intending — this is called "the formation that has ignorance as condition, with ignorance as its cause". ⤵ Therein, what is the consciousness that has the formation as condition, with the formation as its cause? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the consciousness that has the formation as condition, with the formation as its cause". ⤵ Therein, what are the mentality and material form that have consciousness as condition, with consciousness as their cause? There is mentality, there is material form. Therein, what is mentality? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations — this is called "mentality". Therein, what is material form? The growth of the eye sense-field, the growth of the ear sense-field, the growth of the nose sense-field, the growth of the tongue sense-field, the growth of the body sense-field, or whatever other material form there is that is born of mind, caused by mind, originated by mind — this is called "material form". So this is mentality and this is material form. This is called "the mentality and material form that have consciousness as condition, with consciousness as their cause". ⤵ "With mentality and material form as condition, the six sense-fields with mentality and material form as their cause": there is mentality, there is material form. Therein, what is mentality? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations — this is called "mentality". Therein, what is material form? The four great elements and the material form depending on which the mind-consciousness element occurs — this is called "material form". So this is mentality and this is material form. This is called "mentality and material form". ⤵ Therein, what are the six sense-fields that have mentality and material form as condition, with mentality and material form as their cause? The eye sense-field, the ear sense-field, the nose sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the body sense-field, the mind sense-field — this is called "the six sense-fields that have mentality and material form as condition, with mentality and material form as their cause". ⤵ Therein, what is the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition, with the sixth sense-field as its cause? The contact, touching, being in contact, state of being in contact — this is called "the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition, with the sixth sense-field as its cause". ⤵ Therein, what is the feeling that has contact as condition, with contact as its cause? Mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "the feeling that has contact as condition, with contact as its cause". ⤵ Therein, what is the craving that has feeling as condition, with feeling as its cause? The lust, passion… passion of the mind — this is called "the craving that has feeling as condition, with feeling as its cause". ⤵ Therein, what is the clinging that has craving as condition, with craving as its cause? The view, resort to views… the sectarian domain, the distorted grip — this is called "the clinging that has craving as condition, with craving as its cause"… therefore it is said, "thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering".

Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

**en** `388537–389297`
On that occasion, with ignorance as condition, a formation associated with ignorance; with the formation as condition, consciousness associated with the formation; with consciousness as condition, mentality associated with consciousness; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense-field associated with mentality; with the sixth sense-field as condition, contact associated with the sixth sense-field; with contact as condition, feeling associated with contact; with feeling as condition, craving associated with feeling; with craving as condition, clinging associated with craving; with clinging as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

**en** `398369–401298`
Therein, what is ignorance? The lack of knowledge, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "ignorance". ⤵ Therein, what is the formation that has ignorance as condition, associated with ignorance? The intention, intending, state of intending — this is called "the formation that has ignorance as condition, associated with ignorance". ⤵ Therein, what is the consciousness that has the formation as condition, associated with the formation? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the consciousness that has the formation as condition, associated with the formation". ⤵ Therein, what are the mentality and material form that have consciousness as condition, the mentality being associated with consciousness? There is mentality, there is material form. Therein, what is mentality? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations — this is called "mentality". Therein, what is material form? The growth of the eye sense-field, the growth of the ear sense-field, the growth of the nose sense-field, the growth of the tongue sense-field, the growth of the body sense-field, or whatever other material form there is that is born of mind, caused by mind, originated by mind — this is called "material form". So this is mentality and this is material form. This is called "the mentality and material form that have consciousness as condition, the mentality being associated with consciousness". ⤵ "With mentality and material form as condition, the six sense-fields, the sixth sense-field being associated with mentality": there is mentality, there is material form. Therein, what is mentality? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations — this is called "mentality". Therein, what is material form? The four great elements and the material form depending on which the mind-consciousness element occurs — this is called "material form". So this is mentality and this is material form. This is called "mentality and material form". ⤵ Therein, what are the six sense-fields that have mentality and material form as condition, the sixth sense-field being associated with mentality? The eye sense-field, the ear sense-field, the nose sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the body sense-field, the mind sense-field — this is called "the six sense-fields that have mentality and material form as condition, the sixth sense-field being associated with mentality". ⤵ Therein, what is the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition, associated with the sixth sense-field? The contact, touching, being in contact, state of being in contact — this is called "the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition, associated with the sixth sense-field"… therefore it is said, "thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering".

On that occasion, with ignorance as condition, a formation, and with the formation as condition, ignorance too; with the formation as condition, consciousness, and with consciousness as condition, the formation too; with consciousness as condition, mentality, and with mentality as condition, consciousness too; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense-field, and with the sixth sense-field as condition, mentality too; with the sixth sense-field as condition, contact, and with contact as condition, the sixth sense-field too; with contact as condition, feeling, and with feeling as condition, contact too; with feeling as condition, craving, and with craving as condition, feeling too; with craving as condition, clinging, and with clinging as condition, craving too; with clinging as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. ### 429

**pi** `290527–291230`
Katame dhammā akusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ diṭṭhigatasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagataṃ diṭṭhigatavippayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… somanassasahagataṃ diṭṭhigatavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇaṃ vā saddārammaṇaṃ vā gandhārammaṇaṃ vā rasārammaṇaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

**en** `421941–422964`
Which things are unwholesome? On the occasion when an unwholesome mind has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with a view, with prompting… accompanied by joy, dissociated from a view, with a sight as its object… accompanied by joy, dissociated from a view, with prompting, with a sight as its object, or a sound as its object, or a smell as its object, or a taste as its object, or a tangible thing as its object, or a mental object as its object, or based on whatever it may be — on that occasion, with ignorance as condition, a formation; with the formation as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense-field; with the sixth sense-field as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, decision; with decision as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

### 430

**pi** `291231–291826`
Tattha katamā avijjā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "avijjā". ⤵ Tattha katamo avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati "taṇhāpaccayā adhimokkho". ⤵ Tattha katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati "adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo"…pe… tena vuccati "evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī"ti.

**en** `422965–423847`
Therein, what is ignorance? The intention, intending, state of intending — this is called the formation that has ignorance as condition…. ⤵ Therein, what is the decision that has craving as condition? The decision of the mind, deciding, the state of being decided upon — this is called "the decision that has craving as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the existence that has decision as condition? Setting aside decision: the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness — this is called "the existence that has decision as condition"… therefore it is said, "thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering".

### 443

**pi** `298023–298604`
Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā saddārammaṇaṃ vā gandhārammaṇaṃ vā rasārammaṇaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

**en** `433052–433956`
Which things are wholesome? On the occasion when a wholesome mind of the sense sphere has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, with a sight as its object, or a sound as its object, or a smell as its object, or a taste as its object, or a tangible thing as its object, or a mental object as its object, or based on whatever it may be — on that occasion, with a wholesome root as condition, a formation; with the formation as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense-field; with the sixth sense-field as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, confidence; with confidence as condition, decision; with decision as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

### 444

**pi** `298605–299856`
Tattha katame kusalamūlā? Alobho, adoso, amoho. ⤵ Tattha katamo alobho? Yo alobho alubbhanā alubbhitattaṃ asārāgo asārajjanā asārajjitattaṃ anabhijjhā alobho kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "alobho". ⤵ Tattha katamo adoso? Yo adoso adussanā adussitattaṃ abyāpādo abyāpajjo adoso kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "adoso". ⤵ Tattha katamo amoho? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati "amoho". Ime vuccanti "kusalamūlā". ⤵ Tattha katamo kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ…pe… nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ…pe… chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso…pe… phassapaccayā vedanā…pe… ayaṃ vuccati "phassapaccayā vedanā". ⤵ Tattha katamo vedanāpaccayā pasādo? Yā saddhā saddahanā okappanā abhippasādo – ayaṃ vuccati "vedanāpaccayā pasādo". ⤵ Tattha katamo pasādapaccayā adhimokkho? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati "pasādapaccayā adhimokkho". ⤵ Tattha katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati "adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo"…pe… tena vuccati "evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī"ti.

**en** `433957–435925`
Therein, what are the wholesome roots? Non-greed, non-hate, non-delusion. ⤵ Therein, what is non-greed? The non-greed, absence of greed, state of being without greed, non-passion, absence of passion, state of being without passion, non-covetousness, the non-greed that is a wholesome root — this is called "non-greed". ⤵ Therein, what is non-hate? The non-hate, absence of hating, state of being without hate, non-ill-will, freedom from ill-will, the non-hate that is a wholesome root — this is called "non-hate". ⤵ Therein, what is non-delusion? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view — this is called "non-delusion". These are called "the wholesome roots". ⤵ Therein, what is the formation that has a wholesome root as condition? The intention, intending, state of intending — this is called "the formation that has a wholesome root as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the consciousness that has the formation as condition… the mentality that has consciousness as condition… the sixth sense-field that has mentality as condition… the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition… the feeling that has contact as condition… this is called "the feeling that has contact as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the confidence that has feeling as condition? The confidence, trusting, reliance, full confidence — this is called "the confidence that has feeling as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the decision that has confidence as condition? The decision of the mind, deciding, the state of being decided upon — this is called "the decision that has confidence as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the existence that has decision as condition? Setting aside decision: the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness — this is called "the existence that has decision as condition"… therefore it is said, "thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering".

Which things are neutral? Which things are neutral? On the occasion when, because unwholesome action has been done and accumulated, resultant eye-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, with a sight as its object… ear-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, with a sound as its object… nose-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, with a smell as its object… tongue-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, with a taste as its object… body-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by pain, with a tangible thing as its object — on that occasion, with the formation as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense-field; with the sixth sense-field as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Therein, what is the formation? The intention, intending, state of intending — this is called "the formation". ⤵ Therein, what is the consciousness that has the formation as condition? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ saddārammaṇaṃ…pe… ghānaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ gandhārammaṇaṃ…pe… jivhāviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rasārammaṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti dukkhasahagataṃ phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ…pe… manodhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… phoṭṭhabbārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye akusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

**en** `490335–491463`
Which things are neutral? On the occasion when, because unwholesome action has been done and accumulated, resultant ear-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, with a sound as its object… nose-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, with a smell as its object… tongue-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, with a taste as its object… body-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by pain, with a tangible thing as its object… the mind element has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, with a sight as its object… or a tangible thing as its object, or based on whatever it may be — on that occasion, with an unwholesome root as condition, a formation; with the formation as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense-field; with the sixth sense-field as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, decision; with decision as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

### 511

**pi** `335868–336377`
Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye akusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso , phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti , jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

**en** `491464–492257`
Which things are neutral? On the occasion when, because unwholesome action has been done and accumulated, the resultant mind-consciousness element has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, with a sight as its object… or a mental object as its object, or based on whatever it may be — on that occasion, with an unwholesome root as condition, a formation; with the formation as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense-field; with the sixth sense-field as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, decision; with decision as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

### 512

**pi** `336378–338262`
Tattha katamo akusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "akusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati "saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati "viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati "nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamo chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso? Yo phasso phusanā samphusanā samphusitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso". ⤵ Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "phassapaccayā vedanā". ⤵ Tattha katamo vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati "vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho". ⤵ Tattha katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati "adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo". ⤵ Tattha katamā bhavapaccayā jāti? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ jāti sañjāti nibbatti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo – ayaṃ vuccati "bhavapaccayā jāti". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ? Atthi jarā, atthi maraṇaṃ. Tattha katamā jarā? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ jarā jīraṇatā āyuno saṃhāni – ayaṃ vuccati jarā. Tattha katamaṃ maraṇaṃ? Yo tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ khayo vayo bhedo paribhedo aniccatā antaradhānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "maraṇaṃ". Iti ayañca jarā, idañca maraṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati "jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ". ⤵ Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotīti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa saṅgati hoti, samāgamo hoti, samodhānaṃ hoti, pātubhāvo hoti. Tena vuccati evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī"ti.

**en** `492258–495114`
Therein, what is the formation that has an unwholesome root as condition? The intention, intending, state of intending — this is called "the formation that has an unwholesome root as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the consciousness that has the formation as condition? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the consciousness that has the formation as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the mentality that has consciousness as condition? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations — this is called "the mentality that has consciousness as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the sixth sense-field that has mentality as condition? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the sixth sense-field that has mentality as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition? The contact, touching, being in contact, state of being in contact — this is called "the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the feeling that has contact as condition? Mental experience that is neither comfortable nor uncomfortable, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant experience born of mind-contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "the feeling that has contact as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the decision that has feeling as condition? The decision of the mind, deciding, the state of being decided upon — this is called "the decision that has feeling as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the existence that has decision as condition? Setting aside decision: the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness — this is called "the existence that has decision as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the birth that has existence as condition? The birth of the various states, their being born, arising, coming forth, appearance — this is called "the birth that has existence as condition". ⤵ Therein, what are the aging and death that have birth as condition? There is aging, there is death. Therein, what is aging? The aging of the various states, their growing old, the decline of their life span — this is called aging. Therein, what is death? The destruction of the various states, their vanishing, breakup, disintegration, impermanence, disappearance — this is called "death". So this is aging and this is death. This is called "the aging and death that have birth as condition". ⤵ "Thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering": thus there is the coming together of this entire mass of suffering, its meeting, its combination, its appearance. Therefore it is said, "thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering".

### 518

**pi** `338445–339202`
Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā – idha bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ kāye kāyānupassī viharati bahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati ajjhattabahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, ajjhattaṃ vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati bahiddhā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ajjhattabahiddhā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, ajjhattaṃ citte cittānupassī viharati bahiddhā citte cittānupassī viharati ajjhattabahiddhā citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, ajjhattaṃ dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati bahiddhā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ajjhattabahiddhā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

**en** `495389–496636`
There are four foundations of mindfulness. Here a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body internally, dwells contemplating the body in the body externally, dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings internally, dwells contemplating feelings in feelings externally, dwells contemplating feelings in feelings both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world. He dwells contemplating the mind in the mind internally, dwells contemplating the mind in the mind externally, dwells contemplating the mind in the mind both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world. He dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects internally, dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects externally, dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world.

### 520

**pi** `339236–341030`
Kathañca bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ kāye kāyānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ kāyaṃ uddhaṃ pādatalā adho kesamatthakā tacapariyantaṃ pūraṃ nānappakārassa asucino paccavekkhati – "atthi imasmiṃ kāye kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru [nahāru (sī.)] aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ [aṭṭhimiñjā (sī.)] vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā mutta"nti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapeti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevitvā bhāvetvā bahulīkaritvā svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapetvā bahiddhā kāye cittaṃ upasaṃharati. ⤵ Kathañca bhikkhu bahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu bahiddhā kāyaṃ uddhaṃ pādatalā adho kesamatthakā tacapariyantaṃ pūraṃ nānappakārassa asucino paccavekkhati – "atthissa kāye kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā mutta"nti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapeti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevitvā bhāvetvā bahulīkaritvā svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapetvā ajjhattabahiddhā kāye cittaṃ upasaṃharati. ⤵ Kathañca bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā kāyaṃ uddhaṃ pādatalā adho kesamatthakā tacapariyantaṃ pūraṃ nānappakārassa asucino paccavekkhati – "atthi imasmiṃ kāye kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā mutta"nti. Evaṃ bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

**en** `496690–498948`
And how does a monk dwell contemplating the body in the body internally? Here a monk reviews his own body internally, from the soles of the feet up and from the top of the head down, enclosed by skin, full of many kinds of impurity: "There are in this body head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, membranes, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach contents, excrement, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, fluid of the joints, urine." He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to the body externally. ⤵ And how does a monk dwell contemplating the body in the body externally? Here a monk reviews a body externally, from the soles of the feet up and from the top of the head down, enclosed by skin, full of many kinds of impurity: "There are in this person's body head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, membranes, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach contents, excrement, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, fluid of the joints, urine." He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to the body both internally and externally. ⤵ And how does a monk dwell contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally? Here a monk reviews the body both internally and externally, from the soles of the feet up and from the top of the head down, enclosed by skin, full of many kinds of impurity: "There are in this body head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, membranes, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach contents, excrement, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, fluid of the joints, urine." Thus a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world.

### 521

**pi** `341031–341266`
Anupassīti. Tattha katamā anupassanā? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati "anupassanā". Imāya anupassanāya upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati "anupassī"ti.

**en** `498949–499290`
"Contemplating": therein, what is contemplation? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view — this is called "contemplation". He is endowed with this contemplation, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "contemplating".

### 522

**pi** `341267–341359`

**en** `499291–499421`
"Dwells": he moves, goes on, keeps going, maintains himself, carries on, conducts himself, dwells. Therefore it is said, "dwells".

### 523

**pi** `341360–341591`
Ātāpīti. Tattha katamo ātāpo [katamaṃ ātāpaṃ (sabbattha)]? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – ayaṃ vuccati "ātāpo". Iminā ātāpena upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati "ātāpī"ti.

**en** `499422–499697`
"Ardent": therein, what is ardour? The mental initiation of energy… right effort — this is called "ardour". He is endowed with this ardour, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "ardent".

### 524

**pi** `341592–341833`
Sampajānoti . Tattha katamaṃ sampajaññaṃ? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati "sampajaññaṃ". Iminā sampajaññena upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati "sampajāno"ti.

**en** `499698–500073`
"Clearly comprehending": therein, what is clear comprehension? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view — this is called "clear comprehension". He is endowed with this clear comprehension, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "clearly comprehending".

### 525

**pi** `341834–342025`
Satimāti. Tattha katamā sati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati – ayaṃ vuccati "sati". Imāya satiyā upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati "satimā"ti.

**en** `500074–500369`
"Mindful": therein, what is mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness — this is called "mindfulness". He is endowed with this mindfulness, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "mindful".

### 526

**pi** `342026–342624`
Vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassanti. Tattha katamo loko? Sveva kāyo loko. Pañcapi upādānakkhandhā loko. Ayaṃ vuccati "loko". Tattha katamā abhijjhā? Yo rāgo sārāgo…pe… cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati "abhijjhā". Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "domanassaṃ". Iti ayañca abhijjhā idañca domanassaṃ imamhi loke vinītā honti paṭivinītā santā samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati "vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassa"nti.

**en** `500370–501200`
"Having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world": therein, what is the world? This very body is the world; the five aggregates that can be clung to are also the world. This is called "the world". Therein, what is covetousness? The lust, passion… passion of the mind — this is called "covetousness". Therein, what is grief? Mental discomfort, mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "grief". So this covetousness and this grief are removed in this world, thoroughly removed, stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world".

### 529

**pi** `342682–345499`
Kathañca bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno "sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī"ti pajānāti, dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno "dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī"ti pajānāti, adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno "adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī"ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ vā sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno "sāmisaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī"ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno "nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī"ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno "sāmisaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī"ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno "nirāmisaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī"ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno "sāmisaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī"ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno "nirāmisaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī"ti pajānāti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapeti. He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to feelings externally. ⤵ And how does a monk dwell contemplating feelings in feelings externally? Here a monk knows of one feeling a pleasant feeling, "he feels a pleasant feeling"; of one feeling a painful feeling, he knows "he feels a painful feeling"; of one feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows "he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling"; of one feeling a worldly pleasant feeling, he knows "he feels a worldly pleasant feeling"; of one feeling an unworldly pleasant feeling, he knows "he feels an unworldly pleasant feeling"; of one feeling a worldly painful feeling, he knows "he feels a worldly painful feeling"; of one feeling an unworldly painful feeling, he knows "he feels an unworldly painful feeling"; of one feeling a worldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows "he feels a worldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling"; of one feeling an unworldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows "he feels an unworldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling". Here a monk knows a pleasant feeling as "a pleasant feeling"; he knows a painful feeling as "a painful feeling"; he knows a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling as "a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling"; he knows a worldly pleasant feeling as "a worldly pleasant feeling"; he knows an unworldly pleasant feeling as "an unworldly pleasant feeling"; he knows a worldly painful feeling as "a worldly painful feeling"; he knows an unworldly painful feeling as "an unworldly painful feeling"; he knows a worldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling as "a worldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling"; he knows an unworldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling as "an unworldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling". Anupassīti …pe… viharatīti…pe… ātāpīti…pe… sampajānoti…pe… satimāti…pe… vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassanti. Tattha katamo loko? Sāyeva vedanā loko. Pañcapi upādānakkhandhā loko. Ayaṃ vuccati "loko". Tattha katamā abhijjhā? Yo rāgo sārāgo…pe… cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati "abhijjhā". Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "domanassaṃ". Iti ayañca abhijjhā idañca domanassaṃ imamhi loke vinītā honti paṭivinītā santā samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. **en** `504614–505520`
"Contemplating"… "dwells"… "ardent"… "clearly comprehending"… "mindful"… "having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world": therein, what is the world? That very feeling is the world; the five aggregates that can be clung to are also the world. This is called "the world". Therein, what is covetousness? The lust, passion… passion of the mind — this is called "covetousness". Therein, what is grief? Mental discomfort, mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "grief". So this covetousness and this grief are removed in this world, thoroughly removed, stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world".

Here a monk knows a mind with lust as "my mind has lust"; he knows a mind without lust as "my mind is without lust"; he knows a mind with hate as "my mind has hate"; he knows a mind without hate as "my mind is without hate"; he knows a mind with delusion as "my mind has delusion"; he knows a mind without delusion as "my mind is without delusion"; he knows a contracted mind as "my mind is contracted"; he knows a distracted mind as "my mind is distracted"; he knows an expanded mind as "my mind is expanded"; he knows an unexpanded mind as "my mind is unexpanded"; he knows a surpassable mind as "my mind is surpassable"; he knows an unsurpassable mind as "my mind is unsurpassable"; he knows a concentrated mind as "my mind is concentrated"; he knows an unconcentrated mind as "my mind is unconcentrated"; he knows a freed mind as "my mind is freed"; he knows an unfreed mind as "my mind is unfreed". He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to the mind externally. ⤵ And how does a monk dwell contemplating the mind in the mind externally? Here a monk knows another's mind with lust as "his mind has lust"; he knows his mind without lust as "his mind is without lust"; he knows his mind with hate as "his mind has hate"; he knows his mind without hate as "his mind is without hate"; he knows his mind with delusion as "his mind has delusion"; he knows his mind without delusion as "his mind is without delusion"; he knows his contracted mind as "his mind is contracted"; he knows his distracted mind as "his mind is distracted"; he knows his expanded mind as "his mind is expanded"; he knows his unexpanded mind as "his mind is unexpanded"; he knows his surpassable mind as "his mind is surpassable"; he knows his unsurpassable mind as "his mind is unsurpassable"; he knows his concentrated mind as "his mind is concentrated"; he knows his unconcentrated mind as "his mind is unconcentrated"; he knows his freed mind as "his mind is freed"; he knows his unfreed mind as "his mind is unfreed". Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to the mind both internally and externally. ⤵ And how does a monk dwell contemplating the mind in the mind both internally and externally? Here a monk knows a mind with lust as "a mind with lust"; he knows a mind without lust as "a mind without lust"; he knows a mind with hate as "a mind with hate"; he knows a mind without hate as "a mind without hate"; he knows a mind with delusion as "a mind with delusion"; he knows a mind without delusion as "a mind without delusion"; he knows a contracted mind as "a contracted mind"; he knows a distracted mind as "a distracted mind"; he knows an expanded mind as "an expanded mind"; he knows an unexpanded mind as "an unexpanded mind"; he knows a surpassable mind as "a surpassable mind"; he knows an unsurpassable mind as "an unsurpassable mind"; he knows a concentrated mind as "a concentrated mind"; he knows an unconcentrated mind as "an unconcentrated mind"; he knows a freed mind as "a freed mind"; he knows an unfreed mind as "an unfreed mind".
