So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevitvā bhāvetvā bahulīkaritvā svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapetvā ajjhattabahiddhā dhammesu cittaṃ upasaṃharati. ⤵ Kathañca bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu santaṃ vā kāmacchandaṃ "atthi kāmacchando"ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā kāmacchandaṃ "natthi kāmacchando"ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa kāmacchandassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa kāmacchandassa pahānaṃ hoti tañca pajānāti , yathā ca pahīnassa kāmacchandassa āyatiṃ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti. Santaṃ vā byāpādaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā thinamiddhaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā uddhaccakukkuccaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā vicikicchaṃ "atthi vicikicchā"ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā vicikicchaṃ "natthi vicikicchā"ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannāya vicikicchāya uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannāya vicikicchāya pahānaṃ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnāya vicikicchāya āyatiṃ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti. ⤵ Santaṃ vā satisambojjhaṅgaṃ "atthi satisambojjhaṅgo"ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā satisambojjhaṅgaṃ "natthi satisambojjhaṅgo"ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti. Santaṃ vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ "atthi upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo"ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ "natthi upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo"ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti. Evaṃ bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

**en** `510167–516581`
And how does a monk dwell contemplating mental objects in mental objects internally? Here a monk, when sense desire is present in him, knows "sense desire is present in me"; when sense desire is not present in him, he knows "sense desire is not present in me"; he knows how unarisen sense desire arises; he knows how arisen sense desire is abandoned; and he knows how abandoned sense desire does not arise again in the future. When ill will is present in him… when dullness and drowsiness are present in him… when restlessness and remorse are present in him… when doubt is present in him, he knows "doubt is present in me"; when doubt is not present in him, he knows "doubt is not present in me"; he knows how unarisen doubt arises; he knows how arisen doubt is abandoned; and he knows how abandoned doubt does not arise again in the future. ⤵ When the awakening factor of mindfulness is present in him, he knows "the awakening factor of mindfulness is present in me"; when the awakening factor of mindfulness is not present in him, he knows "the awakening factor of mindfulness is not present in me"; he knows how the unarisen awakening factor of mindfulness arises; and he knows how the arisen awakening factor of mindfulness is perfected by development. When the awakening factor of investigation of things is present in him… when the awakening factor of energy is present in him… when the awakening factor of joy is present in him… when the awakening factor of tranquillity is present in him… when the awakening factor of concentration is present in him… when the awakening factor of equanimity is present in him, he knows "the awakening factor of equanimity is present in me"; when the awakening factor of equanimity is not present in him, he knows "the awakening factor of equanimity is not present in me"; he knows how the unarisen awakening factor of equanimity arises; and he knows how the arisen awakening factor of equanimity is perfected by development. He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to mental objects externally. ⤵ And how does a monk dwell contemplating mental objects in mental objects externally? Here a monk, when sense desire is present in another, knows "sense desire is present in him"; when sense desire is not present in him, he knows "sense desire is not present in him"; he knows how unarisen sense desire arises; he knows how arisen sense desire is abandoned; and he knows how abandoned sense desire does not arise again in the future. When ill will is present in him… when dullness and drowsiness are present in him… when restlessness and remorse are present in him… when doubt is present in him, he knows "doubt is present in him"; when doubt is not present in him, he knows "doubt is not present in him"; he knows how unarisen doubt arises; he knows how arisen doubt is abandoned; and he knows how abandoned doubt does not arise again in the future. ⤵ When the awakening factor of mindfulness is present in him, he knows "the awakening factor of mindfulness is present in him"; when the awakening factor of mindfulness is not present in him, he knows "the awakening factor of mindfulness is not present in him"; he knows how the unarisen awakening factor of mindfulness arises; and he knows how the arisen awakening factor of mindfulness is perfected by development. When the awakening factor of investigation of things is present in him… when the awakening factor of energy is present in him… when the awakening factor of joy is present in him… when the awakening factor of tranquillity is present in him… when the awakening factor of concentration is present in him… when the awakening factor of equanimity is present in him, he knows "the awakening factor of equanimity is present in him"; when the awakening factor of equanimity is not present in him, he knows "the awakening factor of equanimity is not present in him"; he knows how the unarisen awakening factor of equanimity arises; and he knows how the arisen awakening factor of equanimity is perfected by development. He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to mental objects both internally and externally. ⤵ And how does a monk dwell contemplating mental objects in mental objects both internally and externally? Here a monk, when sense desire is present, knows "sense desire is present"; when sense desire is not present, he knows "sense desire is not present"; he knows how unarisen sense desire arises; he knows how arisen sense desire is abandoned; and he knows how abandoned sense desire does not arise again in the future. When ill will is present… when dullness and drowsiness are present… when restlessness and remorse are present… when doubt is present, he knows "doubt is present"; when doubt is not present, he knows "doubt is not present"; he knows how unarisen doubt arises; he knows how arisen doubt is abandoned; and he knows how abandoned doubt does not arise again in the future. ⤵ When the awakening factor of mindfulness is present, he knows "the awakening factor of mindfulness is present"; when the awakening factor of mindfulness is not present, he knows "the awakening factor of mindfulness is not present"; he knows how the unarisen awakening factor of mindfulness arises; and he knows how the arisen awakening factor of mindfulness is perfected by development. When the awakening factor of investigation of things is present… when the awakening factor of energy is present… when the awakening factor of joy is present… when the awakening factor of tranquillity is present… when the awakening factor of concentration is present… when the awakening factor of equanimity is present, he knows "the awakening factor of equanimity is present"; when the awakening factor of equanimity is not present, he knows "the awakening factor of equanimity is not present"; he knows how the unarisen awakening factor of equanimity arises; and he knows how the arisen awakening factor of equanimity is perfected by development. Thus a monk dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world.

### 538

**pi** `355744–355977`
Anupassīti. Tattha katamā anupassanā? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati anupassanā. Imāya anupassanāya upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati "anupassī"ti.

**en** `516582–516921`
"Contemplating": therein, what is contemplation? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view — this is called contemplation. He is endowed with this contemplation, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "contemplating".

### 543

**pi** `356583–357182`
Vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassanti. Tattha katamo loko? Teva dhammā loko. Pañcapi upādānakkhandhā loko. Ayaṃ vuccati "loko". Tattha katamā abhijjhā? Yo rāgo sārāgo…pe… cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati "abhijjhā". Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "domanassaṃ". Iti ayañca abhijjhā idañca domanassaṃ imamhi loke vinītā honti paṭivinītā santā samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati "vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassa"nti.

**en** `517746–518588`
"Having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world": therein, what is the world? Those very mental objects are the world; the five aggregates that can be clung to are also the world. This is called "the world". Therein, what is covetousness? The lust, passion… passion of the mind — this is called "covetousness". Therein, what is grief? Mental discomfort, mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "grief". So this covetousness and this grief are removed in this world, thoroughly removed, stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world".

**en** `518752–518990`
There are four foundations of mindfulness. Here a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, dwells contemplating the mind in the mind, dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects.

### 548

**pi** `357418–357850`
Kathañca bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ kāye kāyānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "satipaṭṭhānaṃ". Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

**en** `518991–519691`
And how does a monk dwell contemplating the body in the body? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge, contemplating the body in the body — the mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, awakening factor of mindfulness, path factor, included in the path, that there is on that occasion: this is called "the foundation of mindfulness". The remaining things are associated with the foundation of mindfulness.

Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ citte cittānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "satipaṭṭhānaṃ". Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

**en** `524875–525934`
And how does a monk dwell contemplating the mind in the mind? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge — on that occasion there is contact… there is non-distraction. These things are wholesome. When, because that same wholesome meditative absorption beyond the world has been done and developed, as its result — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge, on emptiness, contemplating the mind in the mind — the mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, awakening factor of mindfulness, path factor, included in the path, that there is on that occasion: this is called "the foundation of mindfulness". The remaining things are associated with the foundation of mindfulness.

### 561

**pi** `363120–363497`
Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā – idha bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

**en** `528138–528805`
There are four foundations of mindfulness. Here a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world; he dwells contemplating feelings in feelings — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world; he dwells contemplating the mind in the mind — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world; he dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world.

### 562

**pi** `363498–363592`

**en** `528806–528969`
Of the four foundations of mindfulness, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral… how many involve conflict, how many are free from conflict?

### 563

**pi** `363593–363610`
<h2>1. Tikaṃ</h2>

**en** `528970–528992`

### 564

**pi** `363611–364533`
Siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Siyā vipākā siyā vipākadhammadhammā. Anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā. Appamāṇā. Appamāṇārammaṇā. Paṇītā. Siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Na maggārammaṇā , siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Bahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

**en** `528993–530662`
They may be wholesome; they may be neutral. They may be associated with pleasant feeling; they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They may be results; they may be things subject to result. They are not taken up at birth and not able to be clung to. They are undefiled and not connected with defilement. They may be with thought and with examination; they may be without thought but with examination only; they may be without thought and without examination. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be accompanied by happiness; they may be accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They may be leading to dismantling; they may be leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling. They may belong to one in training; they may belong to one beyond training. They are measureless. They have measureless objects. They are refined. They may be fixed in rightness; they may be unfixed. They do not have the path as their object; they may have the path as their cause; they may have the path as their dominant factor; they may not be describable either as having the path as their cause or as having the path as their dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they may be due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. They are not describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. They have external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.

### 566

**pi** `364552–365892`
Na hetū. Sahetukā. Hetusampayuttā. Na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Na hetū sahetukā. ⤵ Sappaccayā. Saṅkhatā. Anidassanā. Appaṭighā. Arūpā. Lokuttarā. Kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā. No āsavā. Anāsavā. Āsavavippayuttā. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavācātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttācātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā. Anāsavā. No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā. No cittā. Cetasikā. Cittasampayuttā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhā. Cittasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasahabhuno. Cittānuparivattino. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Bāhirā. No upādā. Anupādinnā . No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. ⤵ Siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā . Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Na kāmāvacarā. Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā. Apariyāpannā. Siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā. Siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā. Anuttarā. Araṇāti.

**en** `530685–533256`
They are not roots. They have roots. They are associated with roots. They are not describable as being both roots and having roots; they have roots but are not roots. They are not describable as being both roots and associated with roots; they are associated with roots but are not roots. They are not roots yet have roots. ⤵ They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. They are beyond the world. They can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another. They are not mental taints. They are without mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. They are not describable either as being mental taints and subject to mental taints, or as being subject to mental taints but not mental taints. They are not describable either as being mental taints and associated with mental taints, or as being associated with mental taints but not mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. They are without mental taints. They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects. They are not minds. They are mental factors. They are associated with mind. They are conjoined with mind. They are originated by mind. They arise together with mind. They follow along with mind. They are conjoined with and originated by mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind. They are external. They are not derived. They are not taken up at birth. They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing, not to be abandoned by meditative development. Their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing. Their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. ⤵ They may be with thought; they may be without thought. They may be with examination; they may be without examination. They may be with joy; they may be without joy. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be not accompanied by joy. They may be accompanied by happiness; they may be not accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity; they may be not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. They are not included in any sphere. They may be leading out; they may be not leading out. They may be fixed; they may be unfixed. They are unsurpassed. They are free from conflict.

### 571

**pi** `366005–366560`
Cattāro sammappadhānā – idha bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

**en** `533452–534164`
There are four right efforts. Here a monk generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the abandoning of evil, unwholesome things that have arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the arising of wholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the persistence of wholesome things that have arisen, for their non-confusion, their increase, their expansion, their development, their perfection.

### 572

**pi** `366561–367123`
Kathañca bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati? Tattha katame anuppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā? Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho, doso, moho. Tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā. Taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ime vuccanti "anuppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā". Iti imesaṃ anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

**en** `534165–534970`
And how does a monk generate desire, strive, initiate energy, exert his mind, and endeavour for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen? Therein, what are the evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen? The three unwholesome roots — greed, hate, delusion — and the defilements that stand together with them; the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness associated with them; and the bodily action, verbal action, and mental action originated by them — these are called "the evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen". So he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of these evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen.

### 573

**pi** `367124–367420`
Chandaṃ janetīti. Tattha katamo chando? Yo chando chandikatā [chandīkatā (syā.)] kattukamyatā kusalo dhammacchando – ayaṃ vuccati "chando". Imaṃ chandaṃ janeti sañjaneti uṭṭhapeti samuṭṭhapeti [uṭṭhāpeti samuṭṭhāpeti (syā.) evamuparipi] nibbatteti abhinibbatteti. Tena vuccati "chandaṃ janetī"ti.

**en** `534971–535250`
"Generates desire": therein, what is desire? The desire, wishing, wish to act, wholesome desire for the Dhamma — this is called "desire". He generates this desire, brings it forth, raises it, rouses it, produces it, brings it into being. Therefore it is said, "generates desire".

### 574

**pi** `367421–367632`
Vāyamatīti. Tattha katamo vāyāmo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – ayaṃ vuccati "vāyāmo". Iminā vāyāmena upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati "vāyamatī"ti.

**en** `535251–535534`
"Strives": therein, what is striving? The mental initiation of energy… right effort — this is called "striving". He is endowed with this striving, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "strives".

### 575

**pi** `367633–367842`
Vīriyaṃ ārabhatīti. Tattha katamaṃ vīriyaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – idaṃ vuccati "vīriyaṃ". Imaṃ vīriyaṃ ārabhati samārabhati āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati "vīriyaṃ ārabhatī"ti.

**en** `535535–535777`
"Initiates energy": therein, what is energy? The mental initiation of energy… right effort — this is called "energy". He initiates this energy, undertakes it, practises it, develops it, cultivates it. Therefore it is said, "initiates energy".

### 576

**pi** `367843–368067`
Cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti. Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati "cittaṃ". Imaṃ cittaṃ paggaṇhāti sampaggaṇhāti upatthambheti paccupatthambheti. Tena vuccati "cittaṃ paggaṇhātī"ti.

**en** `535778–536039`
"Exerts his mind": therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". He exerts this mind, fully exerts it, supports it, upholds it. Therefore it is said, "exerts his mind".

### 577

**pi** `368068–368243`
Padahatīti. Tattha katamaṃ padhānaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – idaṃ vuccati "padhānaṃ". Iminā padhānena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati "padahatī"ti.

**en** `536040–536247`
"Endeavours": therein, what is endeavour? The mental initiation of energy… right effort — this is called "endeavour". He is endowed with this endeavour… furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "endeavours".

### 578

**pi** `368244–368794`
Kathañca bhikkhu uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati? Tattha katame uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā? ### 584

**pi** `369809–370311`
Kathañca bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati? Tattha katame anuppannā kusalā dhammā? Tīṇi kusalamūlāni – alobho, adoso, amoho. Taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho. Taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime vuccanti "anuppannā kusalā dhammā". Iti imesaṃ anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

**en** `538212–538935`
And how does a monk generate desire, strive, initiate energy, exert his mind, and endeavour for the arising of wholesome things that have not yet arisen? Therein, what are the wholesome things that have not yet arisen? The three wholesome roots — non-greed, non-hate, non-delusion; the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness associated with them; and the bodily action, verbal action, and mental action originated by them — these are called "the wholesome things that have not yet arisen". So he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the arising of these wholesome things that have not yet arisen.

**en** `540700–541412`
There are four right efforts. Here a monk generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the abandoning of evil, unwholesome things that have arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the arising of wholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the persistence of wholesome things that have arisen, for their non-confusion, their increase, their expansion, their development, their perfection.

Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge — the mental initiation of energy… right effort, the awakening factor of energy, a path factor, included in the path, that there is on that occasion: this is called "right effort". The remaining things are associated with right effort.

### 612

**pi** `377705–378130`
Cattāro sammappadhānā – idha bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya…pe… anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya…pe… uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

**en** `548580–549132`
There are four right efforts. Here a monk generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen; for the abandoning of evil, unwholesome things that have arisen… for the arising of wholesome things that have not yet arisen… for the persistence of wholesome things that have arisen, for their non-confusion, their increase, their expansion, their development, their perfection he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours.

### 613

### 615

**pi** `378245–379044`
Kusalāyeva . Siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Vipākadhammadhammā . Anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Apacayagāmino. Sekkhā. Appamāṇā. Appamāṇārammaṇā. Paṇītā. Sammattaniyatā. Na maggārammaṇā. Maggahetukā. Siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggādhipatinoti. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā uppādinoti. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Bahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

**en** `549307–550766`
They are wholesome only. They may be associated with pleasant feeling; they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They are things subject to result. They are not taken up at birth and not able to be clung to. They are undefiled and not connected with defilement. They may be with thought and with examination; they may be without thought but with examination only; they may be without thought and without examination. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be accompanied by happiness; they may be accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They are leading to dismantling. They belong to one in training. They are measureless. They have measureless objects. They are refined. They are fixed in rightness. They do not have the path as their object. They have the path as their cause. They may have the path as their dominant factor; they may not be describable as having the path as their dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they are not describable as due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. They are not describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. They have external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.

### 617

**pi** `379063–380360`
Na hetū. Sahetukā. Hetusampayuttā. Na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Na hetū sahetukā. Sappaccayā. Saṅkhatā. Anidassanā. Appaṭighā. Arūpā . Lokuttarā. Kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā. No āsavā. Anāsavā. Āsavavippayuttā. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavā cātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā. Anāsavā. No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā. No cittā. Cetasikā. Cittasampayuttā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhā. Cittasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasahabhuno. Cittānuparivattino. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Bāhirā. No upādā. Anupādinnā. No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā . Siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Na kāmāvacarā. Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā. Apariyāpannā. Niyyānikā. Niyatā. Anuttarā. Araṇāti.

**en** `550789–553309`
They are not roots. They have roots. They are associated with roots. They are not describable as being both roots and having roots; they have roots but are not roots. They are not describable as being both roots and associated with roots; they are associated with roots but are not roots. They are not roots yet have roots. They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. They are beyond the world. They can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another. They are not mental taints. They are without mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. They are not describable either as being mental taints and subject to mental taints, or as being subject to mental taints but not mental taints. They are not describable either as being mental taints and associated with mental taints, or as being associated with mental taints but not mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. They are without mental taints. They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects. They are not minds. They are mental factors. They are associated with mind. They are conjoined with mind. They are originated by mind. They arise together with mind. They follow along with mind. They are conjoined with and originated by mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind. They are external. They are not derived. They are not taken up at birth. They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing. Their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. They may be with thought; they may be without thought. They may be with examination; they may be without examination. They may be with joy; they may be without joy. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be not accompanied by joy. They may be accompanied by happiness; they may be not accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity; they may be not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. They are not included in any sphere. They are leading out. They are fixed. They are unsurpassed. They are free from conflict.

### 622

**pi** `380470–380746`
Cattāro iddhipādā – idha bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti.

**en** `553495–553973`
There are four bases of success. Here a monk develops the basis of success endowed with concentration through desire and the formations of endeavour; he develops the basis of success endowed with concentration through energy and the formations of endeavour; he develops the basis of success endowed with concentration through mind and the formations of endeavour; he develops the basis of success endowed with concentration through investigation and the formations of endeavour.

### 623

**pi** `380747–380773`
<h2>1. Chandiddhipādo</h2>

**en** `553974–554021`
<h2>1. The Basis of Success Through Desire</h2>

### 624

**pi** `380774–381711`
Kathañca bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti? Chandaṃ ce bhikkhu adhipatiṃ karitvā labhati samādhiṃ, labhati cittassekaggataṃ [cittassa ekaggataṃ (sī. syā.)] – ayaṃ vuccati "chandasamādhi". So anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati. Ime vuccanti "padhānasaṅkhārā". Iti ayañca chandasamādhi, ime ca padhānasaṅkhārā. Tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññahitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārotveva saṅkhyaṃ [saṅkhaṃ (sī.)] gacchati.

**en** `554022–555245`
And how does a monk develop the basis of success endowed with concentration through desire and the formations of endeavour? If a monk, making desire the dominant factor, obtains concentration, obtains one-pointedness of mind — this is called "concentration through desire". He generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the abandoning of evil, unwholesome things that have arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the arising of wholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the persistence of wholesome things that have arisen, for their non-confusion, their increase, their expansion, their development, their perfection. These are called "the formations of endeavour". So there is this concentration through desire and there are these formations of endeavour. Gathering them together and summing them up, they are reckoned simply as "concentration through desire and the formations of endeavour".

### 625

**pi** `381712–382456`
Tattha katamo chando? Yo chando chandikatā kattukamyatā kusalo dhammacchando – ayaṃ vuccati "chando". ⤵ Tattha katamo samādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti avaṭṭhiti avisāhāro avikkhepo avisāhaṭamānasatā samatho samādhindriyaṃ samādhibalaṃ sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati "samādhi". ⤵ Tattha katamo padhānasaṅkhāro? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho nikkamo parakkamo uyyāmo vāyāmo ussāho ussoḷhī thāmo ṭhiti asithilaparakkamatā anikkhittachandatā anikkhittadhuratā dhurasampaggāho vīriyaṃ vīriyindriyaṃ vīriyabalaṃ sammāvāyāmo – ayaṃ vuccati "padhānasaṅkhāro". Iti iminā ca chandena, iminā ca samādhinā, iminā ca padhānasaṅkhārena upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati "chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgato"ti.

**en** `555246–556314`
Therein, what is desire? The desire, wishing, wish to act, wholesome desire for the Dhamma — this is called "desire". ⤵ Therein, what is concentration? The steadiness of the mind, its stability, its firm standing, its non-wavering, non-distraction, the state of an undistracted mind, calm, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration — this is called "concentration". ⤵ Therein, what is the formation of endeavour? The mental initiation of energy, exertion, striving forward, effort, striving, zeal, vigour, firmness, steadiness, unrelaxed striving, undiminished desire, undiminished responsibility, taking up the burden, energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, right effort — this is called "the formation of endeavour". So he is endowed with this desire, this concentration, and this formation of endeavour, fully endowed, having reached them, fully reached them, possessed of them, complete in them, furnished with them. Therefore it is said, "endowed with concentration through desire and the formations of endeavour".

### 626

**pi** `382457–382782`
Iddhīti. Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ iddhi samiddhi ijjhanā samijjhanā lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā. ⤵ "Iddhipādo"ti. Tathābhūtassa vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho. ⤵ "Iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī"ti. Te dhamme āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati "iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī"ti.

**en** `556315–556799`
"Success": the success of those things, their prospering, succeeding, fully succeeding, gain, obtaining, attainment, full attainment, touching, realisation, achievement. ⤵ "Basis of success": for one who is such, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness. ⤵ "Develops the basis of success": he practises those things, develops them, cultivates them. Therefore it is said, "develops the basis of success".

### 636

**pi** `385947–386710`
Kathañca bhikkhu vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti? Vīmaṃsaṃ ce bhikkhu adhipatiṃ karitvā labhati samādhiṃ labhati cittassekaggataṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "vīmaṃsāsamādhi". So anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya…pe… anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya…pe… uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati. Ime vuccanti "padhānasaṅkhārā". Iti ayañca vīmaṃsāsamādhi, ime ca padhānasaṅkhārā; tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārotveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

**en** `561251–562349`
And how does a monk develop the basis of success endowed with concentration through investigation and the formations of endeavour? If a monk, making investigation the dominant factor, obtains concentration, obtains one-pointedness of mind — this is called "concentration through investigation". He generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen; for the abandoning of evil, unwholesome things that have arisen… for the arising of wholesome things that have not yet arisen… for the persistence of wholesome things that have arisen, for their non-confusion, their increase, their expansion, their development, their perfection he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours. These are called "the formations of endeavour". So there is this concentration through investigation and there are these formations of endeavour; gathering them together and summing them up, they are reckoned simply as "concentration through investigation and the formations of endeavour".

The mental initiation of energy… right effort — this is called "the formation of endeavour". So he is endowed with this investigation, this concentration, and this formation of endeavour… furnished with them. Therefore it is said, "endowed with concentration through investigation and the formations of endeavour".

Avasesā dhammā vīriyiddhipādasampayuttā.

**en** `572247–572913`
Therein, what is the basis of success through energy? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge — the mental initiation of energy… right effort, the awakening factor of energy, a path factor, included in the path, that there is on that occasion: this is called "the basis of success through energy". The remaining things are associated with the basis of success through energy.

### 661

**pi** `393795–394175`

Avasesā dhammā cittiddhipādasampayuttā.

**en** `572914–573541`
Therein, what is the basis of success through mind? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge — the mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element that there is on that occasion: this is called "the basis of success through mind". The remaining things are associated with the basis of success through mind.

### 662

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "vīmaṃsiddhipādo". Avasesā dhammā vīmaṃsiddhipādasampayuttā.

**en** `573542–574277`
Therein, what is the basis of success through investigation? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge — the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view, the awakening factor of investigation of things, a path factor, included in the path, that there is on that occasion: this is called "the basis of success through investigation". The remaining things are associated with the basis of success through investigation.

### 668

**pi** `394968–395730`
Kusalāyeva. Siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Vipākadhammadhammā. Anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā , siyā avitakkaavicārā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Apacayagāmino. Sekkhā. Appamāṇā. Appamāṇārammaṇā. Paṇītā. Sammattaniyatā. Na maggārammaṇā, maggahetukā, na maggādhipatino. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā uppādinoti. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi , paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Bahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

**en** `574887–576276`
They are wholesome only. They may be associated with pleasant feeling; they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They are things subject to result. They are not taken up at birth and not able to be clung to. They are undefiled and not connected with defilement. They may be with thought and with examination; they may be without thought but with examination only; they may be without thought and without examination. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be accompanied by happiness; they may be accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They are leading to dismantling. They belong to one in training. They are measureless. They have measureless objects. They are refined. They are fixed in rightness. They do not have the path as their object; they have the path as their cause; they do not have the path as their dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they are not describable as due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. They are not describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. They have external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.

### 670

**pi** `395749–397922`
Vīmaṃsiddhipādo hetu, tayo iddhipādā na hetū. Sahetukā. Hetusampayuttā. Vīmaṃsiddhipādo hetu ceva sahetuko ca, tayo iddhipādā na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Vīmaṃsiddhipādo hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, tayo iddhipādā na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Tayo iddhipādā na hetū sahetukā, vīmaṃsiddhipādo na vattabbo na hetu sahetukotipi, na hetu ahetukotipi. Sappaccayā. Saṅkhatā. Anidassanā. Appaṭighā. Arūpā. Lokuttarā. Kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā. No āsavā. Anāsavā. Āsavavippayuttā. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavā cātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā. Anāsavā. ⤵ No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā. Tayo iddhipādā no cittā, cittiddhipādo cittaṃ. Tayo iddhipādā cetasikā, cittiddhipādo acetasiko. Tayo iddhipādā cittasampayuttā, cittiddhipādo na vattabbo cittena sampayuttotipi, cittena vippayuttotipi. Tayo iddhipādā cittasaṃsaṭṭhā, cittiddhipādo na vattabbo cittena saṃsaṭṭhotipi, cittena visaṃsaṭṭhotipi. Tayo iddhipādā cittasamuṭṭhānā, cittiddhipādo no cittasamuṭṭhāno . Tayo iddhipādā cittasahabhuno, cittiddhipādo no cittasahabhū. Tayo iddhipādā cittānuparivattino , cittiddhipādo no cittānuparivatti. Tayo iddhipādā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā, cittiddhipādo no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhāno. Tayo iddhipādā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno, cittiddhipādo no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhū. Tayo iddhipādā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino, cittiddhipādo no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivatti. ⤵ Tayo iddhipādā bāhirā, cittiddhipādo ajjhattiko. No upādā. Anupādinnā. No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā . Siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Na kāmāvacarā . Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā. Apariyāpannā. Niyyānikā. Niyatā. Anuttarā. Araṇāti.

**en** `576299–580304`
The basis of success through investigation is a root; three bases of success are not roots. They have roots. They are associated with roots. The basis of success through investigation is both a root and has roots; three bases of success are not describable as being both roots and having roots; they have roots but are not roots. The basis of success through investigation is both a root and associated with roots; three bases of success are not describable as being both roots and associated with roots; they are associated with roots but are not roots. Three bases of success are not roots yet have roots; the basis of success through investigation is not describable either as being a non-root that has roots or as being a non-root without roots. They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. They are beyond the world. They can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another. They are not mental taints. They are without mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. They are not describable either as being mental taints and subject to mental taints, or as being subject to mental taints but not mental taints. They are not describable either as being mental taints and associated with mental taints, or as being associated with mental taints but not mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. They are without mental taints. ⤵ They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects. Three bases of success are not minds; the basis of success through mind is a mind. Three bases of success are mental factors; the basis of success through mind is not a mental factor. Three bases of success are associated with mind; the basis of success through mind is not describable either as associated with mind or as dissociated from mind. Three bases of success are conjoined with mind; the basis of success through mind is not describable either as conjoined with mind or as disjoined from mind. Three bases of success are originated by mind; the basis of success through mind is not originated by mind. Three bases of success arise together with mind; the basis of success through mind does not arise together with mind. Three bases of success follow along with mind; the basis of success through mind does not follow along with mind. Three bases of success are conjoined with and originated by mind; the basis of success through mind is not conjoined with and originated by mind. Three bases of success are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind; the basis of success through mind is not conjoined with, originated by, and arising together with mind. Three bases of success are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind; the basis of success through mind is not conjoined with, originated by, and following along with mind. ⤵ Three bases of success are external; the basis of success through mind is internal. They are not derived. They are not taken up at birth. They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing. Their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. They may be with thought; they may be without thought. They may be with examination; they may be without examination. They may be with joy; they may be without joy. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be not accompanied by joy. They may be accompanied by happiness; they may be not accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity; they may be not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. They are not included in any sphere. They are leading out. They are fixed. They are unsurpassed. They are free from conflict.

### 675

**pi** `398029–398193`
Satta bojjhaṅgā – satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

**en** `580495–580789`
There are seven awakening factors: the awakening factor of mindfulness, the awakening factor of investigation of things, the awakening factor of energy, the awakening factor of joy, the awakening factor of tranquillity, the awakening factor of concentration, the awakening factor of equanimity.

### 676

**pi** `398194–398995`
Tattha katamo satisambojjhaṅgo? Idha bhikkhu satimā hoti paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā hoti anussaritā – ayaṃ vuccati "satisambojjhaṅgo". ⤵ So tathā sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinati pavicarati parivīmaṃsamāpajjati – ayaṃ vuccati "dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo". ⤵ Tassa taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinato pavicarato parivīmaṃsamāpajjato āraddhaṃ hoti vīriyaṃ asallīnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "vīriyasambojjhaṅgo". ⤵ Āraddhavīriyassa uppajjati pīti nirāmisā – ayaṃ vuccati "pītisambojjhaṅgo". ⤵ Pītimanassa kāyopi passambhati, cittampi passambhati – ayaṃ vuccati "passaddhisambojjhaṅgo". ⤵ Passaddhakāyassa sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati – ayaṃ vuccati "samādhisambojjhaṅgo" . ⤵ So tathā samāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati "upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo".

**en** `580790–581938`
Therein, what is the awakening factor of mindfulness? Here a monk is mindful, endowed with the highest mindfulness and care; he remembers and recalls what was done long ago and said long ago — this is called "the awakening factor of mindfulness". ⤵ Dwelling thus mindful, he investigates that teaching with wisdom, examines it, and enters into a full inquiry of it — this is called "the awakening factor of investigation of things". ⤵ As he investigates that teaching with wisdom, examines it, and enters into a full inquiry of it, energy is initiated in him without slackening — this is called "the awakening factor of energy". ⤵ In one whose energy is initiated, unworldly joy arises — this is called "the awakening factor of joy". ⤵ In one whose mind is joyful, the body becomes tranquil and the mind becomes tranquil — this is called "the awakening factor of tranquillity". ⤵ In one whose body is tranquil and who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated — this is called "the awakening factor of concentration". ⤵ He is one who watches well over the mind thus concentrated, with equanimity — this is called "the awakening factor of equanimity".

### 677

### 678

**pi** `399161–401279`
Tattha katamo satisambojjhaṅgo? Atthi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu sati, atthi bahiddhā dhammesu sati. Yadapi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu sati tadapi satisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi bahiddhā dhammesu sati tadapi satisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. ⤵ Tattha katamo dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo? Atthi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu pavicayo, atthi bahiddhā dhammesu pavicayo. Yadapi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu pavicayo tadapi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi bahiddhā dhammesu pavicayo tadapi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. ⤵ Tattha katamo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo? Atthi kāyikaṃ vīriyaṃ, atthi cetasikaṃ vīriyaṃ. Yadapi kāyikaṃ vīriyaṃ tadapi vīriyasambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi cetasikaṃ vīriyaṃ tadapi vīriyasambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati . ⤵ Tattha katamo pītisambojjhaṅgo? Atthi savitakkasavicārā pīti, atthi avitakkaavicārā pīti. Yadapi savitakkasavicārā pīti tadapi pītisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi avitakkaavicārā pīti tadapi pītisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. ⤵ Tattha katamo passaddhisambojjhaṅgo? Atthi kāyapassaddhi [kāyappassaddhi (syā. ka.)], atthi cittapassaddhi [cittappassaddhi (syā. ka.)]. Yadapi kāyapassaddhi tadapi passaddhisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi cittapassaddhi tadapi passaddhisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. ⤵ Tattha katamo samādhisambojjhaṅgo? Atthi savitakko savicāro samādhi, atthi avitakko avicāro samādhi. Yadapi savitakko savicāro samādhi tadapi samādhisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi avitakko avicāro samādhi tadapi samādhisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. ⤵ Tattha katamo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo? Atthi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu upekkhā, atthi bahiddhā dhammesu upekkhā. Yadapi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu upekkhā tadapi upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi bahiddhā dhammesu upekkhā tadapi upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

**en** `582234–585316`
Therein, what is the awakening factor of mindfulness? There is mindfulness with regard to internal things; there is mindfulness with regard to external things. The mindfulness with regard to internal things is itself the awakening factor of mindfulness, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The mindfulness with regard to external things is itself the awakening factor of mindfulness, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of investigation of things? There is investigation of internal things; there is investigation of external things. The investigation of internal things is itself the awakening factor of investigation of things, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The investigation of external things is itself the awakening factor of investigation of things, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of energy? There is bodily energy; there is mental energy. The bodily energy is itself the awakening factor of energy, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The mental energy is itself the awakening factor of energy, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of joy? There is joy with thought and with examination; there is joy without thought and without examination. The joy with thought and with examination is itself the awakening factor of joy, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The joy without thought and without examination is itself the awakening factor of joy, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of tranquillity? There is tranquillity of the body; there is tranquillity of the mind. The tranquillity of the body is itself the awakening factor of tranquillity, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The tranquillity of the mind is itself the awakening factor of tranquillity, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of concentration? There is concentration with thought and with examination; there is concentration without thought and without examination. The concentration with thought and with examination is itself the awakening factor of concentration, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The concentration without thought and without examination is itself the awakening factor of concentration, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of equanimity? There is equanimity with regard to internal things; there is equanimity with regard to external things. The equanimity with regard to internal things is itself the awakening factor of equanimity, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The equanimity with regard to external things is itself the awakening factor of equanimity, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna.

### 680

**pi** `401445–401830`
Tattha katamo satisambojjhaṅgo? Idha bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ.

**en** `585612–586182`
Therein, what is the awakening factor of mindfulness? Here a monk develops the awakening factor of mindfulness, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, ripening in release; he develops the awakening factor of investigation of things… he develops the awakening factor of energy… he develops the awakening factor of joy… he develops the awakening factor of tranquillity… he develops the awakening factor of concentration… he develops the awakening factor of equanimity, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, ripening in release.

<h1>2. Classification According to the Abhidhamma</h1>

### 683

**pi** `401884–402048`
Satta bojjhaṅgā – satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

**en** `586298–586592`
There are seven awakening factors: the awakening factor of mindfulness, the awakening factor of investigation of things, the awakening factor of energy, the awakening factor of joy, the awakening factor of tranquillity, the awakening factor of concentration, the awakening factor of equanimity.

### 684

**pi** `402049–402374`
Tattha katame satta bojjhaṅgā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye satta bojjhaṅgā honti – satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

**en** `586593–587097`
Therein, what are the seven awakening factors? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge — on that occasion there are seven awakening factors: the awakening factor of mindfulness… the awakening factor of equanimity.

### 685

**pi** `402375–403701`
Tattha katamo satisambojjhaṅgo? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "satisambojjhaṅgo". ⤵ Tattha katamo dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo". ⤵ Tattha katamo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "vīriyasambojjhaṅgo". ⤵ Tattha katamo pītisambojjhaṅgo? Yā pīti pāmojjaṃ āmodanā pamodanā hāso pahāso vitti odagyaṃ [odaggaṃ (sī.) dha. sa. 9] attamanatā cittassa pītisambojjhaṅgo – ayaṃ vuccati "pītisambojjhaṅgo". ⤵ Tattha katamo passaddhisambojjhaṅgo? Yā vedanākkhandhassa saññākkhandhassa saṅkhārakkhandhassa viññāṇakkhandhassa passaddhi paṭippassaddhi passambhanā paṭippassambhanā paṭippassambhitattaṃ passaddhisambojjhaṅgo – ayaṃ vuccati "passaddhisambojjhaṅgo". ⤵ Tattha katamo samādhisambojjhaṅgo? Yā cittassa ṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "samādhisambojjhaṅgo". ⤵ Tattha katamo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo? Yā upekkhā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā majjhattatā cittassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ayaṃ vuccati "upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo". Ime vuccanti satta bojjhaṅgā. Avasesā dhammā sattahi bojjhaṅgehi sampayuttā.

**en** `587098–589031`
Therein, what is the awakening factor of mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness, the awakening factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "the awakening factor of mindfulness". ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of investigation of things? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view, the awakening factor of investigation of things, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "the awakening factor of investigation of things". ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of energy? The mental initiation of energy… right effort, the awakening factor of energy, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "the awakening factor of energy". ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of joy? The joy, gladness, rejoicing, delight, mirth, merriment, felicity, elation, satisfaction of the mind, the awakening factor of joy — this is called "the awakening factor of joy". ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of tranquillity? The tranquillity of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness, their calming down, becoming tranquil, calming, state of being calmed, the awakening factor of tranquillity — this is called "the awakening factor of tranquillity". ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of concentration? The steadiness of the mind… right concentration, the awakening factor of concentration, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "the awakening factor of concentration". ⤵ Therein, what is the awakening factor of equanimity? The equanimity, being equanimous, watching over with equanimity, neutrality of the mind, the awakening factor of equanimity — this is called "the awakening factor of equanimity". These are called the seven awakening factors. The remaining things are associated with the seven awakening factors.

### 698

**pi** `407768–408834`
Siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Pītisambojjhaṅgo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto; cha bojjhaṅgā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā. Anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Pītisambojjhaṅgo na pītisahagato, sukhasahagato, na upekkhāsahagato; cha bojjhaṅgā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā. Appamāṇā. Appamāṇārammaṇā. Paṇītā. Siyā sammattaniyatā , siyā aniyatā. Na maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino; siyā na vattabbā maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Bahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

**en** `595558–597438`
They may be wholesome; they may be neutral. The awakening factor of joy is associated with pleasant feeling; six awakening factors may be associated with pleasant feeling or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They may be results; they may be things subject to result. They are not taken up at birth and not able to be clung to. They are undefiled and not connected with defilement. They may be with thought and with examination; they may be without thought but with examination only; they may be without thought and without examination. The awakening factor of joy is not accompanied by joy, is accompanied by happiness, and is not accompanied by equanimity; six awakening factors may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by happiness, or may be accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They may be leading to dismantling; they may be leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling. They may belong to one in training; they may belong to one beyond training. They are measureless. They have measureless objects. They are refined. They may be fixed in rightness; they may be unfixed. They do not have the path as their object; they may have the path as their cause; they may have the path as their dominant factor; they may not be describable either as having the path as their cause or as having the path as their dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they may be due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. They are not describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. They have external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.

### 700

**pi** `408853–410613`
Dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo hetu, cha bojjhaṅgā hetusampayuttā. Dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo hetu ceva sahetuko ca, cha bojjhaṅgā na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, cha bojjhaṅgā na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Cha bojjhaṅgā na hetū sahetukā, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo na vattabbo na hetusahetukotipi, na hetuahetukotipi. Sappaccayā. Saṅkhatā. Anidassanā. Appaṭighā. Arūpā. Lokuttarā. Kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā. No āsavā. Anāsavā āsavavippayuttā. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavā cātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā. Anāsavā. No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā. No cittā. Cetasikā. Cittasampayuttā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhā . Cittasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasahabhuno. Cittānuparivattino. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Bāhirā. No upādā. Anupādinnā. No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. ⤵ Pītisambojjhaṅgo appītiko, cha bojjhaṅgā siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Pītisambojjhaṅgo na pītisahagato, cha bojjhaṅgā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Pītisambojjhaṅgo sukhasahagato, cha bojjhaṅgā siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Pītisambojjhaṅgo na upekkhāsahagato, cha bojjhaṅgā siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Na kāmāvacarā. Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā. Apariyāpannā. Siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā. Siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā. Anuttarā. Araṇāti.

**en** `597461–600684`
The awakening factor of investigation of things is a root; six awakening factors are associated with roots. The awakening factor of investigation of things is both a root and has roots; six awakening factors are not describable as being both roots and having roots; they have roots but are not roots. The awakening factor of investigation of things is both a root and associated with roots; six awakening factors are not describable as being both roots and associated with roots; they are associated with roots but are not roots. Six awakening factors are not roots yet have roots; the awakening factor of investigation of things is not describable either as being a non-root that has roots or as being a non-root without roots. They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. They are beyond the world. They can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another. They are not mental taints. They are without mental taints and dissociated from mental taints. They are not describable either as being mental taints and subject to mental taints, or as being subject to mental taints but not mental taints. Nor as being mental taints and associated with mental taints, or as being associated with mental taints but not mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. They are without mental taints. They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects. They are not minds. They are mental factors. They are associated with mind. They are conjoined with mind. They are originated by mind. They arise together with mind. They follow along with mind. They are conjoined with and originated by mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind. They are external. They are not derived. They are not taken up at birth. They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing. Their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. They may be with thought; they may be without thought. They may be with examination; they may be without examination. ⤵ The awakening factor of joy is without joy; six awakening factors may be with joy or may be without joy. The awakening factor of joy is not accompanied by joy; six awakening factors may be accompanied by joy or may be not accompanied by joy. The awakening factor of joy is accompanied by happiness; six awakening factors may be accompanied by happiness or may be not accompanied by happiness. The awakening factor of joy is not accompanied by equanimity; six awakening factors may be accompanied by equanimity or may be not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. They are not included in any sphere. They may be leading out; they may be not leading out. They may be fixed; they may be unfixed. They are unsurpassed. They are free from conflict.
