### 706

**pi** `410861–413217`
Tattha katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "sammādiṭṭhi". ⤵ Tattha katamo sammāsaṅkappo? Nekkhammasaṅkappo, abyāpādasaṅkappo, avihiṃsāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāsaṅkappo". ⤵ Tattha katamā sammāvācā? Musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāvācā". ⤵ Tattha katamo sammākammanto? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī – ayaṃ vuccati "sammākammanto". ⤵ Tattha katamo sammāājīvo? Idha ariyasāvako micchāājīvaṃ pahāya sammāājīvena jīvikaṃ kappeti – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāājīvo". ⤵ Tattha katamo sammāvāyāmo? Idha bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāvāyāmo". ⤵ Tattha katamā sammāsati? Idha bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāsati". ⤵ Tattha katamo sammāsamādhi? Idha bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti "upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī"ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāsamādhi".

**en** `601034–604478`
Therein, what is right view? Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of suffering — this is called "right view". ⤵ Therein, what is right intention? The intention of renunciation, the intention of non-ill-will, the intention of harmlessness — this is called "right intention". ⤵ Therein, what is right speech? Abstaining from false speech, abstaining from divisive speech, abstaining from harsh speech, abstaining from idle chatter — this is called "right speech". ⤵ Therein, what is right action? Abstaining from killing living beings, abstaining from taking what is not given, abstaining from sexual misconduct — this is called "right action". ⤵ Therein, what is right livelihood? Here a noble disciple, having abandoned wrong livelihood, makes his living by right livelihood — this is called "right livelihood". ⤵ Therein, what is right effort? Here a monk generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the abandoning of evil, unwholesome things that have arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the arising of wholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the persistence of wholesome things that have arisen, for their non-confusion, their increase, their expansion, their development, their perfection — this is called "right effort". ⤵ Therein, what is right mindfulness? Here a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world; he dwells contemplating feelings in feelings — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world; he dwells contemplating the mind in the mind — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world; he dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world — this is called "right mindfulness". ⤵ Therein, what is right concentration? Here a monk, secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome things, enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, which is with thought and with examination, with joy and happiness born of seclusion; with the stilling of thought and examination, he enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption, which has inner confidence and unification of mind, is without thought and without examination, with joy and happiness born of concentration; with the fading away of joy he dwells equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body — that of which the noble ones declare, "equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily" — he enters and dwells in the third meditative absorption; with the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain, and with the earlier disappearance of joy and grief, he enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption, which is neither painful nor pleasant and has purity of mindfulness through equanimity — this is called "right concentration".

### 713

**pi** `414213–415668`
Tattha katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "sammādiṭṭhi". ⤵ Tattha katamo sammāsaṅkappo? Yo takko vitakko saṅkappo appanā byappanā cetaso abhiniropanā sammāsaṅkappo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāsaṅkappo". ⤵ Tattha katamā sammāvācā? Yā catūhi vacīduccaritehi ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto sammāvācā maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāvācā". ⤵ Tattha katamo sammākammanto? Yā tīhi kāyaduccaritehi ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto sammākammanto maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "sammākammanto". ⤵ Tattha katamo sammāājīvo? Yā micchāājīvā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto sammāājīvo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāājīvo". ⤵ Tattha katamo sammāvāyāmo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāvāyāmo". ⤵ Tattha katamā sammāsati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāsati". ⤵ Tattha katamo sammāsamādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "sammāsamādhi". Ayaṃ vuccati "aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo". Avasesā dhammā aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena sampayuttā.

**en** `605782–607833`
Therein, what is right view? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view, the awakening factor of investigation of things, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right view". ⤵ Therein, what is right intention? The thinking, thought, intention, absorption, full absorption, application of the mind, right intention, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right intention". ⤵ Therein, what is right speech? The refraining from the four kinds of verbal misconduct, abstaining, desisting, abstinence, not doing, not committing, not transgressing, not overstepping the limit, destroying the bridge to them — right speech, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right speech". ⤵ Therein, what is right action? The refraining from the three kinds of bodily misconduct, abstaining, desisting, abstinence, not doing, not committing, not transgressing, not overstepping the limit, destroying the bridge to them — right action, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right action". ⤵ Therein, what is right livelihood? The refraining from wrong livelihood, abstaining, desisting, abstinence, not doing, not committing, not transgressing, not overstepping the limit, destroying the bridge to it — right livelihood, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right livelihood". ⤵ Therein, what is right effort? The mental initiation of energy… right effort, the awakening factor of energy, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right effort". ⤵ Therein, what is right mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness, the awakening factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right mindfulness". ⤵ Therein, what is right concentration? The steadiness of the mind… right concentration, the awakening factor of concentration, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right concentration". This is called "the eightfold path". The remaining things are associated with the eightfold path.

The remaining things are associated with right view… the remaining things are associated with right intention… the remaining things are associated with right effort… the remaining things are associated with right mindfulness. ⤵ Therein, what is right concentration? The remaining things are associated with right concentration.

Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge — on that occasion there is contact… there is non-distraction. These things are wholesome. When, because that same wholesome meditative absorption beyond the world has been done and developed, as its result — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge, on emptiness — the steadiness of the mind, its stability, its firm standing, its non-wavering, non-distraction, the state of an undistracted mind, calm, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration, awakening factor of concentration, path factor, included in the path, that there is on that occasion: this is called "right concentration". The remaining things are associated with right concentration.

### 730

**pi** `421299–422408`
Siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Sammāsaṅkappo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto; satta maggaṅgā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā , siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā. Anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Sammāsaṅkappo avitakkavicāramatto; satta maggaṅgā siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Sammāsaṅkappo pītisahagato, sukhasahagato, na upekkhāsahagato; satta maggaṅgā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā. Appamāṇā. Appamāṇārammaṇā. Paṇītā. Siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Na maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino; siyā na vattabbā maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Bahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

**en** `615895–617803`
They may be wholesome; they may be neutral. Right intention is associated with pleasant feeling; seven path factors may be associated with pleasant feeling or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They may be results; they may be things subject to result. They are not taken up at birth and not able to be clung to. They are undefiled and not connected with defilement. Right intention is without thought but with examination only; seven path factors may be with thought and with examination, may be without thought but with examination only, or may be without thought and without examination. Right intention is accompanied by joy and accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by equanimity; seven path factors may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by happiness, or may be accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They may be leading to dismantling; they may be leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling. They may belong to one in training; they may belong to one beyond training. They are measureless. They have measureless objects. They are refined. They may be fixed in rightness; they may be unfixed. They do not have the path as their object; they may have the path as their cause; they may have the path as their dominant factor; they may not be describable either as having the path as their cause or as having the path as their dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they may be due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. They are not describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. They have external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.

### 732

**pi** `422427–424248`
Sammādiṭṭhi hetu, satta maggaṅgā na hetū. Sahetukā. Hetusampayuttā. Sammādiṭṭhi hetu ceva sahetukā ca, satta maggaṅgā na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Sammādiṭṭhi hetu ceva hetusampayuttā ca, satta maggaṅgā na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Satta maggaṅgā na hetū sahetukā, sammādiṭṭhi na vattabbā na hetu sahetukātipi, na hetu ahetukātipi. ⤵ Sappaccayā . Saṅkhatā. Anidassanā. Appaṭighā. Arūpā. Lokuttarā. Kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā. ⤵ No āsavā. Anāsavā. Āsavavippayuttā. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavā cātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā. Anāsavā. ⤵ No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā. No cittā. Cetasikā. Cittasampayuttā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhā. Cittasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasahabhuno. Cittānuparivattino. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Bāhirā. No upādā. Anupādinnā. ⤵ No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Sammāsaṅkappo avitakko, satta maggaṅgā siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Sammāsaṅkappo savicāro, satta maggaṅgā siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Sammāsaṅkappo sappītiko , satta maggaṅgā siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Sammāsaṅkappo pītisahagato, satta maggaṅgā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Sammāsaṅkappo sukhasahagato, satta maggaṅgā siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Sammāsaṅkappo na upekkhāsahagato, satta maggaṅgā siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Na kāmāvacarā. Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā. Apariyāpannā. Siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā. Siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā. Anuttarā. Araṇāti.

**en** `617826–620994`
Right view is a root; seven path factors are not roots. They have roots. They are associated with roots. Right view is both a root and has roots; seven path factors are not describable as being both roots and having roots; they have roots but are not roots. Right view is both a root and associated with roots; seven path factors are not describable as being both roots and associated with roots; they are associated with roots but are not roots. Seven path factors are not roots yet have roots; right view is not describable either as being a non-root that has roots or as being a non-root without roots. ⤵ They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. They are beyond the world. They can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another. ⤵ They are not mental taints. They are without mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. They are not describable either as being mental taints and subject to mental taints, or as being subject to mental taints but not mental taints. They are not describable either as being mental taints and associated with mental taints, or as being associated with mental taints but not mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. They are without mental taints. ⤵ They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects. They are not minds. They are mental factors. They are associated with mind. They are conjoined with mind. They are originated by mind. They arise together with mind. They follow along with mind. They are conjoined with and originated by mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind. They are external. They are not derived. They are not taken up at birth. ⤵ They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing. Their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Right intention is without thought; seven path factors may be with thought or may be without thought. Right intention is with examination; seven path factors may be with examination or may be without examination. Right intention is with joy; seven path factors may be with joy or may be without joy. Right intention is accompanied by joy; seven path factors may be accompanied by joy or may be not accompanied by joy. Right intention is accompanied by happiness; seven path factors may be accompanied by happiness or may be not accompanied by happiness. Right intention is not accompanied by equanimity; seven path factors may be accompanied by equanimity or may be not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. They are not included in any sphere. They may be leading out; they may be not leading out. They may be fixed; they may be unfixed. They are unsurpassed. They are free from conflict.

### 737

**pi** `424350–426973`
Idha bhikkhu pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati, ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu indriyesu guttadvāro bhojane mattaññū pubbarattāpararattaṃ jāgariyānuyogamanuyutto sātaccaṃ nepakkaṃ bodhipakkhikānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanānuyogamanuyutto. So abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī hoti, samiñjite [sammiñjite (sī. syā.)] pasārite sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ appasaddaṃ appanigghosaṃ vijanavātaṃ manussarāhasseyyakaṃ [manussarāhaseyyakaṃ (sī. syā.)] paṭisallānasāruppaṃ. So araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So abhijjhaṃ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā viharati, abhijjhāya cittaṃ parisodheti. Byāpādapadosaṃ pahāya abyāpannacitto viharati sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī, byāpādapadosā cittaṃ parisodheti. Thinamiddhaṃ pahāya vigatathinamiddho viharati ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thinamiddhā cittaṃ parisodheti. Uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahāya anuddhato viharati ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto , uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṃ parisodheti. Vicikicchaṃ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho viharati akathaṃkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṃ parisodheti. So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – "upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī"ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā "ananto ākāso"ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati; sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma "anantaṃ viññāṇa"nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati; sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma "natthi kiñcī"ti ākiñcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati; sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati.

**en** `621181–625148`
Here a monk dwells restrained by the restraint of the monastic code, endowed with proper conduct and proper resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults; he trains himself, having undertaken the rules of training; he guards the doors of the faculties, knows moderation in food, and is devoted to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night, devoted with perseverance and care to the development of the things that side with awakening. He acts with clear comprehension when going forward and returning; he acts with clear comprehension when looking ahead and looking away; he acts with clear comprehension when bending and stretching; he acts with clear comprehension when carrying the outer robe, the bowl, and the robes; he acts with clear comprehension when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; he acts with clear comprehension when defecating and urinating; he acts with clear comprehension when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent. He resorts to a secluded dwelling place — a forest, the foot of a tree, a mountain, a glen, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a remote forest, the open air, a heap of straw — with little sound, little noise, without the breath of crowds, hidden from people, suitable for retreat. Gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, he sits down, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body straight, and established mindfulness in front of him. Having abandoned covetousness with regard to the world, he dwells with a mind free of covetousness; he purifies his mind of covetousness. Having abandoned ill will and hatred, he dwells with a mind free of ill will, compassionate for the welfare of all living beings; he purifies his mind of ill will and hatred. Having abandoned dullness and drowsiness, he dwells free of dullness and drowsiness, percipient of light, mindful and clearly comprehending; he purifies his mind of dullness and drowsiness. Having abandoned restlessness and remorse, he dwells unagitated, with a mind inwardly stilled; he purifies his mind of restlessness and remorse. Having abandoned doubt, he dwells having crossed over doubt, without perplexity about wholesome things; he purifies his mind of doubt. Having abandoned these five hindrances, corruptions of the mind that weaken wisdom — secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome things, he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, which is with thought and with examination, with joy and happiness born of seclusion; with the stilling of thought and examination, he enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption, which has inner confidence and unification of mind, is without thought and without examination, with joy and happiness born of concentration; with the fading away of joy he dwells equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body — that of which the noble ones declare, "equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily" — he enters and dwells in the third meditative absorption; with the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain, and with the earlier disappearance of joy and grief, he enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption, which is neither painful nor pleasant and has purity of mindfulness through equanimity; completely passing beyond perceptions of material form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, not attending to perceptions of diversity, aware that "space is infinite", he enters and dwells in the field of infinite space; completely passing beyond the field of infinite space, aware that "consciousness is infinite", he enters and dwells in the field of infinite consciousness; completely passing beyond the field of infinite consciousness, aware that "there is nothing", he enters and dwells in the field of nothingness; completely passing beyond the field of nothingness, he enters and dwells in the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Here someone, having seen a sight with the eye, does not grasp at its signs and does not grasp at its details. The guarding, protection, watching over, and restraint of these six faculties — this is called "guarding the doors of the faculties". "Knows moderation in food": there is knowing moderation in food, and there is not knowing moderation in food. ⤵ Therein, what is not knowing moderation in food? Here someone takes food without reflection and unwisely — for amusement, for intoxication, for adornment, for beautification. The lack of contentment there, the lack of moderation, the lack of reflection with regard to food — this is called "not knowing moderation in food". ⤵ Therein, what is knowing moderation in food? Here someone takes food with reflection and wisely — "not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for adornment, not for beautification, but only for the persistence and maintenance of this body, for ending discomfort, for supporting the holy life, thinking: thus I shall put an end to the old feeling and not give rise to a new feeling, and I shall keep going, be blameless, and dwell in comfort." The contentment there, the moderation, the reflection with regard to food — this is called "knowing moderation in food". He is endowed with this knowing of moderation in food… furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "knows moderation in food".

**en** `634128–634785`
And how is a monk devoted to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night? Here a monk during the day purifies his mind of obstructive things by walking and sitting; in the first watch of the night he purifies his mind of obstructive things by walking and sitting; in the middle watch of the night he lies down on his right side in the lion's posture, placing one foot on the other, mindful and clearly comprehending, having attended to the idea of rising; in the last watch of the night, having risen, he purifies his mind of obstructive things by walking and sitting. Thus a monk is devoted to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night.

**en** `635583–636822`
And how does a monk act with clear comprehension when going forward and returning, act with clear comprehension when looking ahead and looking away, act with clear comprehension when bending and stretching, act with clear comprehension when carrying the outer robe, the bowl, and the robes, act with clear comprehension when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting, act with clear comprehension when defecating and urinating, act with clear comprehension when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent? The aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness — this is called "the body". He experiences this happiness with this body. Therefore it is said, "and experiences happiness with the body".

### 818

**pi** `450326–450582`
"Yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhantī"ti tattha katame ariyā? Ariyā vuccanti buddhā ca buddhasāvakā ca. Te imaṃ ācikkhanti desenti paññapenti [paññāpenti (sī. syā.)] paṭṭhapenti vivaranti vibhajanti uttāniṃ karonti pakāsenti. Tena vuccati "yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhantī"ti.

**en** `657006–657317`
"That of which the noble ones declare": therein, who are the noble ones? The Buddhas and the Buddhas' disciples are called the noble ones. They declare this, teach it, make it known, establish it, disclose it, analyse it, make it plain, proclaim it. Therefore it is said, "that of which the noble ones declare".

### 819

**pi** `450583–451126`
"Upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī"ti tattha katamā upekkhā? Yā upekkhā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā majjhattatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati "upekkhā". ⤵ Tattha katamā sati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati – ayaṃ vuccati "sati". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ sukhaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "sukhaṃ". Iti imāya ca upekkhāya imāya ca satiyā iminā ca sukhena samannāgato iriyati vattati pāleti yapeti yāpeti carati viharati. Tena vuccati "upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī"ti.

**en** `657318–658057`
"Equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily": therein, what is equanimity? The equanimity, being equanimous, watching over with equanimity, neutrality of the mind — this is called "equanimity". ⤵ Therein, what is mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness — this is called "mindfulness". ⤵ Therein, what is happiness? Mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "happiness". So, furnished with this equanimity, this mindfulness, and this happiness, he moves, goes on, keeps going, maintains himself, carries on, conducts himself, dwells. Therefore it is said, "equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily".

**en** `658135–658241`

### 824

**pi** `451410–451993`
"Sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā"ti, atthi sukhaṃ, atthi dukkhaṃ. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ sukhaṃ? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ sātaṃ kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "sukhaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "dukkhaṃ". Iti idañca sukhaṃ idañca dukkhaṃ santā honti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati "sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā"ti.

**en** `658422–659185`
"With the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain": there is happiness, there is pain. ⤵ Therein, what is happiness? Bodily comfort, bodily happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of body-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of body-contact — this is called "happiness". ⤵ Therein, what is pain? Bodily discomfort, bodily pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of body-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of body-contact — this is called "pain". So this happiness and this pain are stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "with the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain".

### 825

**pi** `451994–452624`
"Pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā"ti atthi somanassaṃ, atthi domanassaṃ. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ somanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "somanassaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "domanassaṃ". Iti idañca somanassaṃ idañca domanassaṃ pubbeva santā honti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati "pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā"ti.

**en** `659186–659921`
"With the earlier disappearance of joy and grief": there is joy, there is grief. ⤵ Therein, what is joy? Mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "joy". ⤵ Therein, what is grief? Mental discomfort, mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "grief". So this joy and this grief are already earlier stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "with the earlier disappearance of joy and grief".

### 826

**pi** `452625–452793`
"Adukkhamasukha"nti yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā. Tena vuccati "adukkhamasukha"nti.

**en** `659922–660201`
"Neither painful nor pleasant": mental experience that is neither comfortable nor uncomfortable, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant experience born of mind-contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mind-contact. Therefore it is said, "neither painful nor pleasant".

### 827

**pi** `452794–453104`
"Upekkhāsatipārisuddhi"nti, tattha katamā upekkhā? Yā upekkhā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā majjhattatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati "upekkhā". ⤵ Tattha katamā sati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati – ayaṃ vuccati "sati". Ayaṃ sati imāya upekkhāya vivaṭā hoti parisuddhā pariyodātā. Tena vuccati "upekkhāsatipārisuddhi"nti.

**en** `660202–660642`
"Purity of mindfulness through equanimity": therein, what is equanimity? The equanimity, being equanimous, watching over with equanimity, neutrality of the mind — this is called "equanimity". ⤵ Therein, what is mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness — this is called "mindfulness". This mindfulness is opened up by this equanimity, purified, cleansed. Therefore it is said, "purity of mindfulness through equanimity".

### 828

"Enters": the gaining of the fourth meditative absorption, its obtaining, attainment, full attainment, touching, realisation, achievement.

### 832

**pi** `453377–453687`
"Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā"ti tattha katamā rūpasaññā? Rūpāvacarasamāpattiṃ samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa vā saññā sañjānanā sañjānitattaṃ – imā vuccanti "rūpasaññāyo". Imā rūpasaññāyo atikkanto hoti vītikkanto samatikkanto. Tena vuccati "sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā"ti.

**en** `660980–661515`
"Completely passing beyond perceptions of material form": therein, what are perceptions of material form? The perception, perceiving, state of having perceived of one who has attained a fine-material-sphere attainment, or of one who has been reborn there, or of one dwelling happily in this very life — these are called "perceptions of material form". He has passed beyond these perceptions of material form, transcended them, gone completely beyond them. Therefore it is said, "completely passing beyond perceptions of material form".

### 833

**pi** `453688–453981`

**en** `661516–661997`
"With the disappearance of perceptions of resistance": therein, what are perceptions of resistance? Perception of sights, perception of sounds… perception of tangible things — these are called perceptions of resistance. These perceptions of resistance are stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance".

### 834

**pi** `453982–454256`
"Nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā"ti tattha katamā nānattasaññā? Asamāpannassa manodhātu samaṅgissa vā manoviññāṇadhātu samaṅgissa vā saññā sañjānanā sañjānitattaṃ – imā vuccanti "nānattasaññāyo". Imā nānattasaññāyo na manasi karoti. Tena vuccati "nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā"ti.

**en** `661998–662412`
"Not attending to perceptions of diversity": therein, what are perceptions of diversity? The perception, perceiving, state of having perceived of one who has not attained, who possesses the mind element or possesses the mind-consciousness element — these are called "perceptions of diversity". He does not attend to these perceptions of diversity. Therefore it is said, "not attending to perceptions of diversity".

### 835

**pi** `454257–454493`
"Ananto ākāso"ti, tattha katamo ākāso? Yo ākāso ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaro vivaragataṃ asamphuṭṭhaṃ catūhi mahābhūtehi – ayaṃ vuccati "ākāso". Tasmiṃ ākāse cittaṃ ṭhapeti saṇṭhapeti anantaṃ pharati. Tena vuccati "ananto ākāso"ti.

**en** `662413–662744`
"Space is infinite": therein, what is space? The space, what belongs to space, the void, what belongs to the void, the gap, what belongs to the gap, untouched by the four great elements — this is called "space". He places his mind in that space, settles it there, pervades it as infinite. Therefore it is said, "space is infinite".

<h1>2. Classification According to the Abhidhamma</h1>

### 855

**pi** `456631–456660`
<h2>1. Rūpāvacarakusalaṃ</h2>

**en** `665790–665836`
<h2>1. The Fine-Material-Sphere Wholesome</h2>

### 856

**pi** `456661–456745`
Cattāri jhānāni – paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ, dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ.

**en** `665837–666009`
There are four meditative absorptions: the first meditative absorption, the second meditative absorption, the third meditative absorption, the fourth meditative absorption.

### 857

**pi** `456746–457951`
Tattha katamaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye pañcaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – vitakko, vicāro, pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati "paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ". Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ , tasmiṃ samaye tivaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati "dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ". Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati "tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ". Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati "catutthaṃ jhānaṃ". Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

**en** `666010–667977`
Therein, what is the first meditative absorption? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption on the earth device — on that occasion there is the five-factored meditative absorption: thought, examination, joy, happiness, one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the first meditative absorption". The remaining things are associated with the meditative absorption. ⤵ Therein, what is the second meditative absorption? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere — with the stilling of thought and examination… he enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption on the earth device — on that occasion there is the three-factored meditative absorption: joy, happiness, one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the second meditative absorption". The remaining things are associated with the meditative absorption. ⤵ Therein, what is the third meditative absorption? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere — with the fading away of joy… he enters and dwells in the third meditative absorption on the earth device — on that occasion there is the two-factored meditative absorption: happiness, one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the third meditative absorption". The remaining things are associated with the meditative absorption. ⤵ Therein, what is the fourth meditative absorption? Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ …pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati "pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ". Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

**en** `679843–681963`
Therein, what is the first meditative absorption? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge — on that occasion there is contact… there is non-distraction. These things are wholesome. When, because that same wholesome meditative absorption beyond the world has been done and developed, as its result — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge, on emptiness — on that occasion there is the five-factored meditative absorption: thought, examination, joy, happiness, one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the first meditative absorption". The remaining things are associated with the meditative absorption. ⤵ Therein, what is the second meditative absorption? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — with the stilling of thought and examination… he enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge — on that occasion there is contact… there is non-distraction. These things are wholesome. When, because that same wholesome meditative absorption beyond the world has been done and developed, as its result — with the stilling of thought and examination… the second meditative absorption… the third meditative absorption… the fourth meditative absorption… the first meditative absorption… he enters and dwells in the fifth meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge, on emptiness — on that occasion there is the two-factored meditative absorption: equanimity, one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fifth meditative absorption". The remaining things are associated with the meditative absorption.

**en** `682189–683545`
Therein, what is the first meditative absorption? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops a fine-material-sphere meditative absorption — functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not the result of action, a pleasant dwelling in this very life — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption on the earth device — on that occasion there is the five-factored meditative absorption: thought, examination, joy, happiness, one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fifth meditative absorption". The remaining things are associated with the meditative absorption.

### 883

**pi** `467980–468632`
Cattāri jhānāni – idha bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati…pe… vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati…pe… pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – "upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī"ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati…pe… sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.

**en** `684314–685346`
There are four meditative absorptions. Here a monk, secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome things, enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, which is with thought and with examination, with joy and happiness born of seclusion… with the stilling of thought and examination, he enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption, which has inner confidence and unification of mind, is without thought and without examination, with joy and happiness born of concentration… with the fading away of joy he dwells equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body — that of which the noble ones declare, "equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily" — he enters and dwells in the third meditative absorption… with the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain, and with the earlier disappearance of joy and grief, he enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption, which is neither painful nor pleasant and has purity of mindfulness through equanimity.

Siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Tīṇi jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ ṭhapetvā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ – etthuppannaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ ṭhapetvā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ. Siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ – etthuppanne vitakkavicāre ṭhapetvā savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ, tīṇi jhānāni avitakkaavicārā. Dve jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ pītiṃ ṭhapetvā pītisahagatā, tīṇi jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ sukhaṃ ṭhapetvā sukhasahagatā, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ – etthuppannaṃ upekkhaṃ ṭhapetvā upekkhāsahagataṃ. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā ācayagāmino, siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā, siyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Siyā mahaggatā, siyā appamāṇā. Tīṇi jhānāni na vattabbā parittārammaṇātipi, mahaggatārammaṇātipi, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā , siyā na vattabbā appamāṇārammaṇāti; catutthaṃ jhānaṃ siyā parittārammaṇaṃ, siyā mahaggatārammaṇaṃ, siyā appamāṇārammaṇaṃ; siyā na vattabbaṃ parittārammaṇantipi, mahaggatārammaṇantipi, appamāṇārammaṇantipi . Siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Tīṇi jhānāni na maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi; catutthaṃ jhānaṃ siyā maggārammaṇaṃ, siyā maggahetukaṃ, siyā maggādhipati, siyā na vattabbaṃ maggārammaṇantipi, maggahetukantipi maggādhipatītipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Tīṇi jhānāni na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi; catutthaṃ jhānaṃ siyā atītārammaṇaṃ, siyā anāgatārammaṇaṃ, siyā paccuppannārammaṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ atītārammaṇantipi, anāgatārammaṇantipi, paccuppannāramaṇantipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Tīṇi jhānāni bahiddhārammaṇā, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ siyā ajjhattārammaṇaṃ, siyā bahiddhārammaṇaṃ, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ ajjhattārammaṇantipi, bahiddhārammaṇantipi, ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇantipi. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

**en** `685530–689166`
They may be wholesome; they may be neutral. Three meditative absorptions — setting aside the pleasant feeling arisen in them — are associated with pleasant feeling; the fourth meditative absorption — setting aside the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arisen in it — is associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They may be results; they may be things subject to result; they may be neither results nor things subject to result. They may be taken up at birth and able to be clung to; they may be not taken up at birth but able to be clung to; they may be not taken up at birth and not able to be clung to. They may be undefiled but connected with defilement; they may be undefiled and not connected with defilement. The first meditative absorption — setting aside the thought and examination arisen in it — is with thought and with examination; three meditative absorptions are without thought and without examination. Two meditative absorptions — setting aside the joy arisen in them — are accompanied by joy; three meditative absorptions — setting aside the happiness arisen in them — are accompanied by happiness; the fourth meditative absorption — setting aside the equanimity arisen in it — is accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They may be leading to accumulation; they may be leading to dismantling; they may be leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling. They may belong to one in training; they may belong to one beyond training; they may belong to one neither in training nor beyond training. They may be expanded; they may be measureless. Three meditative absorptions are not describable either as having limited objects or as having expanded objects; they may have measureless objects, or they may not be describable as having measureless objects; the fourth meditative absorption may have a limited object, may have an expanded object, may have a measureless object, or may not be describable as having a limited object, an expanded object, or a measureless object. They may be middling; they may be refined. They may be fixed in rightness; they may be unfixed. Three meditative absorptions do not have the path as their object; they may have the path as their cause; they may have the path as their dominant factor; or they may not be describable either as having the path as their cause or as having the path as their dominant factor; the fourth meditative absorption may have the path as its object, may have the path as its cause, may have the path as its dominant factor, or may not be describable as having the path as its object, as its cause, or as its dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they may be due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. Three meditative absorptions are not describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object; the fourth meditative absorption may have a past object, may have a future object, may have a present object, or may not be describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. Three meditative absorptions have external objects; the fourth meditative absorption may have an internal object, may have an external object, may have both an internal and external object, or may not be describable as having an internal object, an external object, or both an internal and external object. They are invisible and offer no resistance.

Dve jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ pītiṃ ṭhapetvā sappītikā, dve jhānāni appītikā. Dve jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ pītiṃ ṭhapetvā pītisahagatā, dve jhānāni na pītisahagatā. Tīṇi jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ sukhaṃ ṭhapetvā sukhasahagatā, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ na sukhasahagataṃ. Catutthaṃ jhānaṃ – etthuppannaṃ upekkhaṃ ṭhapetvā upekkhāsahagataṃ, tīṇi jhānāni upekkhāsahagatā, na kāmāvacarā, siyā rūpāvacarā, siyā na rūpāvacarā, tīṇi jhānāni na arūpāvacarā, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ siyā arūpāvacaraṃ, siyā na arūpāvacaraṃ, siyā pariyāpannā, siyā apariyāpannā, siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā, siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā, siyā sauttarā, siyā anuttarā, araṇāti.

**en** `689189–692819`
They are not roots; they have roots; they are associated with roots; they are not describable as being "both roots and having roots"; they have roots but are not roots; they are not describable as being "both roots and associated with roots"; they are associated with roots but are not roots; they are not roots yet have roots. ⤵ They have conditions; they are conditioned; they are invisible; they offer no resistance; they are immaterial; they may be worldly; they may be beyond the world; they can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another. ⤵ They are not mental taints; they may be subject to mental taints; they may be without mental taints; they are dissociated from mental taints; they are not describable as being "both mental taints and subject to mental taints"; they may be subject to mental taints but not mental taints, or they may not be describable as being "subject to mental taints but not mental taints". They are not describable either as being "both mental taints and associated with mental taints", or as being "associated with mental taints but not mental taints". They may be dissociated from mental taints and subject to mental taints; they may be dissociated from mental taints and without mental taints. ⤵ They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects; they are not minds; they are mental factors; they are associated with mind; they are conjoined with mind; they are originated by mind; they arise together with mind; they follow along with mind; they are conjoined with and originated by mind; they are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind; they are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind; they are external; they are not derived; they may be taken up at birth; they may be not taken up at birth. ⤵ They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing; they are not to be abandoned by meditative development; their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing; their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. The first meditative absorption — setting aside the thought arisen in it — is with thought; three meditative absorptions are without thought. The first meditative absorption — setting aside the examination arisen in it — is with examination; three meditative absorptions are without examination. Two meditative absorptions — setting aside the joy arisen in them — are with joy; two meditative absorptions are without joy. Two meditative absorptions — setting aside the joy arisen in them — are accompanied by joy; two meditative absorptions are not accompanied by joy. Three meditative absorptions — setting aside the happiness arisen in them — are accompanied by happiness; the fourth meditative absorption is not accompanied by happiness. The fourth meditative absorption — setting aside the equanimity arisen in it — is accompanied by equanimity; three meditative absorptions are not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere; they may belong to the fine-material sphere, or they may not belong to the fine-material sphere; three meditative absorptions do not belong to the immaterial sphere; the fourth meditative absorption may belong to the immaterial sphere, or it may not belong to the immaterial sphere. They may be included in a sphere; they may be not included in any sphere. They may be leading out; they may be not leading out. They may be fixed; they may be unfixed. They may be surpassable; they may be unsurpassed. They are free from conflict.

Catasso appamaññāyo – idha bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ [catutthiṃ (sī.)]. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena [abyāpajjhena (sī. syā.)] pharitvā viharati. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ karuṇāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Muditāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ muditāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

**en** `693012–694455`
There are four measureless states. Here a monk dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. So above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. So above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by compassion — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. So above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. So above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will.

**en** `694456–694483`

### 895

**pi** `474126–474682`
Kathañca bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati? Seyyathāpi nāma ekaṃ puggalaṃ piyaṃ manāpaṃ disvā mettāyeyya, evameva sabbe satte mettāya pharati. ⤵ Tattha katamā mettā? Yā sattesu metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati "mettā". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati "cittaṃ". Idaṃ cittaṃ imāya mettāya sahagataṃ hoti sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ. Tena vuccati "mettāsahagatena cetasā"ti.

**en** `694484–695359`
And how does a monk dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness? Just as, on seeing one person who is dear and pleasing, he would feel loving-kindness, in the same way he pervades all beings with loving-kindness. ⤵ Therein, what is loving-kindness? The friendliness towards beings, being friendly, the state of friendliness, the liberation of mind through loving-kindness — this is called "loving-kindness". ⤵ Therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". This mind is accompanied by this loving-kindness, arisen together with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore it is said, "with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness".

When, because that same fine-material-sphere wholesome action has been done and accumulated, as its result — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption accompanied by compassion — the compassion, being compassionate, the state of compassion, the liberation of mind through compassion that there is on that occasion: this is called "compassion". The remaining things are associated with compassion. ⤵ Therein, what is compassion? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere — with the stilling of thought and examination… he enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption accompanied by compassion — on that occasion there is contact… there is non-distraction. These things are wholesome. When, because that same fine-material-sphere wholesome action has been done and accumulated, as its result — with the stilling of thought and examination… the second meditative absorption… the third meditative absorption… the first meditative absorption… the second meditative absorption… the third meditative absorption… he enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption accompanied by compassion — the compassion, being compassionate, the state of compassion, the liberation of mind through compassion that there is on that occasion: this is called "compassion". The remaining things are associated with compassion.

The remaining things are associated with loving-kindness. ⤵ Therein, what is loving-kindness? ### 958

**pi** `492178–493236`
Catasso appamaññāyo – idha bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ, iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati; karuṇāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ, iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ karuṇāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati; muditāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ, iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ muditāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati; upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ, iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

**en** `722812–724255`
There are four measureless states. Here a monk dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; so above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; so above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by compassion — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; so above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; so above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will.

### 961

**pi** `493347–494447`
Siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Tisso appamaññāyo sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, upekkhā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā; upekkhā avitakkaavicārā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, na upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na vattabbā pītisahagatāti; upekkhā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā ācayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino, nevasekkhanāsekkhā, mahaggatā, na vattabbā parittārammaṇātipi, mahaggatārammaṇātipi, appamāṇārammaṇātipi. Majjhimā, aniyatā, na vattabbā maggārammaṇātipi, maggahetukātipi , maggādhipatinotipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā, bahiddhārammaṇā, anidassanaappaṭighā.

**en** `724435–726307`
They may be wholesome; they may be neutral. Three measureless states are associated with pleasant feeling; equanimity is associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They may be results; they may be things subject to result; they may be neither results nor things subject to result. They may be taken up at birth and able to be clung to; they may be not taken up at birth but able to be clung to. They are undefiled but connected with defilement. Three measureless states may be with thought and with examination, may be without thought but with examination only, or may be without thought and without examination; equanimity is without thought and without examination. Three measureless states may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by happiness, are not accompanied by equanimity, or may not be describable as accompanied by joy; equanimity is accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They may be leading to accumulation; they may be leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling. They belong to one neither in training nor beyond training. They are expanded. They are not describable as having limited objects, expanded objects, or measureless objects. They are middling. They are unfixed. They are not describable as having the path as their object, as having the path as their cause, or as having the path as their dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they may be due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. They are not describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. They have external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.

**pi** `494448–494465`

**en** `726308–726329`

### 963

**pi** `494466–496166`
Mettā hetu, tisso appamaññāyo na hetū, sahetukā, hetusampayuttā. Mettā hetu ceva sahetukā ca; tisso appamaññāyo na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Mettā hetu ceva hetusampayuttā ca; tisso appamaññāyo na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Tisso appamaññāyo na hetū sahetukā; mettā na vattabbā na hetu sahetukātipi, na hetu ahetukātipi. ⤵ Sappaccayā, saṅkhatā, anidassanā, appaṭighā, arūpā, lokiyā, kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā, no āsavā, sāsavā, āsavavippayuttā , na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavā cāti, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā, na vattabbā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā sāsavā. ⤵ No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā …pe… sārammaṇā, no cittā, cetasikā, cittasampayuttā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhā, cittasamuṭṭhānā, cittasahabhuno, cittānuparivattino, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino, bāhirā, no upādā, siyā upādinnā, siyā anupādinnā. ⤵ No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbā, na dassanena pahātabbahetukā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā; upekkhā avitakkā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā; upekkhā avicārā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā; upekkhā appītikā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā; upekkhā na pītisahagatā. Tisso appamaññāyo sukhasahagatā, upekkhā na sukhasahagatā. Upekkhā upekkhāsahagatā, tisso appamaññāyo na upekkhāsahagatā, na kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, na arūpāvacarā, pariyāpannā, aniyyānikā, aniyatā, sauttarā, araṇāti.

**en** `726330–729432`
Loving-kindness is a root; three measureless states are not roots; they have roots; they are associated with roots. Loving-kindness is both a root and has roots; three measureless states are not describable as being both roots and having roots; they have roots but are not roots. Loving-kindness is both a root and associated with roots; three measureless states are not describable as being both roots and associated with roots; they are associated with roots but are not roots. Three measureless states are not roots yet have roots; loving-kindness is not describable either as being a non-root that has roots or as being a non-root without roots. ⤵ They have conditions; they are conditioned; they are invisible; they offer no resistance; they are immaterial; they are worldly; they can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another. They are not mental taints; they are subject to mental taints; they are dissociated from mental taints; they are not describable as being both mental taints and subject to mental taints; they are subject to mental taints but not mental taints; they are not describable either as being mental taints and associated with mental taints, or as being associated with mental taints but not mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints but subject to mental taints. ⤵ They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects; they are not minds; they are mental factors; they are associated with mind; they are conjoined with mind; they are originated by mind; they arise together with mind; they follow along with mind; they are conjoined with and originated by mind; they are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind; they are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind; they are external; they are not derived; they may be taken up at birth; they may be not taken up at birth. ⤵ They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing; they are not to be abandoned by meditative development; their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing; their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Three measureless states may be with thought or may be without thought; equanimity is without thought. Three measureless states may be with examination or may be without examination; equanimity is without examination. Three measureless states may be with joy or may be without joy; equanimity is without joy. Three measureless states may be accompanied by joy or may be not accompanied by joy; equanimity is not accompanied by joy. Three measureless states are accompanied by happiness; equanimity is not accompanied by happiness. Equanimity is accompanied by equanimity; three measureless states are not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere; they belong to the fine-material sphere; they do not belong to the immaterial sphere; they are included in a sphere; they are not leading out; they are unfixed; they are surpassable; they are free from conflict.

### 968

**pi** `496276–496482`
Pañca sikkhāpadāni – pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ.

**en** `729622–729975`
There are five training rules: the training rule of abstaining from killing living beings, the training rule of abstaining from taking what is not given, the training rule of abstaining from sexual misconduct, the training rule of abstaining from false speech, the training rule of abstaining from wine, spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness.

### 969

**pi** `496483–498059`
Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ pāṇātipātā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye pāṇātipātā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto – idaṃ vuccati "pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ". Avasesā dhammā veramaṇiyā sampayuttā. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacare kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ paṇītaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto – idaṃ vuccati "surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ". Avasesā dhammā veramaṇiyā sampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā cetanāya sampayuttā…pe… phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo – idaṃ vuccati "surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ".

**en** `743513–745149`
Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from wine, spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness? On the occasion when a wholesome mind of the sense sphere has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting — inferior… middling… refined… with desire as the dominant factor… with energy as the dominant factor… with mind as the dominant factor… with desire as the dominant factor, inferior… middling… refined… with energy as the dominant factor, inferior… middling… refined… with mind as the dominant factor, inferior… middling refined — in one abstaining from wine, spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness, the refraining from wine, spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness, abstaining, desisting, abstinence, not doing, not committing, not transgressing, not overstepping the limit, destroying the bridge to it, that there is on that occasion: this is called "the training rule of abstaining from wine, spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness". The remaining things are associated with the abstinence… the remaining things are associated with the intention… the contact… the exertion, non-distraction — this is called "the training rule of abstaining from wine, spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness".

### 977

**pi** `506237–506992`
Katame dhammā sikkhā? **en** `745150–746183`
Which things are training? On the occasion when a wholesome mind of the sense sphere has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, with a sight as its object… or a mental object as its object, or based on whatever it may be — on that occasion there is contact… there is non-distraction. These things are training. ⤵ Which things are training? On the occasion when a wholesome mind of the sense sphere has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting, with a sight as its object… or a mental object as its object, or based on whatever it may be — on that occasion there is contact… there is non-distraction. These things are training.

### 978

**pi** `506993–507348`
Katame dhammā sikkhā? Yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti…pe… arūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti…pe… lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā sikkhā.

**en** `746184–746735`
Which things are training? On the occasion when one develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere… develops the path for rebirth in the immaterial sphere… develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — secluded from sense pleasures… one enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge — on that occasion there is contact… there is non-distraction. These things are training.

Pañca sikkhāpadāni – pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ.
