### 984

**pi** `507717–508391`
Kusalāyeva. Siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, vipākadhammadhammā, anupādinnupādāniyā, asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, savitakkasavicārā, siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. ⤵ Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, ācayagāmino , nevasekkhanāsekkhā, parittā, parittārammaṇā, majjhimā, aniyatā, na vattabbā maggārammaṇātipi, maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā , na vattabbā uppādinoti, siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā, paccuppannārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā, bahiddhārammaṇā, anidassanaappaṭighā.

**en** `747374–748610`
They are wholesome only. They may be associated with pleasant feeling; they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They are things subject to result. They are not taken up at birth but able to be clung to. They are undefiled but connected with defilement. They are with thought and with examination. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be accompanied by happiness; they may be accompanied by equanimity. ⤵ They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They are leading to accumulation. They belong to one neither in training nor beyond training. They are limited. They have limited objects. They are middling. They are unfixed. They are not describable as having the path as their object, as having the path as their cause, or as having the path as their dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they are not describable as due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. They have present objects. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. They have external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.

### 986

**pi** `508410–509663`
Na hetū sahetukā, hetusampayuttā. Na vattabbā "hetū ceva sahetukā cā"ti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū, na vattabbā "hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cā"ti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū, na hetu sahetūkā, sappaccayā, saṅkhatā, anidassanā, appaṭighā, arūpā, lokiyā, kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā. ⤵ No āsavā, sāsavā, āsavavippayuttā, na vattabbā "āsavā ceva sāsavā cā"ti, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā, na vattabbā "āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cā"tipi, "āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā"tipi. Āsavavippayuttā sāsavā, no saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā, no cittā, cetasikā, cittasampayuttā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhā , cittasamuṭṭhānā, cittasahabhuno, cittānuparivattino, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino , bāhirā, no upādā, anupādinnā, no upādānā…pe… no kilesā. ⤵ Na dassanena pahātabbā, na bhāvanāyapahātabbā, na dassanena pahātabbahetukā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, savitakkā, savicārā, siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā, siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā, kāmāvacarā, na rūpāvacarā, na arūpāvacarā, pariyāpannā, aniyyānikā, aniyatā, sauttarā, araṇāti.

**en** `748633–751078`
They are not roots; they have roots; they are associated with roots. They are not describable as being "both roots and having roots"; they have roots but are not roots. They are not describable as being "both roots and associated with roots"; they are associated with roots but are not roots. They are not roots yet have roots. They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. They are worldly. They can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another. ⤵ They are not mental taints; they are subject to mental taints; they are dissociated from mental taints. They are not describable as being "both mental taints and subject to mental taints"; they are subject to mental taints but not mental taints. They are not describable either as being "mental taints and associated with mental taints", or as being "associated with mental taints but not mental taints". They are dissociated from mental taints but subject to mental taints. They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects. They are not minds. They are mental factors. They are associated with mind. They are conjoined with mind. They are originated by mind. They arise together with mind. They follow along with mind. They are conjoined with and originated by mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind. They are external. They are not derived. They are not taken up at birth. They are not clinging… they are not defilements. ⤵ They are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing. Their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. They are with thought. They are with examination. They may be with joy; they may be without joy. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be not accompanied by joy. They may be accompanied by happiness; they may be not accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity; they may be not accompanied by equanimity. They belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. They are included in a sphere. They are not leading out. They are unfixed. They are surpassable. They are free from conflict.

### 992

**pi** `509798–510118`
Catasso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā [paṭibhāṇapaṭisambhidā (syā.) evamuparipi]. Atthe ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā, dhamme ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Ayaṃ saṅgahavāro.

**en** `751303–751890`
There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. Knowledge with regard to meaning is the analytical knowledge of meaning; knowledge with regard to principles is the analytical knowledge of principles; knowledge with regard to the expression of the language of those principles is the analytical knowledge of language; knowledge with regard to knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. This is the summary section.

Catasso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Ye dhammā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā, imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā; yamhā dhammā te dhammā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā, tesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā; tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā; ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. This is the things section.

### 1003

**pi** `512287–512831`
Catasso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. ⤵ Tattha katamā dhammapaṭisambhidā? Idha bhikkhu dhammaṃ jānāti – suttaṃ geyyaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ gāthaṃ udānaṃ itivuttakaṃ jātakaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ vedallaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati "dhammapaṭisambhidā". So tassa tasseva bhāsitassa atthaṃ jānāti – "ayaṃ imassa bhāsitassa attho, ayaṃ imassa bhāsitassa attho"ti. Ayaṃ vuccati "atthapaṭisambhidā". Tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Ayaṃ pariyattivāro.

**en** `755983–756957`
There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. ⤵ Therein, what is the analytical knowledge of principles? Here a monk knows the teaching — the discourses, the mixed prose-and-verse, the expositions, the verses, the inspired utterances, the "thus it was said" texts, the birth stories, the marvellous accounts, the question-and-answer texts. This is called "the analytical knowledge of principles". He knows the meaning of each thing that has been spoken — "this is the meaning of this saying, this is the meaning of this saying". This is called "the analytical knowledge of meaning". Knowledge with regard to the expression of the language of those principles is the analytical knowledge of language. Knowledge with regard to knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. This is the scripture section.

There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. ⤵ Which things are wholesome? These things are wholesome. Knowledge with regard to these things is the analytical knowledge of principles. Knowledge of their result is the analytical knowledge of meaning. The language by which those things are made known — knowledge with regard to the expression of the language of those principles is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges — "these knowledges illuminate this meaning" — knowledge with regard to knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding.

Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – "imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī"ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

**en** `781676–783232`
There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. ⤵ Which things are neutral? On the occasion when the mind-consciousness element has arisen — functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not the result of action — accompanied by joy, with a sight as its object… or a mental object as its object… the mind-consciousness element has arisen — functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not the result of action — accompanied by equanimity, with a sight as its object… or a mental object as its object, or based on whatever it may be — on that occasion there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is intention, there is mind, there is thought, there is examination, there is equanimity, there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the energy faculty, there is the concentration faculty, there is the mind faculty, there is the equanimity faculty, there is the life faculty; and whatever other immaterial, dependently arisen things there are on that occasion. These things are neutral. Knowledge with regard to these things is the analytical knowledge of meaning. The language by which those things are made known — knowledge with regard to the expression of the language of those principles is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges — "these knowledges illuminate this meaning" — knowledge with regard to knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding.

Yasmiṃ samaye manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… rūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti…pe… arūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti kiriyaṃ neva kusalaṃ nākusalaṃ na ca kammavipākaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ…pe… sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – "imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī"ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

**en** `783233–785019`
There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. ⤵ Which things are neutral? On the occasion when the mind-consciousness element has arisen — functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not the result of action — accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge… accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting… one develops a fine-material-sphere meditative absorption… one develops an immaterial-sphere meditative absorption — functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not the result of action, a pleasant dwelling in this very life… completely passing beyond the field of nothingness, accompanied by the perception of the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, with the abandoning of happiness… one enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption — on that occasion there is contact… there is non-distraction. These things are neutral. Knowledge with regard to these things is the analytical knowledge of meaning. The language by which those things are made known — knowledge with regard to the expression of the language of those principles is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges — "these knowledges illuminate this meaning" — knowledge with regard to knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding.

### 1031

**pi** `530585–530908`
Catasso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Tisso paṭisambhidā kāmāvacarakusalato catūsu ñāṇasampayuttesu cittuppādesu, kiriyato catūsu ñāṇasampayuttesu cittuppādesu uppajjanti. Atthapaṭisambhidā etesu ceva uppajjati, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu ca uppajjati.

**en** `785020–785547`
There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. Three analytical knowledges arise in the four arisings of mind associated with knowledge on the wholesome sense-sphere side, and in the four arisings of mind associated with knowledge on the functional side. The analytical knowledge of meaning arises in these too, and it also arises in the four paths and in the four fruits.

Siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Tisso paṭisambhidā siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Tisso paṭisambhidā anupādinnupādāniyā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Tisso paṭisambhidā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. ⤵ Tisso paṭisambhidā savitakkasavicārā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Tisso paṭisambhidā parittā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā parittā, siyā appamāṇā. Niruttipaṭisambhidā parittārammaṇā; tisso paṭisambhidā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā. ⤵ Tisso paṭisambhidā majjhimā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Tisso paṭisambhidā aniyatā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Niruttipaṭisambhidā na vattabbā – maggārammaṇātipi, maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinītipi; atthapaṭisambhidā na maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatinī, siyā na vattabbā maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinītipi; dve paṭisambhidā siyā maggārammaṇā, na maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggārammaṇātipi, maggādhipatinotipi. ⤵ Tisso paṭisambhidā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā uppādinoti; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādinī. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Niruttipaṭisambhidā bahiddhārammaṇā; tisso paṭisambhidā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaapaṭighā.

They may be wholesome; they may be neutral. They may be associated with pleasant feeling; they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Three analytical knowledges may be things subject to result, or may be neither results nor things subject to result; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be a result, may be a thing subject to result, or may be neither a result nor a thing subject to result. Three analytical knowledges are not taken up at birth but able to be clung to; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be not taken up at birth but able to be clung to, or may be not taken up at birth and not able to be clung to. Three analytical knowledges are undefiled but connected with defilement; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be undefiled but connected with defilement, or may be undefiled and not connected with defilement. ⤵ Three analytical knowledges are with thought and with examination; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be with thought and with examination, may be without thought but with examination only, or may be without thought and without examination. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be accompanied by happiness; they may be accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. ⤵ Three analytical knowledges may be leading to accumulation, or may be leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be leading to accumulation, may be leading to dismantling, or may be leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling. ⤵ Three analytical knowledges belong to one neither in training nor beyond training; the analytical knowledge of meaning may belong to one in training, may belong to one beyond training, or may belong to one neither in training nor beyond training. Three analytical knowledges are limited; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be limited, or may be measureless. The analytical knowledge of language has a limited object; three analytical knowledges may have limited objects, may have expanded objects, or may have measureless objects. ⤵ Three analytical knowledges are middling; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be middling, or may be refined. Three analytical knowledges are unfixed; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be fixed in rightness, or may be unfixed. The analytical knowledge of language is not describable as having the path as its object, as having the path as its cause, or as having the path as its dominant factor; the analytical knowledge of meaning does not have the path as its object, may have the path as its cause, may have the path as its dominant factor, or may not be describable either as having the path as its cause or as having the path as its dominant factor; two analytical knowledges may have the path as their object, do not have the path as their cause, may have the path as their dominant factor, or may not be describable either as having the path as their object or as having the path as their dominant factor. ⤵ Three analytical knowledges may be arisen, or may be not arisen; they are not describable as due to arise; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be arisen, may be not arisen, or may be due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. The analytical knowledge of language has a present object; two analytical knowledges may have a past object, may have a future object, or may have a present object; the analytical knowledge of meaning may have a past object, may have a future object, may have a present object, or may not be describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. The analytical knowledge of language has an external object; three analytical knowledges may have internal objects, may have external objects, or may have both internal and external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.

Hetū, sahetukā, hetusampayuttā, hetū ceva sahetukā ca, hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca, na vattabbā na hetū sahetukātipi, nahetūahetukātipi. ⤵ Sappaccayā , saṅkhatā, anidassanā, appaṭighā, arūpā, tisso paṭisambhidā lokiyā, atthapaṭisambhidā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā, kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā. ⤵ No āsavā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Tisso paṭisambhidā savitakkā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Tisso paṭisambhidā savicārā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Tisso paṭisambhidā kāmāvacarā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā kāmāvacarā, siyā na kāmāvacarā. Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā . Tisso paṭisambhidā pariyāpannā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā pariyāpannā, siyā apariyāpannā. Tisso paṭisambhidā aniyyānikā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā. Tisso paṭisambhidā aniyatā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā niyatā , siyā aniyatā. Tisso paṭisambhidā sauttarā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā sauttarā , siyā anuttarā. Araṇāti.

**en** `790132–793983`
They are roots. They have roots. They are associated with roots. They are both roots and have roots. They are both roots and associated with roots. They are not describable either as being non-roots that have roots or as being non-roots without roots. ⤵ They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. Three analytical knowledges are worldly; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. They can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another. ⤵ They are not mental taints. Three analytical knowledges are subject to mental taints; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be subject to mental taints, or may be without mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. Three analytical knowledges are not describable as being both mental taints and subject to mental taints; they are subject to mental taints but not mental taints. The analytical knowledge of meaning is not describable as being both a mental taint and subject to mental taints; it may be subject to mental taints but not a mental taint, or it may not be describable as being subject to mental taints but not a mental taint. They are not describable either as being mental taints and associated with mental taints, or as being associated with mental taints but not mental taints. Three analytical knowledges are dissociated from mental taints but subject to mental taints; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be dissociated from mental taints and subject to mental taints, or may be dissociated from mental taints and without mental taints. ⤵ They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects. They are not minds. They are mental factors. They are associated with mind. They are conjoined with mind. They are originated by mind. They arise together with mind. They follow along with mind. They are conjoined with and originated by mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind. They are external. They are not derived. They are not taken up at birth. ⤵ They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing. Their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Three analytical knowledges are with thought; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be with thought, or may be without thought. Three analytical knowledges are with examination; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be with examination, or may be without examination. They may be with joy; they may be without joy. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be not accompanied by joy. They may be accompanied by happiness; they may be not accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity; they may be not accompanied by equanimity. Three analytical knowledges belong to the sense sphere; the analytical knowledge of meaning may belong to the sense sphere, or may not belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. Three analytical knowledges are included in a sphere; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be included in a sphere, or may be not included in any sphere. Three analytical knowledges are not leading out; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be leading out, or may be not leading out. Three analytical knowledges are unfixed; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be fixed, or may be unfixed. Three analytical knowledges are surpassable; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be surpassable, or may be unsurpassed. They are free from conflict.

Dasavidhena ñāṇavatthu – dasa tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. Katamāni dasa? ⤵ (1) Idha tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti . ⤵ (2) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. ⤵ (3) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. ⤵ (4) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato anekadhātu nānādhātulokaṃ [anekadhātuṃ nānādhātuṃ lokaṃ (syā.) ma. ni. 1.148] yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato anekadhātu nānādhātulokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. ⤵ (5) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. ⤵ (6) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti , idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. ⤵ (7) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. ⤵ (8) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato pubbenivāsānussatiṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato pubbenivāsānussatiṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. ⤵ (9) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato sattānaṃ cutūpapātaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Imāni dasa tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni, yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

The ground of knowledge by way of ten: the ten Tathāgata-powers of the Tathāgata, endowed with which the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. Which ten? ⤵ (1) Here the Tathāgata knows as it really is the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. ⤵ (2) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the result of past, future, and present undertakings of action, according to circumstance and according to cause. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the result of past, future, and present undertakings of action, according to circumstance and according to cause — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. ⤵ (3) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the way that leads everywhere. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the way that leads everywhere — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. ⤵ (4) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the world with its many and different elements. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the world with its many and different elements — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. ⤵ (5) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the different inclinations of beings. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the different inclinations of beings — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. ⤵ (6) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the higher and lower state of the faculties of other beings, of other persons. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the higher and lower state of the faculties of other beings, of other persons — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. ⤵ (7) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the defilement, the cleansing, and the emergence in the meditative absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the defilement, the cleansing, and the emergence in the meditative absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. ⤵ (8) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the recollection of past lives. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the recollection of past lives — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. ⤵ (9) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the passing away and rebirth of beings. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the passing away and rebirth of beings — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. ⤵ (10) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the destruction of the mental taints. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the destruction of the mental taints — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. These are the ten Tathāgata-powers of the Tathāgata, endowed with which the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā.

"The five kinds of consciousness have arisen bases and arisen objects": they arise when the basis has arisen and the object has arisen. ⤵ "They have bases arisen before them and objects arisen before them": they arise when the basis has arisen before and the object has arisen before. ⤵ "They have internal bases and external objects": the bases of the five kinds of consciousness are internal; their objects are external. ⤵ "They have unbroken bases and unbroken objects": they arise when the basis is unbroken and the object is unbroken. ⤵ "They have different bases and different objects": the basis and object of eye-consciousness are one thing; the basis and object of ear-consciousness are another; the basis and object of nose-consciousness are another; the basis and object of tongue-consciousness are another; the basis and object of body-consciousness are another.

wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be swept by floods. ⤵ (10) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from floods but able to be swept by them; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from floods and not able to be swept by them. ⤵ (11) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom that can be bound by yokes; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be bound by yokes. ⤵ (12) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from yokes but able to be bound by them; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from yokes and not able to be bound by them. ⤵ (13) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom that can be obstructed by hindrances; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be obstructed by hindrances. ⤵ (14) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from hindrances but able to be obstructed by them; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from hindrances and not able to be obstructed by them. ⤵ (15) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom that can be wrongly grasped; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be wrongly grasped. ⤵ (16) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from wrong grasping but able to be wrongly grasped; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from wrong grasping and not able to be wrongly grasped. ⤵ (17) Wisdom in the results of the three planes is wisdom taken up at birth; wisdom in the wholesome of the three planes, in the functional neutral of the three planes, and in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom not taken up at birth. ⤵ (18) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom that can be clung to; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be clung to. ⤵ (19) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from clinging but able to be clung to; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from clinging and not able to be clung to. ⤵ (20) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom connected with defilement; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom not connected with defilement. ⤵ (21) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from defilements but connected with defilement; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from defilements and not connected with defilement. ⤵ (22) Wisdom associated with thought is wisdom with thought; wisdom dissociated from thought is wisdom without thought. ⤵ (23) Wisdom associated with examination is wisdom with examination; wisdom dissociated from examination is wisdom without examination. ⤵ (24) Wisdom associated with joy is wisdom with joy; wisdom dissociated from joy is wisdom without joy. ⤵ (25) Wisdom associated with joy is wisdom accompanied by joy; wisdom dissociated from joy is wisdom not accompanied by joy. ⤵ (26) Wisdom associated with happiness is wisdom accompanied by happiness; wisdom dissociated from happiness is wisdom not accompanied by happiness. ⤵ (27) Wisdom associated with equanimity is wisdom accompanied by equanimity; wisdom dissociated from equanimity is wisdom not accompanied by equanimity. ⤵ (28) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the sense sphere is wisdom of the sense sphere; wisdom of the fine-material sphere, wisdom of the immaterial sphere, and wisdom not included in any sphere are wisdom not of the sense sphere. ⤵ (29) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the fine-material sphere is wisdom of the fine-material sphere; wisdom of the sense sphere, wisdom of the immaterial sphere, and wisdom not included in any sphere are wisdom not of the fine-material sphere. ⤵ (30) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the immaterial sphere is wisdom of the immaterial sphere; wisdom of the sense sphere, wisdom of the fine-material sphere, and wisdom not included in any sphere are wisdom not of the immaterial sphere. ⤵ (31) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom included in a sphere; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom not included in any sphere. ⤵ (32) Wisdom in the four paths is wisdom that leads out; wisdom in the wholesome of the three planes, in the results of the four planes, and in the functional neutral of the three planes is wisdom that does not lead out. ⤵ (33) Wisdom in the four paths is fixed wisdom; wisdom in the wholesome of the three planes, in the results of the four planes, and in the functional neutral of the three planes is unfixed wisdom. ⤵ (34) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is surpassable wisdom; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is unsurpassed wisdom. ⤵ (35) Therein, what is wisdom that brings about a goal? ⤵ Wisdom in the wholesome of the four planes, and in the functional neutral of an arahant producing a direct knowledge or producing an attainment, is wisdom that brings about a goal; wisdom in the results of the four planes, and in the functional neutral of an arahant when the direct knowledge has been produced and the attainment has been produced, is wisdom whose goal has been brought about.

### 1082

**pi** `561175–561981`
(1. Ka) tattha katamā cintāmayā paññā? ⤵ Yogavihitesu vā kammāyatanesu yogavihitesu vā sippāyatanesu yogavihitesu vā vijjāṭṭhānesu kammassakataṃ vā saccānulomikaṃ vā rūpaṃ aniccanti vā vedanā…pe… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ aniccanti vā, yaṃ evarūpiṃ anulomikaṃ khantiṃ diṭṭhiṃ ruciṃ mudiṃ pekkhaṃ dhammanijjhānakkhantiṃ parato assutvā paṭilabhati – ayaṃ vuccati "cintāmayā paññā". ⤵ (Kha) tattha katamā sutamayā paññā? Yogavihitesu vā kammāyatanesu yogavihitesu vā sippāyatanesu yogavihitesu vā vijjāṭṭhānesu kammassakataṃ vā saccānulomikaṃ vā rūpaṃ aniccanti vā vedanā…pe… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ aniccanti vā, yaṃ evarūpiṃ anulomikaṃ khantiṃ diṭṭhiṃ ruciṃ mudiṃ pekkhaṃ dhammanijjhānakkhantiṃ parato sutvā paṭilabhati – ayaṃ vuccati "sutamayā paññā". ⤵ (Ga) sabbāpi samāpannassa paññā bhāvanāmayā paññā.

**en** `832473–833724`
(1a) Therein, what is wisdom made of reflection? ⤵ In the fields of work arranged with skill, or the fields of craft arranged with skill, or the branches of science arranged with skill, whether concerning ownership of action or in conformity with the truths — "material form is impermanent", or "feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is impermanent" — whatever conforming acceptance, view, preference, understanding, consideration, acceptance upon reflection on things of such a kind one obtains without hearing it from another: this is called "wisdom made of reflection". ⤵ (1b) Therein, what is wisdom made of learning? In the fields of work arranged with skill, or the fields of craft arranged with skill, or the branches of science arranged with skill, whether concerning ownership of action or in conformity with the truths — "material form is impermanent", or "feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is impermanent" — whatever conforming acceptance, view, preference, understanding, consideration, acceptance upon reflection on things of such a kind one obtains by hearing it from another: this is called "wisdom made of learning". ⤵ (1c) All wisdom of one who has entered an attainment is wisdom made of meditative development.

### 1083

(2a) Therein, what is wisdom made of giving? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning giving, in relation to giving: this is called "wisdom made of giving". ⤵ (2b) Therein, what is wisdom made of virtue? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning virtue, in relation to virtue: this is called "wisdom made of virtue". ⤵ (2c) All wisdom of one who has entered an attainment is wisdom made of meditative development.

Wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits: this is called "wisdom concerning higher wisdom".

Ime vā panime dhamme manasikaroto anuppannā ceva akusalā dhammā uppajjanti, uppannā ca akusalā dhammā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattantī"ti – yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati "apāyakosallaṃ". ⤵ (Ga) sabbāpi tatrupāyā paññā upāyakosallaṃ.

**en** `834943–835904`
(4a) Therein, what is skill in gain? "When attending to these things, unwholesome things not yet arisen do not arise, and unwholesome things that have arisen are abandoned. Or, when attending to these things, wholesome things not yet arisen arise, and wholesome things that have arisen lead to increase, expansion, development, and perfection" — the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein: this is called "skill in gain". ⤵ (4b) Therein, what is skill in loss? "When attending to these things, wholesome things not yet arisen do not arise, and wholesome things that have arisen cease. Or, when attending to these things, unwholesome things not yet arisen arise, and unwholesome things that have arisen lead to increase and expansion" — the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein: this is called "skill in loss". ⤵ (4c) All wisdom about the means in each case is skill in means.

### 1110

(1. Ka) tattha katamaṃ kammassakatañāṇaṃ? **en** `841170–842493`
(1a) Therein, what is knowledge that action is one's own? "There is what is given, there is what is offered, there is what is sacrificed; there is the fruit and result of well-done and badly-done actions; there is this world, there is the other world; there is mother, there is father; there are spontaneously reborn beings; there are in the world ascetics and brahmins of right conduct and right practice who declare this world and the other world, having realised them for themselves by direct knowledge" — the wisdom of such a kind, the understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view: this is called "knowledge that action is one's own". Setting aside knowledge in conformity with the truths, all wholesome wisdom that is subject to mental taints is knowledge that action is one's own. ⤵ (1b) Therein, what is knowledge in conformity with the truths? "Material form is impermanent", or "feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is impermanent" — whatever conforming acceptance, view, preference, understanding, consideration, acceptance upon reflection on things of such a kind: this is called "knowledge in conformity with the truths". ⤵ (1c) Wisdom in the four paths is the knowledge of one endowed with the path. ⤵ (1d) Wisdom in the four fruits is the knowledge of one endowed with the fruit.

(4a) Therein, what is knowledge of the teaching? Wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is knowledge of the teaching. ⤵ (4b) By this teaching that is known, seen, reached, understood, and fathomed, he draws the inference concerning past and future: "Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past directly knew suffering, directly knew the origin of suffering, directly knew the cessation of suffering, directly knew the way leading to the cessation of suffering, it was just this suffering they directly knew, just this origin of suffering they directly knew, just this cessation of suffering they directly knew, just this way leading to the cessation of suffering they directly knew. Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the future will directly know suffering, will directly know the origin of suffering, will directly know the cessation of suffering, will directly know the way leading to the cessation of suffering, it is just this suffering they will directly know, just this origin of suffering they will directly know, just this cessation of suffering they will directly know, just this way leading to the cessation of suffering they will directly know" — the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein: this is called "inferential knowledge". ⤵ (4c) Therein, what is knowledge of encompassing others' minds? Here a monk knows the minds of other beings, of other persons, having encompassed them with his own mind. He knows a mind with lust as "a mind with lust"; he knows a mind without lust as "a mind without lust"; he knows a mind with hate as "a mind with hate"; he knows a mind without hate as "a mind without hate"; he knows a mind with delusion as "a mind with delusion"; he knows a mind without delusion as "a mind without delusion"; he knows a contracted mind as "a contracted mind"; he knows a distracted mind as "a distracted mind"; he knows an expanded mind as "an expanded mind"; he knows an unexpanded mind as "an unexpanded mind"; he knows a surpassable mind as "a surpassable mind"; he knows an unsurpassable mind as "an unsurpassable mind"; he knows a concentrated mind as "a concentrated mind"; he knows an unconcentrated mind as "an unconcentrated mind"; he knows a freed mind as "a freed mind"; he knows an unfreed mind as "an unfreed mind" — the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein: this is called "knowledge of encompassing others' minds". ⤵ (4d) Setting aside knowledge of the teaching, inferential knowledge, and knowledge of encompassing others' minds, the remaining wisdom is conventional knowledge.

**en** `846207–846641`
(5a) Therein, what is wisdom for accumulation and not for dismantling? Wisdom in the wholesome of the sense sphere is for accumulation and not for dismantling. ⤵ (5b) Wisdom in the four paths is for dismantling and not for accumulation. ⤵ (5c) Wisdom in the wholesome of the fine-material and immaterial spheres is both for accumulation and for dismantling. ⤵ (5d) The remaining wisdom is neither for accumulation nor for dismantling.

Yāya paññāya kāmesu vītarāgo hoti, na ca abhiññāyo paṭivijjhati na ca saccāni – ayaṃ vuccati "paññā nibbidāya no paṭivedhāya". ⤵ (Kha) sveva paññāya kāmesu vītarāgo samāno abhiññāyo paṭivijjhati na ca saccāni – ayaṃ vuccati "paññā paṭivedhāya no nibbidāya". ⤵ (Ga) catūsu maggesu paññā nibbidāya ceva paṭivedhāya ca. ⤵ (Gha) avasesā paññā neva nibbidāya no paṭivedhāya.

(6a) Therein, what is wisdom for disenchantment and not for penetration? The wisdom by which one becomes dispassionate towards sense pleasures, but does not penetrate the direct knowledges or the truths: this is called "wisdom for disenchantment and not for penetration". ⤵ (6b) Being already dispassionate towards sense pleasures by that wisdom, one penetrates the direct knowledges but not the truths: this is called "wisdom for penetration and not for disenchantment". ⤵ (6c) Wisdom in the four paths is both for disenchantment and for penetration. ⤵ (6d) The remaining wisdom is neither for disenchantment nor for penetration.

When perceptions and attentions accompanied by thought beset one who has gained the second meditative absorption, that is wisdom that shares in decline. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by equanimity beset one who has gained the fourth meditative absorption, that is wisdom that shares in decline. When mindfulness in conformity with that state stands firm, that is wisdom that shares in stability. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by the field of infinite space beset him, that is wisdom that shares in distinction. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by disenchantment, connected with dispassion, beset him, that is wisdom that shares in breaking through. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by material form beset one who has gained the field of infinite space, that is wisdom that shares in decline. When mindfulness in conformity with that state stands firm, that is wisdom that shares in stability. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by the field of infinite consciousness beset him, that is wisdom that shares in distinction. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by disenchantment, connected with dispassion, beset him, that is wisdom that shares in breaking through. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by the field of infinite space beset one who has gained the field of infinite consciousness, that is wisdom that shares in decline. When mindfulness in conformity with that state stands firm, that is wisdom that shares in stability. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by the field of nothingness beset him, that is wisdom that shares in distinction. When mindfulness in conformity with that state stands firm, that is wisdom that shares in stability. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception beset him, that is wisdom that shares in distinction. The analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. Knowledge with regard to meaning is the analytical knowledge of meaning; knowledge with regard to principles is the analytical knowledge of principles; knowledge with regard to the expression of the language of those principles is the analytical knowledge of language; knowledge with regard to knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. (9) Therein, what are the four modes of practice? Wisdom of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge, wisdom of difficult practice and quick direct knowledge, wisdom of easy practice and slow direct knowledge, wisdom of easy practice and quick direct knowledge. ⤵ (a) Therein, what is wisdom of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one producing concentration with trouble and difficulty and knowing that state slowly: this is called "wisdom of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge". ⤵ (b) Therein, what is wisdom of difficult practice and quick direct knowledge? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one producing concentration with trouble and difficulty and knowing that state quickly: this is called "wisdom of difficult practice and quick direct knowledge". ⤵ (c) Therein, what is wisdom of easy practice and slow direct knowledge? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one producing concentration without trouble and without difficulty and knowing that state slowly: this is called "wisdom of easy practice and slow direct knowledge". ⤵ (d) Therein, what is wisdom of easy practice and quick direct knowledge? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one producing concentration without trouble and without difficulty and knowing that state quickly: this is called "wisdom of easy practice and quick direct knowledge". These are the four modes of practice.

Samādhissa na nikāmalābhissa ārammaṇaṃ vipulaṃ pharantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati "parittā appamāṇārammaṇā paññā". ⤵ (Ga) tattha katamā appamāṇā parittārammaṇā paññā? Samādhissa nikāmalābhissa ārammaṇaṃ thokaṃ pharantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati "appamāṇā parittārammaṇā paññā". ⤵ (Gha) tattha katamā appamāṇā appamāṇārammaṇā paññā? Samādhissa nikāmalābhissa ārammaṇaṃ vipulaṃ pharantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati "appamāṇā appamāṇārammaṇā paññā". Imāni cattāri ārammaṇāni. ⤵ (11) Maggasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ jarāmaraṇepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇasamudayepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapetaṃ ñāṇaṃ. ⤵ (Ka) tattha katamaṃ jarāmaraṇe ñāṇaṃ? Jarāmaraṇaṃ ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati "jarāmaraṇe ñāṇaṃ". ⤵ (Kha-gha) jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ ārabbha…pe… jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ ārabbha…pe… jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati "jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ".

**en** `853386–855581`
(10) Therein, what are the four objects? Limited wisdom with a limited object, limited wisdom with a measureless object, measureless wisdom with a limited object, measureless wisdom with a measureless object. ⤵ (a) Therein, what is limited wisdom with a limited object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one who has not fully mastered concentration and who pervades a small object: this is called "limited wisdom with a limited object". ⤵ (b) Therein, what is limited wisdom with a measureless object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one who has not fully mastered concentration and who pervades a vast object: this is called "limited wisdom with a measureless object". ⤵ (c) Therein, what is measureless wisdom with a limited object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one who has fully mastered concentration and who pervades a small object: this is called "measureless wisdom with a limited object". ⤵ (d) Therein, what is measureless wisdom with a measureless object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one who has fully mastered concentration and who pervades a vast object: this is called "measureless wisdom with a measureless object". These are the four objects. ⤵ (11) The knowledge of one endowed with the path is knowledge of aging and death, knowledge of the origin of aging and death, knowledge of the cessation of aging and death, and knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of aging and death. ⤵ (a) Therein, what is knowledge of aging and death? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning aging and death: this is called "knowledge of aging and death". ⤵ (b–d) Concerning the origin of aging and death… concerning the cessation of aging and death… concerning the way leading to the cessation of aging and death, the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises: this is called "knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of aging and death".

### 1120

**pi** `577055–577823`
(12-21) Dhammasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ jātiyāpetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… bhavepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… upādānepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… taṇhāyapetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… vedanāyapetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… phassepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… saḷāyatanepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… nāmarūpepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… viññāṇepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… saṅkhāresupetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhārasamudayepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhāranirodhepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapetaṃ ñāṇaṃ. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhāresu ñāṇaṃ? Saṅkhāre ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati "saṅkhāresu ñāṇaṃ". ⤵ Saṅkhārasamudayaṃ ārabbha…pe… saṅkhāranirodhaṃ ārabbha…pe… saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati "saṅkhāranirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ. Evaṃ catubbidhena ñāṇavatthu.

**en** `855582–856595`
(12-21) The knowledge of one endowed with the teaching is knowledge of birth… knowledge of existence… knowledge of clinging… knowledge of craving… knowledge of feeling… knowledge of contact… knowledge of the six sense-fields… knowledge of mentality and material form… knowledge of consciousness… knowledge of formations, knowledge of the origin of formations, knowledge of the cessation of formations, knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of formations. ⤵ Therein, what is knowledge of formations? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning formations: this is called "knowledge of formations". ⤵ Concerning the origin of formations… concerning the cessation of formations… concerning the way leading to the cessation of formations, the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises: this is called "knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of formations. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of four.

### 1121

**pi** `577824–577833`
Catukkaṃ.

**en** `856596–856606`
The Fours.

### 1122

**pi** `577834–577860`
<h2>5. Pañcakaniddeso</h2>

**en** `856607–856646`
<h2>5. The Exposition of the Fives</h2>

### 1123

**pi** `577861–578785`
(1) Tattha katamo pañcaṅgiko sammāsamādhi? Pītipharaṇatā, sukhapharaṇatā, cetopharaṇatā, ālokapharaṇatā, paccavekkhaṇānimittaṃ. Dvīsu jhānesu paññā pītipharaṇatā. Tīsu jhānesu paññā sukhapharaṇatā. Paracitte ñāṇaṃ cetopharaṇatā. Dibbacakkhu ālokapharaṇatā. Tamhā tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhitassa paccavekkhaṇāñāṇaṃ paccavekkhaṇānimittaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati pañcaṅgiko sammāsamādhi. ⤵ (2) Tattha katamo pañcañāṇiko sammāsamādhi? "Ayaṃ samādhi paccuppannasukho ceva āyatiñca sukhavipāko"ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṃ uppajjati. "Ayaṃ samādhi ariyo nirāmiso"ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṃ uppajjati. "Ayaṃ samādhi akāpurisasevito"ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṃ uppajjati. "Ayaṃ samādhi santo paṇīto paṭippassaddhaladdho ekodibhāvādhigato na sasaṅkhāraniggayhavāritagato"ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṃ uppajjati. So kho panāhaṃ imaṃ samādhiṃ sato samāpajjāmi sato vuṭṭhahāmī"ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ pañcañāṇiko sammāsamādhi. Evaṃ pañcavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

**en** `856647–857954`
(1) Therein, what is five-factored right concentration? The pervasion with joy, the pervasion with happiness, the pervasion with mind, the pervasion with light, and the sign for reviewing. Wisdom in two meditative absorptions is the pervasion with joy. Wisdom in three meditative absorptions is the pervasion with happiness. Knowledge of others' minds is the pervasion with mind. The divine eye is the pervasion with light. The reviewing knowledge of one who has emerged from this or that concentration is the sign for reviewing. This is called five-factored right concentration. ⤵ (2) Therein, what is five-knowledged right concentration? The knowledge arises in oneself: "This concentration is both pleasant now and pleasant in its result in the future." The knowledge arises in oneself: "This concentration is noble and unworldly." The knowledge arises in oneself: "This concentration is not practised by base people." The knowledge arises in oneself: "This concentration is peaceful, refined, obtained by tranquillisation, attained through unification, and not maintained by forceful suppression with effort." The knowledge arises in oneself: "Mindful I enter this concentration, and mindful I emerge from it." This is five-knowledged right concentration. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of five.

**en** `857955–857965`
The Fives.

### 1125

**pi** `578796–578821`
<h2>6. Chakkaniddeso</h2>

**en** `857966–858005`
<h2>6. The Exposition of the Sixes</h2>

### 1126

**pi** `578822–579054`
Tattha katamā chasu abhiññāsu paññā? Iddhividhe ñāṇaṃ, sotadhātuvisuddhiyā ñāṇaṃ, paracitte ñāṇaṃ, pubbenivāsānussatiyā ñāṇaṃ, sattānaṃ cutūpapāte ñāṇaṃ, āsavānaṃ khaye ñāṇaṃ – imā chasu abhiññāsu paññā. Evaṃ chabbidhena ñāṇavatthu.

**en** `858006–858424`
Therein, what is wisdom in the six direct knowledges? Knowledge of the kinds of supernormal power, knowledge of the purification of the ear element, knowledge of others' minds, knowledge of the recollection of past lives, knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings, knowledge of the destruction of the mental taints — this is wisdom in the six direct knowledges. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of six.

### 1127

**pi** `579055–579063`
Chakkaṃ.

**en** `858425–858435`
The Sixes.

### 1128

**pi** `579064–579090`
<h2>7. Sattakaniddeso</h2>

**en** `858436–858476`
<h2>7. The Exposition of the Sevens</h2>

### 1129

**pi** `579091–580223`
Tattha katamāni sattasattati ñāṇavatthūni? Jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, atītampi addhānaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, anāgatampi addhānaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ. Yampissa taṃ dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ tampi khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammanti ñāṇaṃ; bhavapaccayā jātīti ñāṇaṃ…pe… upādānapaccayā bhavoti ñāṇaṃ…pe… taṇhāpaccayā upādānanti ñāṇaṃ…pe… vedanāpaccayā taṇhāti ñāṇaṃ…pe… phassapaccayā vedanāti ñāṇaṃ…pe… saḷāyatanapaccayā phassoti ñāṇaṃ…pe… nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatananti ñāṇaṃ…pe… viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpanti ñāṇaṃ…pe… saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇanti ñāṇaṃ…pe… avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, asati avijjāya natthi saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, atītampi addhānaṃ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, asati avijjāya natthi saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, anāgatampi addhānaṃ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, asati avijjāya natthi saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ. Yampissa taṃ dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ tampi khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammanti ñāṇaṃ. Imāni sattasattati ñāṇavatthūni. Evaṃ sattavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

**en** `858477–860470`
Therein, what are the seventy-seven grounds of knowledge? Knowledge that with birth as condition there is aging and death; knowledge that when there is no birth there is no aging and death; knowledge that in the past too, with birth as condition, there was aging and death; knowledge that when there was no birth there was no aging and death; knowledge that in the future too, with birth as condition, there will be aging and death; knowledge that when there is no birth there will be no aging and death. And the knowledge that this knowledge of the fixity of things is itself subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation. Knowledge that with existence as condition there is birth… knowledge that with clinging as condition there is existence… knowledge that with craving as condition there is clinging… knowledge that with feeling as condition there is craving… knowledge that with contact as condition there is feeling… knowledge that with the six sense-fields as condition there is contact… knowledge that with mentality and material form as condition there are the six sense-fields… knowledge that with consciousness as condition there is mentality and material form… knowledge that with formations as condition there is consciousness… knowledge that with ignorance as condition there are formations; knowledge that when there is no ignorance there are no formations; knowledge that in the past too, with ignorance as condition, there were formations; knowledge that when there was no ignorance there were no formations; knowledge that in the future too, with ignorance as condition, there will be formations; knowledge that when there is no ignorance there will be no formations. And the knowledge that this knowledge of the fixity of things is itself subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation. These are the seventy-seven grounds of knowledge. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of seven.

### 1130

**pi** `580224–580233`
Sattakaṃ.

**en** `860471–860482`
The Sevens.

### 1131

**pi** `580234–580260`
<h2>8. Aṭṭhakaniddeso</h2>

**en** `860483–860523`

### 1132

**pi** `580261–580556`
Tattha katamā catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā? Sotāpattimagge paññā, sotāpattiphale paññā , sakadāgāmimagge paññā, sakadāgāmiphale paññā, anāgāmimagge paññā, anāgāmiphale paññā, arahattamagge paññā, arahattaphale paññā – imā catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

**en** `860524–860986`
Therein, what is wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits? Wisdom in the path of stream-entry, wisdom in the fruit of stream-entry, wisdom in the path of once-returning, wisdom in the fruit of once-returning, wisdom in the path of non-returning, wisdom in the fruit of non-returning, wisdom in the path of arahantship, wisdom in the fruit of arahantship — this is wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of eight.

### 1133

**pi** `580557–580566`
Aṭṭhakaṃ.

**en** `860987–860998`
The Eights.

### 1134

<h2>9. Navakaniddeso</h2>

**en** `860999–861038`
<h2>9. The Exposition of the Nines</h2>

### 1135

**pi** `580593–581056`
Tattha katamā navasu anupubbavihārasamāpattīsu paññā? Paṭhamajjhānasamāpattiyā paññā, dutiyajjhānasamāpattiyā paññā, tatiyajjhānasamāpattiyā paññā, catutthajjhānasamāpattiyā paññā, ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā paññā, viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpattiyā paññā, ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattiyā paññā, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā paññā, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitassa paccavekkhaṇāñāṇaṃ – imā navasu anupubbavihārasamāpattīsu paññā. Evaṃ navavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

**en** `861039–861833`
Therein, what is wisdom in the nine successive dwelling attainments? Wisdom in the attainment of the first meditative absorption, wisdom in the attainment of the second meditative absorption, wisdom in the attainment of the third meditative absorption, wisdom in the attainment of the fourth meditative absorption, wisdom in the attainment of the field of infinite space, wisdom in the attainment of the field of infinite consciousness, wisdom in the attainment of the field of nothingness, wisdom in the attainment of the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and the reviewing knowledge of one who has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling — this is wisdom in the nine successive dwelling attainments. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of nine.

### 1136

**pi** `581057–581065`

**en** `861834–861844`
The Nines.

**en** `861845–861884`

### 1138

**pi** `581093–586507`
(1) Tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ? Idha tathāgato "aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṃ niccato upagaccheyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puthujjano kañci saṅkhāraṃ niccato upagaccheyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṃ sukhato upagaccheyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puthujjano kañci saṅkhāraṃ sukhato upagaccheyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci dhammaṃ atthato upagaccheyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puthujjano kañci dhammaṃ atthato upagaccheyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo mātaraṃ jīvitā voropeyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puthujjano mātaraṃ jīvitā voropeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. ⤵ Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo pitaraṃ jīvitā voropeyya…pe… arahantaṃ jīvitā voropeyya…pe… paduṭṭhena cittena tathāgatassa lohitaṃ uppādeyya…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindeyya…pe… aññaṃ satthāraṃ uddiseyya…pe… aṭṭhamaṃ bhavaṃ nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puthujjano aṭṭhamaṃ bhavaṃ nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. ⤵ "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve arahanto sammāsambuddhā apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyuṃ, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā eko arahaṃ sammāsambuddho uppajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve rājāno cakkavattī [cakkavatti (sī. syā.)] apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyuṃ, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā eko rājā cakkavattī uppajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. ⤵ "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī arahaṃ assa sammāsambuddho, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puriso arahaṃ assa sammāsambuddho, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī rājā assa cakkavattī, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puriso rājā assa cakkavattī, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī sakkattaṃ kareyya, mārattaṃ kareyya, brahmattaṃ kareyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puriso sakkattaṃ kareyya, mārattaṃ kareyya, brahmattaṃ kareyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. ⤵ "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ kāyaduccaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ kāyaduccaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ vacīduccaritassa…pe… yaṃ manoduccaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ vacīduccaritassa…pe… yaṃ manoduccaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. ⤵ "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ kāyasucaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ kāyasucaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. "Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ vacīsucaritassa…pe… yaṃ manosucaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī"ti pajānāti. **en** `861885–868676`
(1) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible? Here the Tathāgata knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a person accomplished in view should take any formation as permanent — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an ordinary person should take some formation as permanent — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a person accomplished in view should take any formation as pleasant — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an ordinary person should take some formation as pleasant — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a person accomplished in view should take any thing as self — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an ordinary person should take some thing as self — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a person accomplished in view should deprive his mother of life — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an ordinary person should deprive his mother of life — this is possible." ⤵ He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a person accomplished in view should deprive his father of life… should deprive an arahant of life… should with a mind of hatred shed the blood of a Tathāgata… should split the Order… should acknowledge another teacher… should produce an eighth existence — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an ordinary person should produce an eighth existence — this is possible." ⤵ He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that two arahants who are fully awakened Buddhas should arise in one world system neither before nor after each other — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one arahant who is a fully awakened Buddha should arise in one world system — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that two wheel-turning kings should arise in one world system neither before nor after each other — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one wheel-turning king should arise in one world system — this is possible." ⤵ He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a woman should be an arahant who is a fully awakened Buddha — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that a man should be an arahant who is a fully awakened Buddha — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a woman should be a wheel-turning king — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that a man should be a wheel-turning king — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a woman should exercise the rulership of Sakka, the rulership of Māra, the rulership of Brahmā — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that a man should exercise the rulership of Sakka, the rulership of Māra, the rulership of Brahmā — this is possible." ⤵ He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a wished-for, desired, agreeable result should come from bodily misconduct — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an unwished-for, undesired, disagreeable result should come from bodily misconduct — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a wished-for, desired, agreeable result should come from verbal misconduct… from mental misconduct — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an unwished-for, undesired, disagreeable result should come from verbal misconduct… from mental misconduct — this is possible." ⤵ He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that an unwished-for, undesired, disagreeable result should come from good bodily conduct — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that a wished-for, desired, agreeable result should come from good bodily conduct — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that an unwished-for, undesired, disagreeable result should come from good verbal conduct… from good mental conduct — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that a wished-for, desired, agreeable result should come from good verbal conduct… from good mental conduct — this is possible." ⤵ He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that one given to bodily misconduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one given to bodily misconduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, hell — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that one given to verbal misconduct… one given to mental misconduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one given to verbal misconduct… one given to mental misconduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, hell — this is possible." ⤵ He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that one given to good bodily conduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, hell — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one given to good bodily conduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that one given to good verbal conduct… one given to good mental conduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, hell — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one given to good verbal conduct… one given to good mental conduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world — this is possible." "Whatever things are causes and conditions of whatever things — that, accordingly, is the possible; whatever things are not causes and not conditions of whatever things — that, accordingly, is the impossible." The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible.

(2) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the result of past, future, and present undertakings of action, according to circumstance and according to cause? Here the Tathāgata knows: "There are some evil undertakings of action which, blocked by a fortunate destination, do not ripen. There are some evil undertakings of action which, blocked by a fortunate body, do not ripen. There are some evil undertakings of action which, blocked by fortunate time, do not ripen. There are some evil undertakings of action which, blocked by fortunate effort, do not ripen. ⤵ "There are some evil undertakings of action which ripen through an unfortunate destination. There are some evil undertakings of action which ripen through an unfortunate body. There are some evil undertakings of action which ripen through unfortunate time. There are some evil undertakings of action which ripen through unfortunate effort. ⤵ "There are some good undertakings of action which, blocked by an unfortunate destination, do not ripen. There are some good undertakings of action which, blocked by an unfortunate body, do not ripen. There are some good undertakings of action which, blocked by unfortunate time, do not ripen. There are some good undertakings of action which, blocked by unfortunate effort, do not ripen. ⤵ "There are some good undertakings of action which ripen through a fortunate destination. There are some good undertakings of action which ripen through a fortunate body. There are some good undertakings of action which ripen through fortunate time. There are some good undertakings of action which ripen through fortunate effort." The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the result of past, future, and present undertakings of action, according to circumstance and according to cause.
