<h2>(13) The three fears</h2>

### 1358

**pi** `635823–636316`
Tattha katamāni tīṇi bhayāni? Jātibhayaṃ, jarābhayaṃ, maraṇabhayaṃ. ⤵ (Ka) tattha katamaṃ jātibhayaṃ? Jātiṃ paṭicca bhayaṃ bhayānakaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso cetaso utrāso – idaṃ vuccati "jātibhayaṃ". ⤵ (Kha) tattha katamaṃ jarābhayaṃ? Jaraṃ paṭicca bhayaṃ bhayānakaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso cetaso utrāso – idaṃ vuccati "jarābhayaṃ". ⤵ (Ga) tattha katamaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ? Maraṇaṃ paṭicca bhayaṃ bhayānakaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso cetaso utrāso – idaṃ vuccati "maraṇabhayaṃ". Imāni tīṇi bhayāni.

**en** `938357–938958`
Therein, what are the three fears? The fear of birth, the fear of aging, the fear of death. ⤵ (a) Therein, what is the fear of birth? On account of birth: the fear, fearfulness, terror, horripilation, alarm of mind — this is called "the fear of birth". ⤵ (b) Therein, what is the fear of aging? On account of aging: the fear, fearfulness, terror, horripilation, alarm of mind — this is called "the fear of aging". ⤵ (c) Therein, what is the fear of death? On account of death: the fear, fearfulness, terror, horripilation, alarm of mind — this is called "the fear of death". These are the three fears.

### 1359

**pi** `636317–636342`
<h2>(14) Tīṇi tamāni</h2>

**en** `938959–938993`
<h2>(14) The three darknesses</h2>

### 1360

**pi** `636343–636641`
Tattha katamāni tīṇi tamāni? Atītaṃ vā addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, anāgataṃ vā addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, etarahi vā paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati – imāni tīṇi tamāni.

**en** `938994–939356`
Therein, what are the three darknesses? Concerning the past one doubts, is perplexed, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; concerning the future one doubts, is perplexed, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; concerning the present one doubts, is perplexed, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence — these are the three darknesses.

### 1361

**pi** `636642–636675`
<h2>(15) Tīṇi titthāyatanāni</h2>

**en** `939357–939398`
<h2>(15) The three sectarian grounds</h2>

### 1362

**pi** `636676–637270`
Tattha katamāni tīṇi titthāyatanāni? Idhekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī hoti evaṃdiṭṭhī – "yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ pubbe katahetū"ti; idha panekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī hoti evaṃdiṭṭhī – "yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ issaranimmānahetū"ti; idha panekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī hoti evaṃdiṭṭhī – "yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ ahetu appaccayā"ti – imāni tīṇi titthāyatanāni.

**en** `939399–940109`
Therein, what are the three sectarian grounds? Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "Whatever this person experiences, whether pleasant or painful or neither painful nor pleasant, all that is caused by what was done in the past." Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "Whatever this person experiences, whether pleasant or painful or neither painful nor pleasant, all that is caused by a supreme being's creation." Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "Whatever this person experiences, whether pleasant or painful or neither painful nor pleasant, all that is without cause and without condition." These are the three sectarian grounds.

### 1363

**pi** `637271–637297`
<h2>(16) Tayo kiñcanā</h2>

**en** `940110–940145`
<h2>(16) The three impediments</h2>

### 1364

**pi** `637298–637433`
Tattha katame tayo kiñcanā [katamāni tīṇi kiñcanāni (?) dī. ni. 3.305]? Rāgo kiñcanaṃ, doso kiñcanaṃ, moho kiñcanaṃ – ime tayo kiñcanā.

**en** `940146–940293`
Therein, what are the three impediments? Lust is an impediment, hate is an impediment, delusion is an impediment — these are the three impediments.

### 1365

**pi** `637434–637461`
<h2>(17) Tīṇi aṅgaṇāni</h2>

**en** `940294–940327`
<h2>(17) The three blemishes</h2>

### 1366

**pi** `637462–637556`
Tattha katamāni tīṇi aṅgaṇāni? Rāgo aṅgaṇaṃ, doso aṅgaṇaṃ, moho aṅgaṇaṃ – imāni tīṇi aṅgaṇāni.

**en** `940328–940459`
Therein, what are the three blemishes? Lust is a blemish, hate is a blemish, delusion is a blemish — these are the three blemishes.

### 1367

**pi** `637557–637582`
<h2>(18) Tīṇi malāni</h2>

**en** `940460–940490`
<h2>(18) The three stains</h2>

### 1368

**pi** `637583–637667`
Tattha katamāni tīṇi malāni? Rāgo malaṃ, doso malaṃ, moho malaṃ – imāni tīṇi malāni.

**en** `940491–940610`
Therein, what are the three stains? Lust is a stain, hate is a stain, delusion is a stain — these are the three stains.

### 1369

**pi** `637668–637695`
<h2>(19) Tīṇi visamāni</h2>

**en** `940611–940647`
<h2>(19) The three unevennesses</h2>

### 1370

**pi** `637696–637790`
Tattha katamāni tīṇi visamāni? Rāgo visamaṃ, doso visamaṃ, moho visamaṃ – imāni tīṇi visamāni.

**en** `940648–940788`
Therein, what are the three unevennesses? Lust is unevenness, hate is unevenness, delusion is unevenness — these are the three unevennesses.

### 1371

**pi** `637791–637828`
<h2>(20) Aparānipi tīṇi visamāni</h2>

**en** `940789–940829`
<h2>(20) Another three unevennesses</h2>

### 1372

**pi** `637829–637930`
Tattha katamāni aparānipi tīṇi visamāni? Kāyavisamaṃ, vacīvisamaṃ, manovisamaṃ – imāni tīṇi visamāni.

**en** `940830–940967`
Therein, what are another three unevennesses? Bodily unevenness, verbal unevenness, mental unevenness — these are the three unevennesses.

### 1373

**pi** `637931–637954`
<h2>(21) Tayo aggī</h2>

**en** `940968–940997`
<h2>(21) The three fires</h2>

### 1374

**pi** `637955–638022`
Tattha katame tayo aggī? Rāgaggi, dosaggi, mohaggi – ime tayo aggī.

**en** `940998–941118`
Therein, what are the three fires? The fire of lust, the fire of hate, the fire of delusion — these are the three fires.

### 1375

**pi** `638023–638048`
<h2>(22) Tayo kasāvā</h2>

**en** `941119–941154`
<h2>(22) The three corruptions</h2>

### 1376

**pi** `638049–638129`
Tattha katame tayo kasāvā? Rāgakasāvo, dosakasāvo, mohakasāvo – ime tayo kasāvā.

**en** `941155–941305`
Therein, what are the three corruptions? The corruption of lust, the corruption of hate, the corruption of delusion — these are the three corruptions.

### 1377

**pi** `638130–638163`
<h2>(23) Aparepi tayo kasāvā</h2>

**en** `941306–941345`
<h2>(23) Another three corruptions</h2>

### 1378

**pi** `638164–638252`
Tattha katame aparepi tayo kasāvā? Kāyakasāvo, vacīkasāvo, manokasāvo – ime tayo kasāvā.

**en** `941346–941481`
Therein, what are another three corruptions? Bodily corruption, verbal corruption, mental corruption — these are the three corruptions.

### 1379

**pi** `638253–638283`
<h2>(24. Ka) assādadiṭṭhi</h2>

**en** `941482–941518`
<h2>(24a) The view of enjoyment</h2>

### 1380

**pi** `638284–638454`
Tattha katamā assādadiṭṭhi? Idhekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī hoti evaṃdiṭṭhī – "natthi kāmesu doso"ti. So kāmesu pātabyataṃ āpajjati. Ayaṃ vuccati "assādadiṭṭhi".

**en** `941519–941733`
Therein, what is the view of enjoyment? Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "There is no fault in sense pleasures." He plunges into sense pleasures. This is called "the view of enjoyment".

### 1381

**pi** `638455–638482`
<h2>(Kha) attānudiṭṭhi</h2>

**en** `941734–941763`
<h2>(b) The view of self</h2>

### 1382

**pi** `638483–638973`
Tattha katamā attānudiṭṭhi? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto – rūpaṃ attato samanupassati rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ attani vā rūpaṃ rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ attani vā viññāṇaṃ viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati "attānudiṭṭhi".

**en** `941764–942486`
Therein, what is the view of self? Here an unlearned ordinary person — who has no regard for the noble ones, is unskilled in the teaching of the noble ones, untrained in the teaching of the noble ones; who has no regard for good people, is unskilled in the teaching of good people, untrained in the teaching of good people — regards material form as self, or self as possessing material form, or material form as in self, or self as in material form. He regards feeling… perception… formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "the view of self".

### 1383

**pi** `638974–639000`
<h2>(Ga) micchādiṭṭhi</h2>

**en** `942487–942510`
<h2>(c) Wrong view</h2>

### 1384

**pi** `639001–639299`
Tattha katamā micchādiṭṭhi? "Natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī"ti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati "micchādiṭṭhi". Sassatadiṭṭhi assādadiṭṭhi, sakkāyadiṭṭhi attānudiṭṭhi, ucchedadiṭṭhi micchādiṭṭhi.

**en** `942511–942935`
Therein, what is wrong view? "There is nothing given, there is nothing offered… who declare this world and the other world, having realised them for themselves by direct knowledge" — whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "wrong view". The eternalist view is the view of enjoyment; the view of a self in the body is the view of self; the annihilationist view is wrong view.

### 1385

**pi** `639300–639323`
<h2>(25. Ka) arati</h2>

**en** `942936–942961`
<h2>(25a) Discontent</h2>

### 1386

**pi** `639324–639494`
Tattha katamā arati? Pantesu vā senāsanesu aññataraññataresu vā adhikusalesu dhammesu arati aratitā anabhirati anabhiramaṇā ukkaṇṭhitā paritassitā – ayaṃ vuccati "arati".

**en** `942962–943179`
Therein, what is discontent? Discontent with remote dwelling places or with any of the higher wholesome things; being discontented, dissatisfaction, not delighting, restlessness, anxiety — this is called "discontent".

### 1387

**pi** `639495–639516`
<h2>(Kha) vihesā</h2>

**en** `943180–943200`
<h2>(b) Cruelty</h2>

### 1388

**pi** `639517–639738`
Tattha katamā vihesā? Idhekacco pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā rajjuyā vā aññataraññatarena satte viheṭheti, yā evarūpā heṭhanā viheṭhanā hiṃsanā vihiṃsanā rosanā virosanā parūpaghāto – ayaṃ vuccati "vihesā".

**en** `943201–943487`
Therein, what is cruelty? Here someone harms beings with the hand, or a clod, or a stick, or a knife, or a rope, or with one thing or another; whatever harming of this kind there is, harassing, hurting, injuring, provoking, enraging, doing violence to others — this is called "cruelty".

### 1389

**pi** `639739–639766`
<h2>(Ga) adhammacariyā</h2>

**en** `943488–943520`
<h2>(c) Unrighteous conduct</h2>

### 1390

**pi** `639767–639928`
Tattha katamā adhammacariyā? Kāyena adhammacariyāvisamacariyā, vācāya adhammacariyāvisamacariyā, manasā adhammacariyāvisamacariyā – ayaṃ vuccati "adhammacariyā".

**en** `943521–943757`
Therein, what is unrighteous conduct? Unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct with the body, unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct with speech, unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct with the mind — this is called "unrighteous conduct".

### 1391

**pi** `639929–639958`
<h2>(26. Ka) dovacassatā</h2>

**en** `943758–943794`
<h2>(26a) Being hard to correct</h2>

### 1392

**pi** `639959–640158`
Tattha katamā dovacassatā? Sahadhammike vuccamāne dovacassāyaṃ dovacassiyaṃ dovacassatā vippaṭikulaggāhitā vipaccanīkasātatā anādariyaṃ anādaratā agāravatā appatissavatā – ayaṃ vuccati "dovacassatā".

**en** `943795–944135`
Therein, what is being hard to correct? When one is addressed in accordance with the teaching: the being hard to speak to, the difficulty in correcting, the state of being hard to correct, contrary grasping, delight in opposition, disrespect, disrespectfulness, lack of reverence, lack of deference — this is called "being hard to correct".

### 1393

**pi** `640159–640185`
<h2>(Kha) pāpamittatā</h2>

**en** `944136–944164`
<h2>(b) Evil friendship</h2>

### 1394

**pi** `640186–640391`
Tattha katamā pāpamittatā? Ye te puggalā assaddhā dussīlā appassutā maccharino duppaññā, yā tesaṃ sevanā nisevanā saṃsevanā bhajanā sambhajanā bhatti sambhatti taṃsampavaṅkatā – ayaṃ vuccati "pāpamittatā".

**en** `944165–944519`
Therein, what is evil friendship? Those persons who are without confidence, of bad conduct, of little learning, stingy, and without wisdom — the resorting to them, the frequenting, the close frequenting, the associating with them, the fully associating, the devotion, the full devotion, the being inclined towards them — this is called "evil friendship".

### 1395

**pi** `640392–640418`
<h2>(Ga) nānattasaññā</h2>

**en** `944520–944556`
<h2>(c) Perception of diversity</h2>

### 1396

**pi** `640419–640551`
Tattha katamā nānattasaññā? Kāmasaññā, byāpādasaññā, vihiṃsāsaññā – ayaṃ vuccati "nānattasaññā". Sabbāpi akusalā saññā nānattasaññā.

**en** `944557–944785`
Therein, what is perception of diversity? The perception of sense pleasure, the perception of ill will, the perception of cruelty — this is called "perception of diversity". All unwholesome perception is perception of diversity.

### 1397

**pi** `640552–640579`
<h2>(27. Ka) uddhaccaṃ</h2>

**en** `944786–944813`
<h2>(27a) Restlessness</h2>

### 1398

**pi** `640580–640702`
Tattha katamaṃ uddhaccaṃ? Yaṃ cittassa uddhaccaṃ avūpasamo cetaso vikkhepo bhantattaṃ cittassa – idaṃ vuccati "uddhaccaṃ".

**en** `944814–944963`
Therein, what is restlessness? The restlessness of the mind, lack of calm, mental distraction, agitation of the mind — this is called "restlessness".

### 1399

**pi** `640703–640726`
<h2>(Kha) kosajjaṃ</h2>

**en** `944964–944985`
<h2>(b) Laziness</h2>

### 1400

**pi** `640727–641083`
Tattha katamaṃ kosajjaṃ? Kāyaduccarite vā vacīduccarite vā manoduccarite vā pañcasu vā kāmaguṇesu cittassa vossaggo vossaggānuppadānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanāya asakkaccakiriyatā asātaccakiriyatā anaṭṭhitakiriyatā olīnavuttitā nikkhittachandatā nikkhittadhuratā anāsevanā abhāvanā abahulīkammaṃ anadhiṭṭhānaṃ ananuyogo pamādo – idaṃ vuccati "kosajjaṃ".

**en** `944986–945478`
Therein, what is laziness? Letting the mind loose in bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, or the five strands of sense pleasure, and repeatedly letting it loose; acting without respect for the development of wholesome things, acting without perseverance, acting inconstantly, sluggish behaviour, putting down desire, putting down the responsibility, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, non-resolution, non-application, heedlessness — this is called "laziness".

### 1401

**pi** `641084–641104`
<h2>(Ga) pamādo</h2>

**en** `945479–945504`
<h2>(c) Heedlessness</h2>

### 1402

**pi** `641105–641499`
Tattha katamo pamādo? Kāyaduccarite vā vacīduccarite vā manoduccarite vā pañcasu vā kāmaguṇesu cittassa vossaggo vossaggānuppadānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanāya asakkaccakiriyatā asātaccakiriyatā anaṭṭhitakiriyatā olīnavuttitā nikkhittachandatā nikkhittadhuratā anāsevanā abhāvanā abahulīkammaṃ anadhiṭṭhānaṃ ananuyogo pamādo, yo evarūpo pamādo pamajjanā pamajjitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "pamādo".

**en** `945505–946093`
Therein, what is heedlessness? Letting the mind loose in bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, or the five strands of sense pleasure, and repeatedly letting it loose; acting without respect for the development of wholesome things, acting without perseverance, acting inconstantly, sluggish behaviour, putting down desire, putting down the responsibility, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, non-resolution, non-application, heedlessness; whatever heedlessness of this kind there is, being heedless, the state of heedlessness — this is called "heedlessness".

### 1403

**pi** `641500–641530`
<h2>(28. Ka) asantuṭṭhitā</h2>

**en** `946094–946123`
<h2>(28a) Discontentment</h2>

### 1404

**pi** `641531–641774`
Tattha katamā asantuṭṭhitā? Itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi pañcahi vā kāmaguṇehi asantuṭṭhassa bhiyyokamyatā, yā evarūpā icchā icchāgatā asantuṭṭhitā rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati "asantuṭṭhitā".

**en** `946124–946473`
Therein, what is discontentment? The wanting of more by one discontented with whatever robes, alms-food, dwelling place, and medicinal supports for the sick he has, or with the five strands of sense pleasure; whatever desire of this kind there is, being desirous, discontentment, lust, passion, passion of the mind — this is called "discontentment".

### 1405

**pi** `641775–641803`
<h2>(Kha) asampajaññatā</h2>

**en** `946474–946514`
<h2>(b) Lack of clear comprehension</h2>

### 1406

**pi** `641804–641920`
Tattha katamā asampajaññatā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "asampajaññatā".

**en** `946515–946704`
Therein, what is lack of clear comprehension? The lack of knowledge, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "lack of clear comprehension".

### 1407

**pi** `641921–641945`
<h2>(Ga) mahicchatā</h2>

**en** `946705–946730`
<h2>(c) Great desire</h2>

### 1408

**pi** `641946–642183`
Tattha katamā mahicchatā? Itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi pañcahi vā kāmaguṇehi asantuṭṭhassa bhiyyokamyatā, yā evarūpā icchā icchāgatā mahicchatā rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati "mahicchatā".

**en** `946731–947074`
Therein, what is great desire? The wanting of more by one discontented with whatever robes, alms-food, dwelling place, and medicinal supports for the sick he has, or with the five strands of sense pleasure; whatever desire of this kind there is, being desirous, great desire, lust, passion, passion of the mind — this is called "great desire".

### 1409

**pi** `642184–642210`
<h2>(29. Ka) ahirikaṃ</h2>

**en** `947075–947103`
<h2>(29a) Shamelessness</h2>

### 1410

**pi** `642211–642348`
Tattha katamaṃ ahirikaṃ? Yaṃ na hirīyati hirīyitabbena, na hirīyati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā – idaṃ vuccati "ahirikaṃ".

**en** `947104–947277`
Therein, what is shamelessness? Not being ashamed of what one should be ashamed of, not being ashamed of taking up evil, unwholesome things — this is called "shamelessness".

### 1411

**pi** `642349–642374`
<h2>(Kha) anottappaṃ</h2>

**en** `947278–947310`
<h2>(b) Lack of moral dread</h2>

### 1412

**pi** `642375–642519`
Tattha katamaṃ anottappaṃ? Yaṃ na ottappati ottappitabbena, na ottappati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā – idaṃ vuccati "anottappaṃ".

**en** `947311–947472`
Therein, what is lack of moral dread? Not dreading what one should dread, not dreading taking up evil, unwholesome things — this is called "lack of moral dread".

### 1413

**pi** `642520–642540`
<h2>(Ga) pamādo</h2>

**en** `947473–947498`
<h2>(c) Heedlessness</h2>

### 1414

**pi** `642541–642935`
Tattha katamo pamādo? Kāyaduccarite vā vacīduccarite vā manoduccarite vā pañcasu vā kāmaguṇesu cittassa vossaggo vossaggānuppadānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanāya asakkaccakiriyatā asātaccakiriyatā anaṭṭhitakiriyatā olīnavuttitā nikkhittachandatā nikkhittadhuratā anāsevanā abhāvanā abahulīkammaṃ anadhiṭṭhānaṃ ananuyogo pamādo, yo evarūpo pamādo pamajjanā pamajjitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "pamādo".

**en** `947499–948087`
Therein, what is heedlessness? Letting the mind loose in bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, or the five strands of sense pleasure, and repeatedly letting it loose; acting without respect for the development of wholesome things, acting without perseverance, acting inconstantly, sluggish behaviour, putting down desire, putting down the responsibility, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, non-resolution, non-application, heedlessness; whatever heedlessness of this kind there is, being heedless, the state of heedlessness — this is called "heedlessness".

### 1415

**pi** `642936–642964`
<h2>(30. Ka) anādariyaṃ</h2>

**en** `948088–948113`
<h2>(30a) Disrespect</h2>

### 1416

**pi** `642965–643160`
Tattha katamaṃ anādariyaṃ? Yaṃ anādariyaṃ anādaratā agāravatā appatissavatā anaddā anaddāyanā anaddāyitattaṃ [anādā anādāyanā anādāyitattaṃ (syā.)] asīlyaṃ acittīkāro – idaṃ vuccati "anādariyaṃ".

**en** `948114–948350`
Therein, what is disrespect? The disrespect, disrespectfulness, lack of reverence, lack of deference, lack of regard, absence of regard, the state of having no regard, lack of virtue, lack of consideration — this is called "disrespect".

### 1417

**pi** `643161–643187`
<h2>(Kha) dovacassatā</h2>

**en** `948351–948385`
<h2>(b) Being hard to correct</h2>

### 1418

**pi** `643188–643387`
Tattha katamā dovacassatā? Sahadhammike vuccamāne dovacassāyaṃ dovacassiyaṃ dovacassatā vippaṭikulaggāhitā vipaccanīkasātatā anādariyaṃ anādaratā agāravatā appatissavatā – ayaṃ vuccati "dovacassatā".

**en** `948386–948726`
Therein, what is being hard to correct? When one is addressed in accordance with the teaching: the being hard to speak to, the difficulty in correcting, the state of being hard to correct, contrary grasping, delight in opposition, disrespect, disrespectfulness, lack of reverence, lack of deference — this is called "being hard to correct".

### 1419

**pi** `643388–643413`
<h2>(Ga) pāpamittatā</h2>

**en** `948727–948755`
<h2>(c) Evil friendship</h2>

### 1420

**pi** `643414–643630`
Tattha katamā pāpamittatā? Ye te puggalā assaddhā dussīlā appassutā maccharino duppaññā, yā tesaṃ sevanā nisevanā saṃsevanā paṭisevanā bhajanā sambhajanā bhatti sambhatti taṃsampavaṅkatā – ayaṃ vuccati "pāpamittatā".

**en** `948756–949135`
Therein, what is evil friendship? Those persons who are without confidence, of bad conduct, of little learning, stingy, and without wisdom — the resorting to them, the frequenting, the close frequenting, the attending upon them, the associating with them, the fully associating, the devotion, the full devotion, the being inclined towards them — this is called "evil friendship".

### 1421

**pi** `643631–643660`
<h2>(31. Ka) assaddhiyaṃ</h2>

**en** `949136–949169`
<h2>(31a) Lack of confidence</h2>

### 1422

**pi** `643661–643852`
Tattha katamaṃ assaddhiyaṃ? Idhekacco assaddho hoti, na saddahati buddhaṃ vā dhammaṃ vā saṅghaṃ vā, yaṃ evarūpaṃ assaddhiyaṃ assaddahanā anokappanā anabhippasādo – idaṃ vuccati "assaddhiyaṃ".

**en** `949170–949475`
Therein, what is lack of confidence? Here someone is without confidence: he does not have confidence in the Buddha, or the teaching, or the Order; whatever lack of confidence of this kind there is, absence of trusting, absence of reliance, absence of full confidence — this is called "lack of confidence".

### 1423

**pi** `643853–643878`
<h2>(Kha) avadaññutā</h2>

**en** `949476–949505`
<h2>(b) Uncharitableness</h2>

### 1424

**pi** `643879–644153`
Tattha katamā avadaññutā? Pañca macchariyāni – āvāsamacchariyaṃ, kulamacchariyaṃ, lābhamacchariyaṃ, vaṇṇamacchariyaṃ, dhammamacchariyaṃ. Yaṃ evarūpaṃ maccheraṃ maccharāyanā maccharāyitattaṃ vevicchaṃ kadariyaṃ kaṭukañcukatā aggahitattaṃ cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati "avadaññutā".

**en** `949506–949897`
Therein, what is uncharitableness? The five kinds of stinginess: stinginess about dwellings, stinginess about families, stinginess about gains, stinginess about praise, stinginess about the teaching. Whatever stinginess of this kind there is, being stingy, the state of stinginess; meanness, miserliness, tight-fistedness, the ungenerous grip of the mind — this is called "uncharitableness".

### 1425

**pi** `644154–644176`
<h2>(Ga) kosajjaṃ</h2>

**en** `949898–949919`
<h2>(c) Laziness</h2>

### 1426

**pi** `644177–644535`
Tattha katamaṃ kosajjaṃ? Kāyaduccarite vā vacīduccarite vā manoduccarite vā pañcasu vā kāmaguṇesu cittassa vossaggo, vossaggānuppadānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ, bhāvanāya asakkaccakiriyatā asātaccakiriyatā anaṭṭhitakiriyatā olīnavuttitā nikkhittachandatā nikkhittadhuratā anāsevanā abhāvanā abahulīkammaṃ anadhiṭṭhānaṃ ananuyogo pamādo – idaṃ vuccati "kosajjaṃ".

**en** `949920–950412`
Therein, what is laziness? Letting the mind loose in bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, or the five strands of sense pleasure, and repeatedly letting it loose; acting without respect for the development of wholesome things, acting without perseverance, acting inconstantly, sluggish behaviour, putting down desire, putting down the responsibility, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, non-resolution, non-application, heedlessness — this is called "laziness".

### 1427

**pi** `644536–644563`
<h2>(32. Ka) uddhaccaṃ</h2>

**en** `950413–950440`
<h2>(32a) Restlessness</h2>

### 1428

**pi** `644564–644688`
Tattha katamaṃ uddhaccaṃ? Yaṃ cittassa uddhaccaṃ avūpasamo cetaso vikkhepo bhavantattaṃ cittassa – idaṃ vuccati "uddhaccaṃ".

**en** `950441–950590`
Therein, what is restlessness? The restlessness of the mind, lack of calm, mental distraction, agitation of the mind — this is called "restlessness".

### 1429

**pi** `644689–644712`
<h2>(Kha) asaṃvaro</h2>

**en** `950591–950617`
<h2>(b) Non-restraint</h2>

### 1430

**pi** `644713–645401`
Tattha katamo asaṃvaro? Idhekacco cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā nimittaggāhī hoti anubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya na paṭipajjati, na rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya nimittaggāhī hoti anubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya na paṭipajjati, na rakkhati manindriyaṃ, manindriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati – ayaṃ vuccati "asaṃvaro".

**en** `950618–951543`
Therein, what is non-restraint? Here someone, having seen a sight with the eye, grasps at its signs and grasps at its details. Since, if he dwelt with the eye faculty unrestrained, covetousness and grief, evil, unwholesome things, might flow in upon him, he does not practise for its restraint, he does not guard the eye faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the eye faculty. Having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled a smell with the nose… having tasted a taste with the tongue… having touched a tangible thing with the body… having known a mental object with the mind, he grasps at its signs and grasps at its details. Since, if he dwelt with the mind faculty unrestrained, covetousness and grief, evil, unwholesome things, might flow in upon him, he does not practise for its restraint, he does not guard the mind faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the mind faculty — this is called "non-restraint".

### 1431

**pi** `645402–645425`
<h2>(Ga) dussīlyaṃ</h2>

**en** `951544–951568`
<h2>(c) Bad conduct</h2>

### 1432

**pi** `645426–645542`
Tattha katamaṃ dussīlyaṃ? Kāyiko vītikkamo, vācasiko vītikkamo, kāyikavācasiko vītikkamo – idaṃ vuccati "dussīlyaṃ".

**en** `951569–951711`
Therein, what is bad conduct? Transgression in body, transgression in speech, transgression in body and speech — this is called "bad conduct".

### 1433

**pi** `645543–645585`
<h2>(33. Ka) ariyānaṃ adassanakamyatā</h2>

**en** `951712–951760`
<h2>(33a) Not wishing to see the noble ones</h2>

### 1434

**pi** `645586–645814`
Tattha katamā ariyānaṃ adassanakamyatā? Tattha katame ariyā? Ariyā vuccanti buddhā ca buddhasāvakā ca. Yā imesaṃ ariyānaṃ adassanakamyatā adaṭṭhukamyatā asametukamyatā asamāgantukamyatā – ayaṃ vuccati "ariyānaṃ adassanakamyatā".

**en** `951761–952111`
Therein, what is not wishing to see the noble ones? Therein, who are the noble ones? The Buddhas and the Buddhas' disciples are called the noble ones. The not wishing to see these noble ones, the not wishing to behold them, the not wishing to meet them, the not wishing to come together with them — this is called "not wishing to see the noble ones".

### 1435

**pi** `645815–645853`
<h2>(Kha) saddhammaṃ asotukamyatā</h2>

**en** `952112–952162`
<h2>(b) Not wishing to hear the good teaching</h2>

### 1436

**pi** `645854–646205`
Tattha katamā saddhammaṃ asotukamyatā? Tattha katamo saddhammo? Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro iddhipādā, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅgā, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo – ayaṃ vuccati "saddhammo". Yā imassa saddhammassa asotukamyatā asavanakamyatā anuggahetukamyatā adhāretukamyatā – ayaṃ vuccati "saddhammaṃ asotukamyatā".

**en** `952163–952664`
Therein, what is not wishing to hear the good teaching? Therein, what is the good teaching? The four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of success, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, the noble eightfold path — this is called "the good teaching". The not wishing to hear this good teaching, the not wishing to listen to it, the not wishing to learn it, the not wishing to retain it — this is called "not wishing to hear the good teaching".

### 1437

**pi** `646206–646236`
<h2>(Ga) upārambhacittatā</h2>

**en** `952665–952698`
<h2>(c) A fault-finding mind</h2>

### 1438

**pi** `646237–646434`
Tattha katamā upārambhacittatā? Tattha katamo upārambho? Yo upārambho anupārambho upārambhanā anupārambhanā anupārambhitattaṃ uññā avaññā paribhavo randhagavesitā – ayaṃ vuccati "upārambhacittatā".

**en** `952699–953009`
Therein, what is a fault-finding mind? Therein, what is fault-finding? The fault-finding, constant fault-finding, being a fault-finder, constantly finding fault, the state of constant fault-finding, the contempt, the scorn, the disparagement, the seeking of weak points — this is called "a fault-finding mind".

### 1439

**pi** `646435–646466`
<h2>(34. Ka) muṭṭhassaccaṃ</h2>

**en** `953010–953038`
<h2>(34a) Forgetfulness</h2>

### 1440

**pi** `646467–646613`
Tattha katamaṃ muṭṭhassaccaṃ? Yā assati ananussati appaṭissati assati assaraṇatā adhāraṇatā pilāpanatā sammusanatā – idaṃ vuccati "muṭṭhassaccaṃ".

**en** `953039–953268`
Therein, what is forgetfulness? The absence of mindfulness, absence of recollection, absence of remembering; the absence of mindfulness, the not bearing in mind, the floating away, the forgetting — this is called "forgetfulness".

### 1441

**pi** `646614–646641`
<h2>(Kha) asampajaññaṃ</h2>

**en** `953269–953309`
<h2>(b) Lack of clear comprehension</h2>

### 1442

**pi** `646642–646758`
Tattha katamaṃ asampajaññaṃ? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ …pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "asampajaññaṃ".

**en** `953310–953499`
Therein, what is lack of clear comprehension? The lack of knowledge, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "lack of clear comprehension".

### 1443

**pi** `646759–646788`
<h2>(Ga) cetaso vikkhepo</h2>

**en** `953500–953532`
<h2>(c) Distraction of mind</h2>

### 1444

**pi** `646789–646922`
Tattha katamo cetaso vikkhepo? Yaṃ cittassa uddhaccaṃ avūpasamo cetaso vikkhepo bhantattaṃ cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati "cetaso vikkhepo".

**en** `953533–953696`
Therein, what is distraction of mind? The restlessness of the mind, lack of calm, mental distraction, agitation of the mind — this is called "distraction of mind".

### 1445

**pi** `646923–646959`
<h2>(35. Ka) ayoniso manasikāro</h2>

**en** `953697–953728`
<h2>(35a) Unwise attention</h2>

### 1446

**pi** `646960–647263`
Tattha katamo ayoniso manasikāro? Anicce "nicca"nti ayoniso manasikāro, dukkhe "sukha"nti ayoniso manasikāro, anattani "attā"ti ayoniso manasikāro, asubhe "subha"nti ayoniso manasikāro, saccavippaṭikulena vā cittassa āvaṭṭanā anāvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro – ayaṃ vuccati "ayoniso manasikāro".

**en** `953729–954125`
Therein, what is unwise attention? Unwise attention taking the impermanent as "permanent", unwise attention taking the painful as "pleasant", unwise attention taking what is not self as "self", unwise attention taking the unattractive as "attractive"; or the turning of the mind, repeated turning, engagement, bringing-to-mind, attention contrary to the truth — this is called "unwise attention".

### 1447

**pi** `647264–647293`
<h2>(Kha) kummaggasevanā</h2>

**en** `954126–954163`
<h2>(b) Following the wrong path</h2>

### 1448

**pi** `647294–647618`
Tattha katamā kummaggasevanā? Tattha katamo kummaggo? Micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati "kummaggo". Yā imassa kummaggassa sevanā nisevanā saṃsevanā bhajanā sambhajanā bhatti sambhatti taṃsampavaṅkatā – ayaṃ vuccati "kummaggasevanā".

**en** `954164–954632`
Therein, what is following the wrong path? Therein, what is the wrong path? Wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration — this is called "the wrong path". The resorting to this wrong path, the frequenting, the close frequenting, the associating with it, the fully associating, the devotion, the full devotion, the being inclined towards it — this is called "following the wrong path".

### 1449

**pi** `647619–647651`
<h2>(Ga) cetaso ca līnattaṃ</h2>

**en** `954633–954666`
<h2>(c) Sluggishness of mind</h2>

### 1450

**pi** `647652–647834`
Tattha katamaṃ cetaso ca līnattaṃ? Yā cittassa akalyatā akammaññatā olīyanā sallīyanā līnaṃ līyanā līyitattaṃ thinaṃ thiyanā thiyitattaṃ cittassa – idaṃ vuccati "cetaso ca līnattaṃ".

**en** `954667–954922`
Therein, what is sluggishness of mind? The mind's lack of readiness, its unworkableness, its sagging, its slumping; sloth, being slothful, the mind's slothfulness; dullness, being dull, the mind's state of dullness — this is called "sluggishness of mind".

### 1451

**pi** `647835–647841`
Tikaṃ.

**en** `954923–954934`
The Threes.

### 1452

**pi** `647842–647868`
<h1>4. Catukkaniddeso</h1>

**en** `954935–954974`
<h1>4. The Exposition of the Fours</h1>

### 1453

**pi** `647869–647895`
<h2>(1) Cattāro āsavā</h2>

**en** `954975–955010`
<h2>(1) The four mental taints</h2>

### 1454

**pi** `647896–647969`
Tattha katame cattāro āsavā? Kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, diṭṭhāsavo, avijjāsavo.

**en** `955011–955149`
Therein, what are the four mental taints? The taint of sense pleasure, the taint of existence, the taint of views, the taint of ignorance.

### 1455

**pi** `647970–647992`
<h2>(Ka) kāmāsavo</h2>

**en** `955150–955190`
<h2>(a) The taint of sense pleasure</h2>

### 1456

**pi** `647993–648143`
Tattha katamo kāmāsavo? Yo kāmesu kāmacchando kāmarāgo kāmanandī kāmataṇhā kāmasineho kāmapariḷāho kāmamucchā kāmajjhosānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "kāmāsavo".

**en** `955191–955584`
Therein, what is the taint of sense pleasure? The desire for sense pleasures with regard to sense pleasures, the lust for sense pleasures, the delight in sense pleasures, the craving for sense pleasures, the affection for sense pleasures, the burning for sense pleasures, the infatuation with sense pleasures, the holding fast to sense pleasures — this is called "the taint of sense pleasure".

### 1457

**pi** `648144–648168`
<h2>(Kha) bhavāsavo</h2>

**en** `955585–955620`
<h2>(b) The taint of existence</h2>

### 1458

**pi** `648169–648264`
Tattha katamo bhavāsavo? Yo bhavesu bhavacchando…pe… bhavajjhosānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "bhavāsavo".

**en** `955621–955795`
Therein, what is the taint of existence? The desire for existence with regard to states of existence… the holding fast to existence — this is called "the taint of existence".

### 1459

**pi** `648265–648289`
<h2>(Ga) diṭṭhāsavo</h2>

**en** `955796–955827`
<h2>(c) The taint of views</h2>

### 1460

**pi** `648290–648753`
Tattha katamo diṭṭhāsavo? "Sassato loko"ti vā, "asassato loko"ti vā, "antavā loko"ti vā, "anantavā loko"ti vā, "taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra"nti vā, "aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra"nti vā, "hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā"ti vā, "na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā"ti vā, "hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā"ti vā, "neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā"ti vā. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati "diṭṭhāsavo". Sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi diṭṭhāsavo.

**en** `955828–956420`
Therein, what is the taint of views? "The world is eternal", or "the world is not eternal", or "the world is finite", or "the world is infinite", or "the soul and the body are the same", or "the soul is one thing and the body another", or "a Tathāgata exists after death", or "a Tathāgata does not exist after death", or "a Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death", or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death". Whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "the taint of views". All wrong view is the taint of views.

### 1461

**pi** `648754–648779`
<h2>(Gha) avijjāsavo</h2>

**en** `956421–956456`
<h2>(d) The taint of ignorance</h2>

### 1462

**pi** `648780–649137`
Tattha katamo avijjāsavo? Dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ , dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ, pubbante aññāṇaṃ, aparante aññāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante aññāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇaṃ. Yaṃ evarūpaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "avijjāsavo". Ime cattāro āsavā.

**en** `956457–957019`
Therein, what is the taint of ignorance? Not knowing suffering, not knowing the origin of suffering, not knowing the cessation of suffering, not knowing the way leading to the cessation of suffering; not knowing the past, not knowing the future, not knowing the past and the future; not knowing things that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality. Whatever lack of knowledge of this kind there is, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "the taint of ignorance". These are the four mental taints.

### 1463

**pi** `649138–649169`
<h2>(2-5) Cattāro ganthādī</h2>

**en** `957020–957061`
<h2>(2-5) The four ties and the rest</h2>

### 1464

**pi** `649170–649319`
Tattha katame cattāro ganthā …pe… cattāro oghā…pe… cattāro yogā…pe… cattāri upādānāni? Kāmupādānaṃ, diṭṭhupādānaṃ, sīlabbatupādānaṃ, attavādupādānaṃ.

**en** `957062–957270`
Therein, what are the four ties… the four floods… the four yokes… the four kinds of clinging? Clinging to sense pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, clinging to a doctrine of self.

### 1465

**pi** `649320–649345`
<h2>(Ka) kāmupādānaṃ</h2>

**en** `957271–957311`
<h2>(a) Clinging to sense pleasures</h2>

### 1466

**pi** `649346–649443`
Tattha katamaṃ kāmupādānaṃ? Yo kāmesu kāmacchando…pe… kāmajjhosānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati "kāmupādānaṃ".

**en** `957312–957504`
Therein, what is clinging to sense pleasures? The desire for sense pleasures with regard to sense pleasures… the holding fast to sense pleasures — this is called "clinging to sense pleasures".

### 1467

**pi** `649444–649472`
<h2>(Kha) diṭṭhupādānaṃ</h2>

**en** `957505–957535`
<h2>(b) Clinging to views</h2>

### 1468

**pi** `649473–649771`
Tattha katamaṃ diṭṭhupādānaṃ? "Natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī"ti. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati "diṭṭhupādānaṃ". Ṭhapetvā sīlabbatupādānañca attavādupādānañca sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi diṭṭhupādānaṃ.

**en** `957536–957956`
Therein, what is clinging to views? "There is nothing given, there is nothing offered… who declare this world and the other world, having realised them for themselves by direct knowledge." Whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "clinging to views". Setting aside clinging to rules and observances and clinging to a doctrine of self, all wrong view is clinging to views.

### 1469

**pi** `649772–649802`
<h2>(Ga) sīlabbatupādānaṃ</h2>

**en** `957957–958003`
<h2>(c) Clinging to rules and observances</h2>

### 1470

**pi** `649803–650001`
Tattha katamaṃ sīlabbatupādānaṃ? Ito bahiddhā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ sīlena suddhi vatena suddhi sīlabbatena suddhīti. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati "sīlabbatupādānaṃ".

**en** `958004–958339`
Therein, what is clinging to rules and observances? "Purity comes through virtue, purity comes through observances, purity comes through virtue-and-observances of ascetics and brahmins outside this teaching." Whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "clinging to rules and observances".

### 1471

**pi** `650002–650032`
<h2>(Gha) attavādupādānaṃ</h2>

**en** `958340–958383`
<h2>(d) Clinging to a doctrine of self</h2>

### 1472

**pi** `650033–650555`
Tattha katamaṃ attavādupādānaṃ? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto – rūpaṃ attato samanupassati rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ attani vā rūpaṃ rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ attani vā viññāṇaṃ viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – idaṃ vuccati "attavādupādānaṃ". Imāni cattāri upādānāni.

**en** `958384–959172`
Therein, what is clinging to a doctrine of self? Here an unlearned ordinary person — who has no regard for the noble ones, is unskilled in the teaching of the noble ones, untrained in the teaching of the noble ones; who has no regard for good people, is unskilled in the teaching of good people, untrained in the teaching of good people — regards material form as self, or self as possessing material form, or material form as in self, or self as in material form. He regards feeling… perception… formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "clinging to a doctrine of self". These are the four kinds of clinging.

### 1473

**pi** `650556–650587`
<h2>(6) Cattāro taṇhuppādā</h2>

**en** `959173–959214`
<h2>(6) The four arisings of craving</h2>

### 1474

**pi** `650588–650870`
Tattha katame cattāro taṇhuppādā? Cīvarahetu vā bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, piṇḍapātahetu vā bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, senāsanahetu vā bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, itibhavābhavahetu vā bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati – ime cattāro taṇhuppādā.

**en** `959215–959580`
Therein, what are the four arisings of craving? Craving, when it arises in a monk, arises because of robes; craving, when it arises in a monk, arises because of alms-food; craving, when it arises in a monk, arises because of a dwelling place; craving, when it arises in a monk, arises because of this or that state of being — these are the four arisings of craving.

### 1475

**pi** `650871–650905`
<h2>(7) Cattāri agatigamanāni</h2>

**en** `959581–959623`
<h2>(7) The four ways of going astray</h2>

### 1476

**pi** `650906–651127`
Tattha katamāni cattāri agatigamanāni? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati. Yā evarūpā agati agatigamanaṃ chandagamanaṃ vaggagamanaṃ vārigamanaṃ – imāni cattāri agatigamanāni.

**en** `959624–959956`
Therein, what are the four ways of going astray? One goes astray through desire, one goes astray through hate, one goes astray through delusion, one goes astray through fear. Whatever going astray of this kind there is, the wrong course, going by desire, going by faction, going by evasion — these are the four ways of going astray.

### 1477

**pi** `651128–651159`
<h2>(8) Cattāro vipariyāsā</h2>

**en** `959957–959990`
<h2>(8) The four distortions</h2>

### 1478

**pi** `651160–651490`
Tattha katame cattāro vipariyāsā? Anicce "nicca"nti saññāvipariyāso cittavipariyāso diṭṭhivipariyāso, dukkhe "sukha"nti saññāvipariyāso cittavipariyāso diṭṭhivipariyāso, anattani "attā"ti saññāvipariyāso cittavipariyāso diṭṭhivipariyāso, asubhe "subha"nti saññāvipariyāso cittavipariyāso diṭṭhivipariyāso – ime cattāro vipariyāsā.

**en** `959991–960508`
Therein, what are the four distortions? Taking the impermanent as "permanent" is a distortion of perception, a distortion of mind, a distortion of view; taking the painful as "pleasant" is a distortion of perception, a distortion of mind, a distortion of view; taking what is not self as "self" is a distortion of perception, a distortion of mind, a distortion of view; taking the unattractive as "attractive" is a distortion of perception, a distortion of mind, a distortion of view — these are the four distortions.

### 1479

**pi** `651491–651525`
<h2>(9) Cattāro anariyavohārā</h2>

**en** `960509–960553`
<h2>(9) The four ignoble ways of speech</h2>

### 1480

**pi** `651526–651673`
Tattha katame cattāro anariyavohārā? Adiṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā, assute sutavāditā, amute mutavāditā, aviññāte viññātavāditā – ime cattāro anariyavohārā.

**en** `960554–960828`
Therein, what are the four ignoble ways of speech? Saying one has seen what one has not seen, saying one has heard what one has not heard, saying one has sensed what one has not sensed, saying one has known what one has not known — these are the four ignoble ways of speech.

### 1481

**pi** `651674–651717`
<h2>(10) Aparepi cattāro anariyavohārā</h2>

**en** `960829–960878`
<h2>(10) Another four ignoble ways of speech</h2>

### 1482

**pi** `651718–651873`
Tattha katame aparepi cattāro anariyavohārā? Diṭṭhe adiṭṭhavāditā, sute assutavāditā, mute amutavāditā, viññāte aviññātavāditā – ime cattāro anariyavohārā.

**en** `960879–961157`
Therein, what are another four ignoble ways of speech? Saying one has not seen what one has seen, saying one has not heard what one has heard, saying one has not sensed what one has sensed, saying one has not known what one has known — these are the four ignoble ways of speech.

### 1483

**pi** `651874–651907`
<h2>(11) Cattāri duccaritāni</h2>

**en** `961158–961200`
<h2>(11) The four kinds of misconduct</h2>

### 1484

**pi** `651908–652025`
Tattha katamāni cattāri duccaritāni? Pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo – imāni cattāri duccaritāni.

**en** `961201–961371`
Therein, what are the four kinds of misconduct? Killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech — these are the four kinds of misconduct.

### 1485

**pi** `652026–652069`
<h2>(12) Aparānipi cattāri duccaritāni</h2>

**en** `961372–961418`
<h2>(12) Another four kinds of misconduct</h2>

### 1486

**pi** `652070–652196`
Tattha katamāni aparānipi cattāri duccaritāni? Musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo – imāni cattāri duccaritāni.

**en** `961419–961570`
Therein, what are another four kinds of misconduct? False speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, idle chatter — these are the four kinds of misconduct.

### 1487

**pi** `652197–652226`
<h2>(13) Cattāri bhayāni</h2>

**en** `961571–961599`
<h2>(13) The four fears</h2>

### 1488

**pi** `652227–652335`
Tattha katamāni cattāri bhayāni? Jātibhayaṃ, jarābhayaṃ, byādhibhayaṃ, maraṇabhayaṃ – imāni cattāri bhayāni.

**en** `961600–961739`
Therein, what are the four fears? The fear of birth, the fear of aging, the fear of sickness, the fear of death — these are the four fears.

### 1489

**pi** `652336–652375`
<h2>(14) Aparānipi cattāri bhayāni</h2>

**en** `961740–961772`
<h2>(14) Another four fears</h2>

### 1490

**pi** `652376–652491`
Tattha katamāni aparānipi cattāri bhayāni? Rājabhayaṃ, corabhayaṃ, aggibhayaṃ, udakabhayaṃ – imāni cattāri bhayāni.

**en** `961773–961914`
Therein, what are another four fears? The fear of kings, the fear of thieves, the fear of fire, the fear of water — these are the four fears.

### 1491

**pi** `652492–652677`
Tattha katamāni aparānipi cattāri bhayāni? Ūmibhayaṃ, kumbhīlabhayaṃ [kumbhīrabhayaṃ, kumbhīḷabhayaṃ (?) (kumbha + īra + a = bhaya)], āvaṭṭabhayaṃ, susukābhayaṃ – imāni cattāri bhayāni.

**en** `961915–962066`
Therein, what are another four fears? The fear of waves, the fear of crocodiles, the fear of whirlpools, the fear of sharks — these are the four fears.

### 1492

**pi** `652678–652808`
Tattha katamāni aparānipi cattāri bhayāni? Attānuvādabhayaṃ, parānuvādabhayaṃ, daṇḍabhayaṃ, duggatibhayaṃ – imāni cattāri bhayāni.

**en** `962067–962243`
Therein, what are another four fears? The fear of self-reproach, the fear of others' reproach, the fear of punishment, the fear of a bad destination — these are the four fears.

### 1493

**pi** `652809–652839`
<h2>(15) Catasso diṭṭhiyo</h2>

**en** `962244–962272`
<h2>(15) The four views</h2>

### 1494

**pi** `652840–653189`
Tattha katamā catasso diṭṭhiyo? "Sayaṅkataṃ sukhadukkha"nti saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati, "paraṅkataṃ sukhadukkha"nti saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati, "sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca sukhadukkha"nti saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati, "asayaṅkāraṃ aparaṅkāraṃ adhiccasamuppannaṃ sukhadukkha"nti saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati – imā catasso diṭṭhiyo.

**en** `962273–962750`
Therein, what are the four views? The view arises as true and established, "Happiness and suffering are made by oneself"; the view arises as true and established, "Happiness and suffering are made by another"; the view arises as true and established, "Happiness and suffering are made both by oneself and by another"; the view arises as true and established, "Happiness and suffering are made neither by oneself nor by another, but arisen by chance" — these are the four views.

### 1495

**pi** `653190–653199`
Catukkaṃ.

**en** `962751–962761`
The Fours.

### 1496

**pi** `653200–653226`
<h1>5. Pañcakaniddeso</h1>

**en** `962762–962801`
<h1>5. The Exposition of the Fives</h1>

### 1497

**pi** `653227–653269`
<h2>(1) Pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni</h2>

**en** `962802–962837`
<h2>(1) The five lower fetters</h2>

### 1498

**pi** `653270–653422`
Tattha katamāni pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni? Sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso, kāmacchando, byāpādo – imāni pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni.

**en** `962838–963019`
Therein, what are the five lower fetters? The view of a self in the body, doubt, wrong grasping of virtue and observances, sense desire, ill will — these are the five lower fetters.

### 1499

**pi** `653423–653467`
<h2>(2) Pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni</h2>

**en** `963020–963056`
<h2>(2) The five higher fetters</h2>

### 1500

**pi** `653468–653602`
Tattha katamāni pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni? Rūparāgo, arūparāgo, māno, uddhaccaṃ, avijjā – imāni pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni.

**en** `963057–963218`
Therein, what are the five higher fetters? Lust for material form, lust for the immaterial, conceit, restlessness, ignorance — these are the five higher fetters.

### 1501

**pi** `653603–653634`
<h2>(3) Pañca macchariyāni</h2>

**en** `963219–963260`
<h2>(3) The five kinds of stinginess</h2>

### 1502

**pi** `653635–653787`
Tattha katamāni pañca macchariyāni? Āvāsamacchariyaṃ, kulamacchariyaṃ, lābhamacchariyaṃ, vaṇṇamacchariyaṃ, dhammamacchariyaṃ – imāni pañca macchariyāni.

**en** `963261–963484`
Therein, what are the five kinds of stinginess? Stinginess about dwellings, stinginess about families, stinginess about gains, stinginess about praise, stinginess about the teaching — these are the five kinds of stinginess.

### 1503

**pi** `653788–653812`
<h2>(4) Pañca saṅgā</h2>

**en** `963485–963518`
<h2>(4) The five attachments</h2>

### 1504

**pi** `653813–653914`
Tattha katame pañca saṅgā? Rāgasaṅgo, dosasaṅgo, mohasaṅgo, mānasaṅgo, diṭṭhisaṅgo – ime pañca saṅgā.

**en** `963519–963719`
Therein, what are the five attachments? The attachment of lust, the attachment of hate, the attachment of delusion, the attachment of conceit, the attachment of views — these are the five attachments.

### 1505

**pi** `653915–653939`
<h2>(5) Pañca sallā</h2>

**en** `963720–963747`
<h2>(5) The five darts</h2>

### 1506

**pi** `653940–654046`
Tattha katame pañca sallā? Rāgasallaṃ, dosasallaṃ, mohasallaṃ, mānasallaṃ, diṭṭhisallaṃ – ime pañca sallā.

**en** `963748–963906`
Therein, what are the five darts? The dart of lust, the dart of hate, the dart of delusion, the dart of conceit, the dart of views — these are the five darts.

### 1507

**pi** `654047–654075`
<h2>(6) Pañca cetokhilā</h2>

**en** `963907–963949`
<h2>(6) The five barrennesses of mind</h2>

### 1508

**pi** `654076–654424`
Tattha katame pañca cetokhilā? Satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, dhamme kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, saṅghe kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, sikkhāya kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto – ime pañca cetokhilā.

**en** `963950–964529`
Therein, what are the five barrennesses of mind? One doubts and is perplexed about the Teacher, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; one doubts and is perplexed about the teaching, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; one doubts and is perplexed about the Order, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; one doubts and is perplexed about the training, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; one is angry with one's companions in the holy life, displeased, with a struck-down mind, become barren — these are the five barrennesses of mind.

### 1509

**pi** `654425–654461`
<h2>(7) Pañca cetaso vinibandhā</h2>

**en** `964530–964568`
<h2>(7) The five bondages of mind</h2>

### 1510

**pi** `654462–654906`
Tattha katame pañca cetaso vinibandhā? Kāme avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho; kāye avītarāgo hoti… rūpe avītarāgo hoti… yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati; aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – "imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā"ti – ime pañca cetasovinibandhā.

**en** `964569–965189`
Therein, what are the five bondages of mind? One is not without lust for sense pleasures, not without desire, not without affection, not without thirst, not without burning, not without craving; one is not without lust for the body… one is not without lust for material form… having eaten as much as one's belly will hold, one dwells devoted to the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of lolling, the pleasure of sleep; one lives the holy life aspiring to some order of gods — "By this virtue, or observance, or austerity, or holy life, I shall become a god or one among the gods" — these are the five bondages of mind.

### 1511

**pi** `654907–654936`
<h2>(8) Pañca nīvaraṇāni</h2>

**en** `965190–965222`
<h2>(8) The five hindrances</h2>

### 1512

**pi** `654937–655105`
Tattha katamāni pañca nīvaraṇāni? Kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ, byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ, thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṃ, vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ – imāni pañca nīvaraṇāni.

**en** `965223–965460`
Therein, what are the five hindrances? The hindrance of sense desire, the hindrance of ill will, the hindrance of dullness and drowsiness, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, the hindrance of doubt — these are the five hindrances.

### 1513

**pi** `655106–655145`
<h2>(9) Pañca kammāni ānantarikāni</h2>

**en** `965461–965512`
<h2>(9) The five actions with immediate result</h2>

### 1514

**pi** `655146–655384`
Tattha katamāni pañca kammāni ānantarikāni? Mātā jīvitā voropitā hoti, pitā jīvitā voropito hoti, arahanto jīvitā voropito hoti, duṭṭhena cittena tathāgatassa lohitaṃ uppāditaṃ hoti , saṅgho bhinno hoti – imāni pañca kammāni ānantarikāni.

**en** `965513–965827`
Therein, what are the five actions with immediate result? One's mother has been deprived of life, one's father has been deprived of life, an arahant has been deprived of life, the blood of a Tathāgata has been shed with a mind of hatred, the Order has been split — these are the five actions with immediate result.

### 1515

**pi** `655385–655413`
<h2>(10) Pañca diṭṭhiyo</h2>

**en** `965828–965856`
<h2>(10) The five views</h2>

### 1516

**pi** `655414–655760`
Tattha katamā pañca diṭṭhiyo? "Saññī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti ittheke abhivadanti, "asaññī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti ittheke abhivadanti, "nevasaññīnāsaññī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti ittheke abhivadanti, sato vā pana sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññāpenti, diṭṭhadhammanibbānaṃ vā paneke abhivadanti – imā pañca diṭṭhiyo.

**en** `965857–966279`
Therein, what are the five views? Some declare, "The self is percipient and unimpaired after death"; some declare, "The self is non-percipient and unimpaired after death"; some declare, "The self is neither percipient nor non-percipient and unimpaired after death"; or they proclaim the cutting off, destruction, and non-existence of an existing being; or some declare Nibbāna in this very life — these are the five views.

### 1517

**pi** `655761–655785`
<h2>(11) Pañca verā</h2>

**en** `966280–966314`
<h2>(11) The five hostilities</h2>

### 1518

**pi** `655786–655910`
Tattha katame pañca verā? Pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā – ime pañca verā.

**en** `966315–966525`
Therein, what are the five hostilities? Killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, wine, spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness — these are the five hostilities.

### 1519

**pi** `655911–655938`
<h2>(12) Pañca byasanā</h2>

**en** `966526–966555`
<h2>(12) The five losses</h2>

### 1520

**pi** `655939–656060`
Tattha katame pañca byasanā? Ñātibyasanaṃ, bhogabyasanaṃ, rogabyasanaṃ, sīlabyasanaṃ, diṭṭhibyasanaṃ – ime pañca byasanā.

**en** `966556–966705`
Therein, what are the five losses? Loss of relatives, loss of wealth, loss through illness, loss of virtue, loss of view — these are the five losses.

### 1521

**pi** `656061–656099`
<h2>(13) Pañca akkhantiyā ādīnavā</h2>

**en** `966706–966750`
<h2>(13) The five dangers of impatience</h2>

### 1522

**pi** `656100–656337`
Tattha katame pañca akkhantiyā ādīnavā? Bahuno janassa appiyo hoti amanāpo, verabahulo ca hoti, vajjabahulo ca, sammūḷho kālaṅkaroti, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati – ime pañca akkhantiyā ādīnavā.

**en** `966751–967072`
Therein, what are the five dangers of impatience? One is disliked and displeasing to many people; one has much hostility; one has many faults; one dies confused; with the breakup of the body after death one is reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, hell — these are the five dangers of impatience.

### 1523

**pi** `656338–656365`
<h2>(14) Pañca bhayāni</h2>

**en** `967073–967101`
<h2>(14) The five fears</h2>

### 1524

**pi** `656366–656498`
Tattha katamāni pañca bhayāni? Ājīvakabhayaṃ, asilokabhayaṃ, parisasārajjabhayaṃ, maraṇabhayaṃ, duggatibhayaṃ – imāni pañca bhayāni.

**en** `967102–967298`
Therein, what are the five fears? The fear about livelihood, the fear of disrepute, the fear of timidity in assemblies, the fear of death, the fear of a bad destination — these are the five fears.

### 1525

**pi** `656499–656542`
<h2>(15) Pañca diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādā</h2>

**en** `967299–967360`
<h2>(15) The five doctrines of Nibbāna in this very life</h2>

### 1526

**pi** `656543–658838`
Tattha katame pañca diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādā? ⤵ (Ka) idhekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī hoti evaṃdiṭṭhi [evaṃdiṭṭhi (syā.)] – "yato kho, bho , ayaṃ attā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti, ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānaṃ paññapenti. ⤵ (Kha) tamañño evamāha – "atthi kho, bho, eso attā yaṃ tvaṃ vadesi neso natthīti vadāmi. No ca kho, bho, ayaṃ attā ettāvatā paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto hoti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Kāmā hi, bho, aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā. Tesaṃ vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā. Yato kho, bho, ayaṃ attā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānaṃ paññapenti. ⤵ (Ga) tamañño evamāha – "atthi kho, bho, eso attā yaṃ tvaṃ vadesi. Neso natthīti vadāmi. No ca kho, bho, ayaṃ attā ettāvatā paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto hoti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yadeva tattha vitakkitaṃ vicāritaṃ etena etaṃ oḷārikaṃ akkhāyati. Yato kho, bho, ayaṃ attā vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānaṃ paññapenti. ⤵ (Gha) tamañño evamāha – "atthi kho, bho, eso attā yaṃ tvaṃ vadesi. Neso natthīti vadāmi. No ca kho, bho, ayaṃ attā ettāvatā paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto hoti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yadeva tattha pītigataṃ cetaso uppilāvitaṃ, etena etaṃ oḷārikaṃ akkhāyati. Yato kho, bho, ayaṃ attā pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānaṃ paññapenti. ⤵ (Ṅa) tamañño evamāha – "atthi kho, bho, eso attā yaṃ tvaṃ vadesi. Neso natthīti vadāmi. No ca kho, bho, ayaṃ attā ettāvatā paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto hoti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yadeva tattha sukhapīti cetaso ābhogo, etena etaṃ oḷārikaṃ akkhāyati. Yato kho, bho, ayaṃ attā sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānaṃ paññapenti. Ime pañca diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādā.

**en** `967361–970189`
Therein, what are the five doctrines of Nibbāna in this very life? ⤵ (a) Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "When this self, sir, furnished and provided with the five strands of sense pleasure, amuses itself, to that extent, sir, this self has reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life." Thus some declare the highest Nibbāna in this very life of an existing being. ⤵ (b) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, has not to that extent reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life. Why is that? Because, sir, sense pleasures are impermanent, painful, and subject to change; with their change and alteration arise sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. When this self, sir, secluded from sense pleasures… enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, to that extent, sir, this self has reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life." Thus some declare the highest Nibbāna in this very life of an existing being. ⤵ (c) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, has not to that extent reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life. Why is that? Because whatever there is of thought and examination there, by that it is reckoned gross. When this self, sir, with the stilling of thought and examination… enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption, to that extent, sir, this self has reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life." Thus some declare the highest Nibbāna in this very life of an existing being. ⤵ (d) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, has not to that extent reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life. Why is that? Because whatever there is of joy and mental elation there, by that it is reckoned gross. When this self, sir, with the fading away of joy… enters and dwells in the third meditative absorption, to that extent, sir, this self has reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life." Thus some declare the highest Nibbāna in this very life of an existing being. ⤵ (e) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, has not to that extent reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life. Why is that? Because whatever there is of the mind's engagement with happiness and joy there, by that it is reckoned gross. When this self, sir, with the abandoning of happiness… enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption, to that extent, sir, this self has reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life." Thus some declare the highest Nibbāna in this very life of an existing being. These are the five doctrines of Nibbāna in this very life.

### 1544

**pi** `660587–660884`
Tattha katame cha somanassupavicārā? Cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā somanassaṭṭhāniyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati, sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya somanassaṭṭhāniyaṃ dhammaṃ upavicarati – ime cha somanassupavicārā.

**en** `972750–973177`
Therein, what are the six explorations with joy? Having seen a sight with the eye, one explores a sight that is a basis for joy; having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled a smell with the nose… having tasted a taste with the tongue… having touched a tangible thing with the body… having known a mental object with the mind, one explores a mental object that is a basis for joy — these are the six explorations with joy.

Tattha katame cha domanassupavicārā? Cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā domanassaṭṭhāniyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati, sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā …pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya domanassaṭṭhāniyaṃ dhammaṃ upavicarati – ime cha domanassupavicārā.

### 1550

**pi** `661584–662033`
Tattha katamāni cha gehasitāni somanassāni? Manāpiyesu rūpesu gehasitaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā, manāpiyesu saddesu…pe… manāpiyesu gandhesu…pe… manāpiyesu rasesu…pe… manāpiyesu phoṭṭhabbesu…pe… manāpiyesu dhammesu gehasitaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – imāni cha gehasitāni somanassāni.

**en** `974211–974854`
Therein, what are the six kinds of household joy? Concerning pleasing sights: the mental comfort connected with the household life, the mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact; concerning pleasing sounds… concerning pleasing smells… concerning pleasing tastes… concerning pleasing tangible things… concerning pleasing mental objects: the mental comfort connected with the household life, the mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact — these are the six kinds of household joy.

### 1552

**pi** `662075–662542`
Tattha katamāni cha gehasitāni domanassāni? Amanāpiyesu rūpesu gehasitaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā, amanāpiyesu saddesu…pe… amanāpiyesu gandhesu…pe… amanāpiyesu rasesu…pe… amanāpiyesu phoṭṭhabbesu…pe… amanāpiyesu dhammesu gehasitaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – imāni cha gehasitāni domanassāni.

**en** `974902–975579`
Therein, what are the six kinds of household grief? Concerning displeasing sights: the mental discomfort connected with the household life, the mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact; concerning displeasing sounds… concerning displeasing smells… concerning displeasing tastes… concerning displeasing tangible things… concerning displeasing mental objects: the mental discomfort connected with the household life, the mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact — these are the six kinds of household grief.

### 1553

**pi** `662543–662577`

<h2>(13) The six kinds of household equanimity</h2>

### 1554

**pi** `662578–663059`
Tattha katamā cha gehasitā upekkhā? Upekkhāṭṭhāniyesu rūpesu gehasitaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā, upekkhāṭṭhāniyesu saddesu…pe… upekkhāṭṭhāniyesu gandhesu…pe… upekkhāṭṭhāniyesu rasesu…pe… upekkhāṭṭhāniyesu phoṭṭhabbesu…pe… upekkhāṭṭhāniyesu dhammesu gehasitaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – imā cha gehasitā upekkhā.

**en** `975632–976525`
Therein, what are the six kinds of household equanimity? Concerning sights that are a basis for equanimity: the mental experience connected with the household life that is neither comfortable nor uncomfortable, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant experience born of mind-contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mind-contact; concerning sounds that are a basis for equanimity… concerning smells that are a basis for equanimity… concerning tastes that are a basis for equanimity… concerning tangible things that are a basis for equanimity… concerning mental objects that are a basis for equanimity: the mental experience connected with the household life that is neither comfortable nor uncomfortable, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant experience born of mind-contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mind-contact — these are the six kinds of household equanimity.

### 1555

**pi** `663060–663086`
<h2>(14) Cha diṭṭhiyo</h2>

**en** `976526–976553`
<h2>(14) The six views</h2>

### 1556

**pi** `663087–663746`
Tattha katamā cha diṭṭhiyo? "Atthi me attā"ti vā assa saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati, "natthi me attā"ti vā assa saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati, "attanā vā attānaṃ sañjānāmī"ti vā assa saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati, "attanā vā anattānaṃ sañjānāmī"ti vā assa saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati, "anattanā vā attānaṃ sañjānāmī"ti vā assa saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati; atha vā panassa evaṃdiṭṭhi hoti – "so me ayaṃ attā vado vedeyyo tatra tatra dīgharattaṃ kalyāṇapāpakānaṃ kammānaṃ vipākaṃ paccanubhoti. Na so jāto nāhosi, na so jāto na bhavissati, nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo"ti vā panassa saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati. Imā cha diṭṭhiyo.

**en** `976554–977343`
Therein, what are the six views? The view arises in one as true and established, "There is a self for me"; or the view arises in one as true and established, "There is no self for me"; or the view arises in one as true and established, "By self I perceive self"; or the view arises in one as true and established, "By self I perceive non-self"; or the view arises in one as true and established, "By non-self I perceive self"; or else one holds a view like this: "It is this self of mine that speaks and feels, that experiences here and there the result of good and evil actions. It was not born and did not exist before; it was not born and will not exist; it is permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change" — the view arises in one as true and established. These are the six views.

### 1572

**pi** `664983–668369`
(Ka) tattha katamā satta diṭṭhiyo? Idhekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī hoti evaṃdiṭṭhi – "yato kho, bho, ayaṃ attā rūpī cātumahābhūtiko [cātummahābhūtiko (sī. syā.)] mātāpettikasambhavo kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā, ettāvatā kho bho, ayaṃ attā sammā samucchinno hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññapenti. ⤵ (Kha) tamañño evamāha – "atthi kho, bho, eso attā yaṃ tvaṃ vadesi. ‘Neso natthī’ti vadāmi. No ca kho, bho, ayaṃ attā ettāvatā sammā samucchinno hoti. Atthi kho bho añño attā dibbo rūpī kāmāvacaro kabaḷīkārabhakkho. Taṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi na passasi. Tamahaṃ jānāmi passāmi. So kho, bho, attā yato kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā, ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā sammāsamucchinno hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññapenti. ⤵ (Ga) tamañño evamāha – "atthi kho, bho, eso attā yaṃ tvaṃ vadesi. ‘Neso natthī’ti vadāmi. No ca kho, bho, ayaṃ attā ettāvatā sammā samucchinno hoti. Atthi kho, bho, añño attā dibbo rūpī manomayo sabbaṅgapaccaṅgī ahīnindriyo. Taṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi na passasi. Tamahaṃ jānāmi passāmi. So kho, bho, attā yato kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā, ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā sammā samucchinno hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññapenti. ⤵ (Gha) tamañño evamāha – "atthi kho, bho, eso attā yaṃ tvaṃ vadesi. ‘Neso natthī’ti vadāmi. No ca kho, bho, ayaṃ attā ettāvatā sammā samucchinno hoti. Atthi kho, bho, añño attā sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ananto ākāsoti ākāsānañcāyatanūpago. Taṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi na passasi. Tamahaṃ jānāmi passāmi. So kho, bho, attā yato kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā, ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā sammā samucchinno hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññapenti. ⤵ (Ṅa) tamañño evamāha – "atthi kho, bho, eso attā yaṃ tvaṃ vadesi. ‘Neso natthī’ti vadāmi. No ca kho, bho, ayaṃ attā ettāvatā sammā samucchinno hoti. Atthi kho, bho, añño attā sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma anantaṃ viññāṇanti viññāṇañcāyatanūpago. Taṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi na passasi. Tamahaṃ jānāmi passāmi. So kho, bho, attā yato kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā, ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā sammā samucchinno hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññapenti. ⤵ (Ca) tamañño evamāha – "atthi kho, bho, eso attā yaṃ tvaṃ vadesi. ‘Neso natthī’ti vadāmi. No ca kho, bho, ayaṃ attā ettāvatā sammā samucchinno hoti. Atthi kho, bho, añño attā sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma natthi kiñcīti ākiñcaññāyatanūpago. Taṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi na passasi. Tamahaṃ jānāmi passāmi. So kho, bho, attā yato kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā, ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā sammā samucchinno hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññapenti. ⤵ (Cha) tamañño evamāha – "atthi kho pana eso attā yaṃ tvaṃ vadesi. ‘Neso natthī’ti vadāmi. No ca kho, bho, ayaṃ attā ettāvatā sammā samucchinno hoti. Atthi kho, bho, añño attā sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpago. Taṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi na passasi. Tamahaṃ jānāmi passāmi. So kho, bho, attā yato kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā, ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā sammā samucchinno hotī"ti. Ittheke sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññapenti. Imā satta diṭṭhiyo.

**en** `979181–983447`
(a) Therein, what are the seven views? Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "Since, sir, this self, having material form, made of the four great elements, produced by mother and father, is cut off and destroyed with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death, to that extent, sir, this self is completely cut off." Thus some declare the cutting off, destruction, and non-existence of an existing being. ⤵ (b) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, is not to that extent completely cut off. There is, sir, another self — divine, having material form, belonging to the sense sphere, feeding on solid food. That you do not know or see; that I know and see. Since, sir, that self is cut off and destroyed with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death, to that extent, sir, this self is completely cut off." Thus some declare the cutting off, destruction, and non-existence of an existing being. ⤵ (c) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, is not to that extent completely cut off. There is, sir, another self — divine, having material form, made of mind, complete in all its limbs, not lacking in faculties. That you do not know or see; that I know and see. Since, sir, that self is cut off and destroyed with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death, to that extent, sir, this self is completely cut off." Thus some declare the cutting off, destruction, and non-existence of an existing being. ⤵ (d) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, is not to that extent completely cut off. There is, sir, another self which, completely passing beyond perceptions of material form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, not attending to perceptions of diversity, aware that 'space is infinite', has reached the field of infinite space. That you do not know or see; that I know and see. Since, sir, that self is cut off and destroyed with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death, to that extent, sir, this self is completely cut off." Thus some declare the cutting off, destruction, and non-existence of an existing being. ⤵ (e) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, is not to that extent completely cut off. There is, sir, another self which, completely passing beyond the field of infinite space, aware that 'consciousness is infinite', has reached the field of infinite consciousness. That you do not know or see; that I know and see. Since, sir, that self is cut off and destroyed with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death, to that extent, sir, this self is completely cut off." Thus some declare the cutting off, destruction, and non-existence of an existing being. ⤵ (f) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, is not to that extent completely cut off. There is, sir, another self which, completely passing beyond the field of infinite consciousness, aware that 'there is nothing', has reached the field of nothingness. That you do not know or see; that I know and see. Since, sir, that self is cut off and destroyed with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death, to that extent, sir, this self is completely cut off." Thus some declare the cutting off, destruction, and non-existence of an existing being. ⤵ (g) Another says to him: "There is that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, is not to that extent completely cut off. There is, sir, another self which, completely passing beyond the field of nothingness, has reached the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. That you do not know or see; that I know and see. Since, sir, that self is cut off and destroyed with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death, to that extent, sir, this self is completely cut off." Thus some declare the cutting off, destruction, and non-existence of an existing being. These are the seven views.
