### 1577

**pi** `668572–668605`
<h2>(2) Aṭṭha kusītavatthūni</h2>

**en** `983711–983753`
<h2>(2) The eight grounds of laziness</h2>

### 1578

**pi** `668606–671540`
Tattha katamāni aṭṭha kusītavatthūni? ⤵ (Ka) idha bhikkhunā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ hoti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – "kammaṃ kho me kātabbaṃ bhavissati. Kammaṃ kho pana me karontassa kāyo kilamissati. Handāhaṃ nipajjāmī"ti. So nipajjati; na vīriyaṃ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ kusītavatthu. ⤵ (Kha) puna caparaṃ bhikkhunā kammaṃ kataṃ hoti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – "ahaṃ kho kammaṃ akāsiṃ. Kammaṃ kho pana me karontassa kāyo kilanto. Handāhaṃ nipajjāmī"ti. So nipajjati; na vīriyaṃ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya. Idaṃ dutiyaṃ kusītavatthu. ⤵ (Ga) puna caparaṃ bhikkhunā maggo gantabbo hoti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – "maggo kho me gantabbo bhavissati. Maggaṃ kho pana me gacchantassa kāyo kilamissati. Handāhaṃ nipajjāmī"ti. So nipajjati; na vīriyaṃ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya. Idaṃ tatiyaṃ kusītavatthu. ⤵ (Gha) puna caparaṃ bhikkhunā maggo gato hoti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – "ahaṃ kho maggaṃ agamāsiṃ. Maggaṃ kho pana me gacchantassa kāyo kilanto. Handāhaṃ nipajjāmī"ti. So nipajjati ; na vīriyaṃ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya. Idaṃ catutthaṃ kusītavatthu. ⤵ (Ṅa) puna caparaṃ bhikkhu gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya caranto na labhati lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ. Tassa evaṃ hoti – "ahaṃ kho gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya caranto nālatthaṃ lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ. Tassa me kāyo kilanto akammañño. Handāhaṃ nipajjāmī"ti. So nipajjati; na vīriyaṃ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya. Idaṃ pañcamaṃ kusītavatthu. ⤵ (Ca) puna caparaṃ bhikkhu gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya caranto labhati lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ. Tassa evaṃ hoti – "ahaṃ kho gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya caranto alatthaṃ lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ. Tassa me kāyo kilanto akammañño māsācitaṃ maññe. Handāhaṃ nipajjāmī"ti. So nipajjati; na vīriyaṃ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya. Idaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ kusītavatthu. ⤵ (Cha) puna caparaṃ bhikkhuno uppanno hoti appamattako ābādho. Tassa evaṃ hoti – "uppanno kho me ayaṃ appamattako ābādho. Atthi kappo nipajjituṃ . Handāhaṃ nipajjāmī"ti. So nipajjati; na vīriyaṃ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya. Idaṃ sattamaṃ kusītavatthu. ⤵ (Ja) puna caparaṃ bhikkhu gilānā vuṭṭhito [gilānavuṭṭhito (saddanībhi) a. ni. 6.16 pāḷiyā ṭīkā passitabbā] hoti aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā. Tassa evaṃ hoti – "ahaṃ kho gilānā vuṭṭhito aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā. Tassa me kāyo dubbalo akammañño. Handāhaṃ nipajjāmī"ti. So nipajjati; na vīriyaṃ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya. Idaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ kusītavatthu. Imāni aṭṭha kusītavatthūni.

**en** `983754–986773`
Therein, what are the eight grounds of laziness? ⤵ (a) Here a monk has work to do. He thinks: "I shall have work to do. But while doing the work my body will get tired. Well then, let me lie down." He lies down; he does not initiate energy for reaching the unreached, attaining the unattained, realising the unrealised. This is the first ground of laziness. ⤵ (b) Further, a monk has done work. He thinks: "I have done work. But while doing the work my body got tired. Well then, let me lie down." He lies down; he does not initiate energy for reaching the unreached, attaining the unattained, realising the unrealised. This is the second ground of laziness. ⤵ (c) Further, a monk has a journey to make. He thinks: "I shall have a journey to make. But while making the journey my body will get tired. Well then, let me lie down." He lies down; he does not initiate energy for reaching the unreached, attaining the unattained, realising the unrealised. This is the third ground of laziness. ⤵ (d) Further, a monk has made a journey. He thinks: "I have made a journey. But while making the journey my body got tired. Well then, let me lie down." He lies down; he does not initiate energy for reaching the unreached, attaining the unattained, realising the unrealised. This is the fourth ground of laziness. ⤵ (e) Further, a monk, walking for alms in a village or town, does not get his fill of coarse or fine food as much as he needs. He thinks: "Walking for alms in a village or town, I did not get my fill of coarse or fine food as much as I needed. My body is tired and unworkable. Well then, let me lie down." He lies down; he does not initiate energy for reaching the unreached, attaining the unattained, realising the unrealised. This is the fifth ground of laziness. ⤵ (f) Further, a monk, walking for alms in a village or town, gets his fill of coarse or fine food as much as he needs. He thinks: "Walking for alms in a village or town, I got my fill of coarse or fine food as much as I needed. My body is heavy and unworkable, like a load of soaked beans, I think. Well then, let me lie down." He lies down; he does not initiate energy for reaching the unreached, attaining the unattained, realising the unrealised. This is the sixth ground of laziness. ⤵ (g) Further, a slight illness has arisen in a monk. He thinks: "This slight illness has arisen in me. There is reason enough to lie down. Well then, let me lie down." He lies down; he does not initiate energy for reaching the unreached, attaining the unattained, realising the unrealised. This is the seventh ground of laziness. ⤵ (h) Further, a monk has recovered from illness, has recently recovered from sickness. He thinks: "I have recovered from illness, recently recovered from sickness. My body is weak and unworkable. Well then, let me lie down." He lies down; he does not initiate energy for reaching the unreached, attaining the unattained, realising the unrealised. This is the eighth ground of laziness. These are the eight grounds of laziness.

### 1579

**pi** `671541–671593`
<h2>(3) Aṭṭhasu lokadhammesu cittassa paṭighāto</h2>

**en** `986774–986840`
<h2>(3) The mind's resistance to the eight worldly conditions</h2>

### 1580

**pi** `671594–671837`
Tattha katamesu aṭṭhasu lokadhammesu cittassa paṭighāto? Lābhe sārāgo, alābhe paṭivirodho, yase sārāgo, ayase paṭivirodho, pasaṃsāya sārāgo, nindāya paṭivirodho, sukhe sārāgo, dukkhe paṭivirodho – imesu aṭṭhasu lokadhammesu cittassa paṭighāto.

**en** `986841–987142`
Therein, what is the mind's resistance to the eight worldly conditions? Passion at gain, opposition at loss; passion at fame, opposition at disrepute; passion at praise, opposition at blame; passion at happiness, opposition at suffering — this is the mind's resistance to the eight worldly conditions.

### 1581

**pi** `671838–671869`

**en** `987143–987188`
<h2>(4) The eight ignoble ways of speech</h2>

### 1582

**pi** `671870–672096`
Tattha katame aṭṭha anariyavohārā? Adiṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā, assute sutavāditā, amute mutavāditā, aviññāte viññātavāditā, diṭṭhe adiṭṭhavāditā, sute assutavāditā, mute amutavāditā, viññāte aviññātavāditā – ime aṭṭha anariyavohārā.

**en** `987189–987645`
Therein, what are the eight ignoble ways of speech? Saying one has seen what one has not seen, saying one has heard what one has not heard, saying one has sensed what one has not sensed, saying one has known what one has not known, saying one has not seen what one has seen, saying one has not heard what one has heard, saying one has not sensed what one has sensed, saying one has not known what one has known — these are the eight ignoble ways of speech.

### 1584

**pi** `672126–672290`
Tattha katame aṭṭha micchattā? Micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi – ime aṭṭha micchattā.

**en** `987681–987884`
Therein, what are the eight wrongnesses? Wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration — these are the eight wrongnesses.

### 1585

**pi** `672291–672320`
<h2>(6) Aṭṭha purisadosā</h2>

**en** `987885–987926`
<h2>(6) The eight faults of a person</h2>

### 1586

**pi** `672321–674182`
Tattha katame aṭṭha purisadosā? (Ka) idha bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā codenti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno [codiyamāno (sī. syā.) a. ni. 8.14] "na sarāmi na sarāmī"ti assatiyāva nibbeṭheti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo purisadoso. ⤵ (Kha) puna caparaṃ bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā codenti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno codakaṃyeva paṭippharati – "kiṃ nu kho tuyhaṃ bālassa abyattassa bhaṇitena! Tvampi nāma maṃ bhaṇitabbaṃ maññasī"ti! Ayaṃ dutiyo purisadoso. ⤵ (Ga) puna caparaṃ bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā codenti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno codakaṃyeva [codakasseva (syā.) a. ni. 8.14] paccāropeti – "tvampi khosi itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno. Tvaṃ tāva paṭhamaṃ paṭikarohī"ti. Ayaṃ tatiyo purisadoso. ⤵ (Gha) puna caparaṃ bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā codenti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno aññenāññaṃ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti. Ayaṃ catuttho purisadoso. ⤵ (Ṅa) puna caparaṃ bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā codenti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno saṅghamajjhe bāhāvikkhepakaṃ bhaṇati. Ayaṃ pañcamo purisadoso. ⤵ (Ca) puna caparaṃ bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā codenti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno anādiyitvā saṅghaṃ, anādiyitvā codakaṃ, sāpattikova [āpattikova (ka.) a. ni. 8.14] yenakāmaṃ pakkamati. Ayaṃ chaṭṭho purisadoso. ⤵ (Cha) puna caparaṃ bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā codenti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno "nevāhaṃ āpannomhi, na panāhaṃ anāpannomhī"ti tuṇhībhūto saṅghaṃ viheseti. Ayaṃ sattamo purisadoso. ⤵ (Ja) puna caparaṃ bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā codenti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno evamāha – "kiṃ nu kho tumhe āyasmanto atibāḷhaṃ mayi byāvaṭā. Idānāhaṃ sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmī"ti. So sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattitvā evamāha – "idāni kho tumhe āyasmanto attamanā hothā"ti. Ayaṃ aṭṭhamo purisadoso. Ime aṭṭha purisadosā.

**en** `987927–990163`
Therein, what are the eight faults of a person? (a) Here monks charge a monk with an offence. That monk, being charged with the offence by the monks, evades it through sheer forgetfulness: "I do not remember, I do not remember." This is the first fault of a person. ⤵ (b) Further, monks charge a monk with an offence. That monk, being charged with the offence by the monks, snaps back at the very one who charges him: "What is the use of the talk of a fool and incompetent like you! Do you really think you have something to say to me?" This is the second fault of a person. ⤵ (c) Further, monks charge a monk with an offence. That monk, being charged with the offence by the monks, throws the charge back at the very one who charges him: "You too have committed such-and-such an offence. You make amends first." This is the third fault of a person. ⤵ (d) Further, monks charge a monk with an offence. That monk, being charged with the offence by the monks, answers one thing with another, leads the talk aside, and displays anger, hate, and displeasure. This is the fourth fault of a person. ⤵ (e) Further, monks charge a monk with an offence. That monk, being charged with the offence by the monks, speaks waving his arms about in the midst of the Order. This is the fifth fault of a person. ⤵ (f) Further, monks charge a monk with an offence. That monk, being charged with the offence by the monks, disregarding the Order and disregarding the one who charges him, goes off wherever he likes while still bearing the offence. This is the sixth fault of a person. ⤵ (g) Further, monks charge a monk with an offence. That monk, being charged with the offence by the monks, saying "I have neither committed an offence nor not committed one", vexes the Order by remaining silent. This is the seventh fault of a person. ⤵ (h) Further, monks charge a monk with an offence. That monk, being charged with the offence by the monks, says: "Why are you venerable ones so extremely busy about me? Now I shall renounce the training and return to the lower life." Having renounced the training and returned to the lower life, he says: "Now, venerable ones, be satisfied." This is the eighth fault of a person. These are the eight faults of a person.

### 1587

**pi** `674183–674212`
<h2>(7) Aṭṭha asaññīvādā</h2>

**en** `990164–990218`
<h2>(7) The eight doctrines of the non-percipient</h2>

### 1588

**pi** `674213–674684`
Tattha katame aṭṭha asaññīvādā? "Rūpī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – asaññīti naṃ paññapenti; arūpī attā…pe… rūpī ca arūpī ca…pe… nevarūpīnārūpī…pe… "antavā attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – asaññīti naṃ paññapenti; "anantavā attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – asaññīti naṃ paññapenti; "antavā ca anantavā ca attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – asaññīti naṃ paññapenti; "nevantavā nānantavā attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – asaññīti naṃ paññapenti. Ime aṭṭha asaññīvādā.

**en** `990219–990932`
Therein, what are the eight doctrines of the non-percipient? "The self has material form and is unimpaired after death" — they declare it non-percipient; "the self is immaterial…"; "the self both has material form and is immaterial…"; "the self neither has material form nor is immaterial…"; "the self is finite and unimpaired after death" — they declare it non-percipient; "the self is infinite and unimpaired after death" — they declare it non-percipient; "the self is both finite and infinite and unimpaired after death" — they declare it non-percipient; "the self is neither finite nor infinite and unimpaired after death" — they declare it non-percipient. These are the eight doctrines of the non-percipient.

### 1589

**pi** `674685–674724`
<h2>(8) Aṭṭha nevasaññīnāsaññīvādā</h2>

**en** `990933–991010`
<h2>(8) The eight doctrines of the neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient</h2>

### 1590

**pi** `674725–675459`
Tattha katame aṭṭha nevasaññīnāsaññīvādā? "Rūpī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – nevasaññīnāsaññīti naṃ paññapenti; "arūpī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – nevasaññīnāsaññīti naṃ paññapenti; "rūpī ca arūpī ca attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – nevasaññīnāsaññīti naṃ paññapenti; "nevarūpīnārūpī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – nevasaññīnāsaññīti naṃ paññapenti; "antavā attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – nevasaññīnāsaññīti naṃ paññapenti; "anantavā attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – nevasaññīnāsaññīti naṃ paññapenti; "antavā ca anantavā ca attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – nevasaññīnāsaññīti naṃ paññapenti; "nevantavā nānantavā attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā"ti – nevasaññīnāsaññīti naṃ paññapenti. Ime aṭṭha nevasaññīnāsaññīvādā.

**en** `991011–992137`
Therein, what are the eight doctrines of the neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient? "The self has material form and is unimpaired after death" — they declare it neither percipient nor non-percipient; "the self is immaterial and unimpaired after death" — they declare it neither percipient nor non-percipient; "the self both has material form and is immaterial and is unimpaired after death" — they declare it neither percipient nor non-percipient; "the self neither has material form nor is immaterial and is unimpaired after death" — they declare it neither percipient nor non-percipient; "the self is finite and unimpaired after death" — they declare it neither percipient nor non-percipient; "the self is infinite and unimpaired after death" — they declare it neither percipient nor non-percipient; "the self is both finite and infinite and unimpaired after death" — they declare it neither percipient nor non-percipient; "the self is neither finite nor infinite and unimpaired after death" — they declare it neither percipient nor non-percipient. These are the eight doctrines of the neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient.

<h2>(1) Nava āghātavatthūni</h2>

**en** `992190–992233`
<h2>(1) The nine grounds of resentment</h2>

### 1594

**pi** `675529–675900`
Tattha katamāni nava āghātavatthūni? "Anatthaṃ me acarī"ti āghāto jāyati ; "anatthaṃ me caratī"ti āghāto jāyati; "anatthaṃ me carissatī"ti āghāto jāyati; "piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari"…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… anatthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati; appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati. Imāni nava āghātavatthūni.

**en** `992234–992657`
Therein, what are the nine grounds of resentment? Resentment arises: "He has done me harm"; resentment arises: "He is doing me harm"; resentment arises: "He will do me harm"; "He has done harm… is doing harm… will do harm to one dear and pleasing to me" — resentment arises; "He has done good… is doing good… will do good to one disliked and displeasing to me" — resentment arises. These are the nine grounds of resentment.

### 1595

**en** `992658–992698`

### 1596

**pi** `675932–676079`
Tattha katamāni nava purisamalāni? Kodho, makkho, issā, macchariyaṃ, māyā, sāṭheyyaṃ, musāvādo, pāpicchatā, micchādiṭṭhi – imāni nava purisamalāni.

**en** `992699–992878`
Therein, what are the nine stains of a person? Anger, contempt, envy, stinginess, deceit, treachery, false speech, evil desire, wrong view — these are the nine stains of a person.

### 1597

**pi** `676080–676107`
<h2>(3) Navavidhā mānā</h2>

**en** `992879–992917`
<h2>(3) The nine kinds of conceit</h2>

### 1598

**pi** `676108–676446`
Tattha katame navavidhā mānā? "Seyyassa seyyohamasmī"ti māno, "seyyassa sadisohamasmī"ti māno, "seyyassa hīnohamasmī"ti māno, "sadisassa seyyohamasmī"ti māno, "sadisassa sadisohamasmī"ti māno, "sadisassa hīnohamasmī"ti māno, "hīnassa seyyohamasmī"ti māno, "hīnassa sadisohamasmī"ti māno, "hīnassa hīnohamasmī"ti māno – ime navavidhā mānā.

**en** `992918–993429`
Therein, what are the nine kinds of conceit? The conceit of one who is better, "I am better"; the conceit of one who is better, "I am equal"; the conceit of one who is better, "I am worse"; the conceit of one who is equal, "I am better"; the conceit of one who is equal, "I am equal"; the conceit of one who is equal, "I am worse"; the conceit of one who is worse, "I am better"; the conceit of one who is worse, "I am equal"; the conceit of one who is worse, "I am worse" — these are the nine kinds of conceit.

### 1599

**pi** `676447–676483`
<h2>(4) Nava taṇhāmūlakā dhammā</h2>

**en** `993430–993476`
<h2>(4) The nine things rooted in craving</h2>

### 1600

**pi** `676484–676917`
Tattha katame nava taṇhāmūlakā dhammā? Taṇhaṃ paṭicca pariyesanā, pariyesanaṃ paṭicca lābho, lābhaṃ paṭicca vinicchayo, vinicchayaṃ paṭicca chandarāgo, chandarāgaṃ paṭicca ajjhosānaṃ, ajjhosānaṃ paṭicca pariggaho, pariggahaṃ paṭicca macchariyaṃ, macchariyaṃ paṭicca ārakkho, ārakkhādhikaraṇaṃ daṇḍādāna-satthādāna-kalaha-viggahavivāda-tuvaṃtuvaṃ-pesuñña-musāvādā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti – ime nava taṇhāmūlakā dhammā.

**en** `993477–994125`
Therein, what are the nine things rooted in craving? Because of craving there is seeking; because of seeking there is gain; because of gain there is deciding; because of deciding there is desire-and-lust; because of desire-and-lust there is holding fast; because of holding fast there is taking possession; because of taking possession there is stinginess; because of stinginess there is guarding; and with guarding as the occasion, there come to be the taking up of sticks and weapons, quarrels, contention, disputes, accusations, divisive speech, false speech, and many other evil, unwholesome things. These are the nine things rooted in craving.

### 1601

**pi** `676918–676944`
<h2>(5) Nava iñjitāni</h2>

**en** `994126–994158`
<h2>(5) The nine agitations</h2>

### 1602

**pi** `676945–677278`
Tattha katamāni nava iñjitāni? "Asmī"ti iñjitametaṃ, "ahamasmī"ti iñjitametaṃ , "ayamahamasmī"ti iñjitametaṃ "bhavissa"nti iñjitametaṃ, "rūpī bhavissa"nti iñjitametaṃ, "arūpī bhavissa"nti iñjitametaṃ, "saññī bhavissa"nti iñjitametaṃ, "asaññī bhavissa"nti iñjitametaṃ, "nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissa"nti iñjitametaṃ – imāni nava iñjitāni.

**en** `994159–994582`
Therein, what are the nine agitations? "I am" is an agitation; "I am this" is an agitation; "this I am" is an agitation; "I shall be" is an agitation; "I shall have material form" is an agitation; "I shall be immaterial" is an agitation; "I shall be percipient" is an agitation; "I shall be non-percipient" is an agitation; "I shall be neither percipient nor non-percipient" is an agitation — these are the nine agitations.

### 1603

**pi** `677279–677310`

Tattha katamāni nava maññitāni… nava phanditāni… nava papañcitāni… nava saṅkhatāni? "Asmī"ti saṅkhatametaṃ, "ahamasmī"ti saṅkhatametaṃ , "ayamahamasmī"ti saṅkhatametaṃ, "bhavissa"nti saṅkhatametaṃ, "rūpī bhavissa"nti saṅkhatametaṃ, "arūpī bhavissa"nti saṅkhatametaṃ, "saññī bhavissa"nti saṅkhatametaṃ , "asaññī bhavissa"nti saṅkhatametaṃ, "nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissa"nti saṅkhatametaṃ – imāni nava saṅkhatāni.

**en** `994631–995144`
Therein, what are the nine imaginings… the nine waverings… the nine proliferations… the nine constructions? "I am" is a construction; "I am this" is a construction; "this I am" is a construction; "I shall be" is a construction; "I shall have material form" is a construction; "I shall be immaterial" is a construction; "I shall be percipient" is a construction; "I shall be non-percipient" is a construction; "I shall be neither percipient nor non-percipient" is a construction — these are the nine constructions.

Therein, what are the ten grounds of defilement? Greed, hate, delusion, conceit, views, doubt, dullness, restlessness, shamelessness, lack of moral dread — these are the ten grounds of defilement.

### 1609

**pi** `677940–677972`

### 1610

**pi** `677973–678375`
Tattha katamāni dasa āghātavatthūni? "Anatthaṃ me acarī"ti āghāto jāyati, "anatthaṃ me caratī"ti āghāto jāyati, "anatthaṃ me carissatī"ti āghāto jāyati, "piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari"…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… anatthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, aṭṭhāne vā pana āghāto jāyati – imāni dasa āghātavatthūni.

**en** `995479–995936`
Therein, what are the ten grounds of resentment? Resentment arises: "He has done me harm"; resentment arises: "He is doing me harm"; resentment arises: "He will do me harm"; "He has done harm… is doing harm… will do harm to one dear and pleasing to me" — resentment arises; "He has done good… is doing good… will do good to one disliked and displeasing to me" — resentment arises; or resentment arises groundlessly — these are the ten grounds of resentment.

### 1611

**pi** `678376–678411`

### 1612

**pi** `678412–678606`
Tattha katame dasa akusalakammapathā? Pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo, abhijjhā, byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi – ime dasa akusalakammapathā.

**en** `995988–996257`
Therein, what are the ten courses of unwholesome action? Killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, idle chatter, covetousness, ill will, wrong view — these are the ten courses of unwholesome action.

### 1614

**pi** `678637–678897`
Tattha katamāni dasa saṃyojanāni? Kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ , mānasaṃyojanaṃ, diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ, vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ, sīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanaṃ, bhavarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, issāsaṃyojanaṃ, macchariyasaṃyojanaṃ, avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ – imāni dasa saṃyojanāni.

**en** `996287–996627`
Therein, what are the ten fetters? The fetter of sensual lust, the fetter of aversion, the fetter of conceit, the fetter of views, the fetter of doubt, the fetter of wrong grasping of virtue and observances, the fetter of lust for existence, the fetter of envy, the fetter of stinginess, the fetter of ignorance — these are the ten fetters.

**en** `996661–996895`
Therein, what are the ten wrongnesses? Wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration, wrong knowledge, wrong liberation — these are the ten wrongnesses.

### 1617

<h2>(6) The wrong view with ten grounds</h2>

### 1618

**pi** `679157–679550`
Tattha katamā dasavatthukā micchādiṭṭhi? Natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, natthi hutaṃ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, natthi ayaṃ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā [samaggatā (ka.)] sammā paṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentīti – ayaṃ dasavatthukā micchādiṭṭhi.

**en** `996941–997495`
Therein, what is the wrong view with ten grounds? "There is nothing given, there is nothing offered, there is nothing sacrificed; there is no fruit and result of well-done and badly-done actions; there is no this world, there is no other world; there is no mother, there is no father; there are no spontaneously reborn beings; there are in the world no ascetics and brahmins of right conduct and right practice who declare this world and the other world, having realised them for themselves by direct knowledge" — this is the wrong view with ten grounds.

### 1619

**pi** `679551–679595`
<h2>(7) Dasavatthukā antaggāhikā diṭṭhi</h2>

<h2>(7) The extremist view with ten grounds</h2>

**pi** `680498–686434`
Kathañca asmīti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ [anavakārī (sī. ka.)] karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ asmīti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, asmīti mānaṃ paṭilabhati , asmīti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – itthasmīti vā evasmīti vā aññathāsmīti vā. ⤵ (2) Kathañca itthasmīti hoti? Khattiyosmīti vā, brāhmaṇosmīti vā, vessosmīti vā, suddosmīti vā, gahaṭṭhosmīti vā, pabbajitosmīti vā, devosmīti vā, manussosmīti vā, rūpīsmīti vā, arūpīsmīti vā, saññīsmīti vā, asaññīsmīti vā, nevasaññīnāsaññīsmīti vā – evaṃ itthasmīti hoti. ⤵ (3) Kathañca evasmīti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ [paraṃ puggalaṃ (syā.)] upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo tathāhaṃ khattiyosmīti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇosmīti vā, yathā so vesso tathāhaṃ vessosmīti vā yathā so suddo tathāhaṃ suddosmīti vā, yathā so gahaṭṭho tathāhaṃ gahaṭṭhosmīti vā, yathā so pabbajito tathāhaṃ pabbajitosmīti vā, yathā so devo tathāhaṃ devosmīti vā, yathā so manusso tathāhaṃ manussosmīti vā, yathā so rūpī tathāhaṃ rūpīsmīti vā, yathā so arūpī tathāhaṃ arūpīsmīti vā, yathā so saññī tathāhaṃ saññīsmīti vā, yathā so asaññī tathāhaṃ asaññīsmīti vā, yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññīsmīti vā – evaṃ evasmīti hoti. ⤵ (4) Kathañca aññathāsmīti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo nāhaṃ tathā khattiyosmīti vā yathā so brāhmaṇo nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇosmīti vā, yathā so vesso nāhaṃ tathā vessosmīti vā, yathā so suddo nāhaṃ tathā suddosmīti vā, yathā so gahaṭṭho nāhaṃ tathā gahaṭṭhosmīti vā, yathā so pabbajito nāhaṃ tathā pabbajitosmīti vā, yathā so devo nāhaṃ tathā devosmīti vā, yathā so manusso nāhaṃ tathā manussosmīti vā, yathā so rūpī nāhaṃ tathā rūpīsmīti vā, yathā so arūpī nāhaṃ tathā arūpīsmīti vā, yathā so saññī nāhaṃ tathā saññīsmīti vā, yathā so asaññī nāhaṃ tathā asaññīsmīti vā, yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññīsmīti vā – evaṃ aññathāsmīti hoti. ⤵ (5) Kathañca bhavissanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ bhavissanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, bhavissanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati , bhavissanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – itthaṃ bhavissanti vā, evaṃ bhavissanti vā, aññathā bhavissanti vā. ⤵ (6) Kathañca itthaṃ bhavissanti hoti? Khattiyo bhavissanti vā, brāhmaṇo bhavissanti vā, vesso bhavissanti vā, suddo bhavissanti vā, gahaṭṭho bhavissanti vā, pabbajito bhavissanti vā, devo bhavissanti vā, manusso bhavissanti vā, rūpī bhavissanti vā, arūpī bhavissanti vā, saññī bhavissanti vā, asaññī bhavissanti vā, nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ itthaṃ bhavissanti hoti. ⤵ (7) Kathañca evaṃ bhavissanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo tathāhaṃ khattiyo bhavissanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇo bhavissanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ bhavissanti hoti. ⤵ (8) Kathañca aññathā bhavissanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo nāhaṃ tathā khattiyo bhavissanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo bhavissanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ aññathā bhavissanti hoti. ⤵ (9) Kathañca asasmīti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ niccosmi dhuvosmi sassatosmi avipariṇāmadhammosmīti – evaṃ asasmīti hoti. ⤵ (10) Kathañca sātasmīti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ ucchijjissāmi vinassissāmi na bhavissāmīti – evaṃ sātasmīti hoti. ⤵ (11) Kathañca siyanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ siyanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, siyanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati , siyanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – itthaṃ siyanti vā, evaṃ siyanti vā, aññathā siyanti vā. ⤵ (12) Kathañca itthaṃ siyanti hoti? Khattiyo siyanti vā, brāhmaṇo siyanti vā, vesso siyanti vā, suddo siyanti vā, gahaṭṭho siyanti vā, pabbajito siyanti vā, devo siyanti vā, manusso siyanti vā, rūpī siyanti vā, arūpī siyanti vā, saññī siyanti vā, asaññī siyanti vā, nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti. ⤵ (13) Kathañca evaṃ siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo tathāhaṃ khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti. ⤵ (14) Kathañca aññathā siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo nāhaṃ tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti. ⤵ (15) Kathañca apāhaṃ siyanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ apāhaṃ siyanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, apāhaṃ siyanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati, apāhaṃ siyanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti vā, apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti vā, apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti vā. ⤵ (16) Kathañca apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti? Apāhaṃ khattiyo siyanti vā, apāhaṃ brāhmaṇo siyanti vā, apāhaṃ vesso siyanti vā, apāhaṃ suddo siyanti vā, apāhaṃ gahaṭṭho siyanti vā, apāhaṃ pabbajito siyanti vā, apāhaṃ devo siyanti vā, apāhaṃ manusso siyanti vā, apāhaṃ rūpī siyanti vā, apāhaṃ arūpī siyanti vā, apāhaṃ saññī siyanti vā, apāhaṃ asaññī siyanti vā, apāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti. (17) Kathañca apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo apāhaṃ tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo apāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī apāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti. ⤵ (18) Kathañca apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo apāhaṃ na tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo apāhaṃ na tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī apāhaṃ na tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti.

**en** `998765–1006327`
And how is there "I am"? Not having discarded some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one obtains the desire "I am", one obtains the conceit "I am", one obtains the view "I am". When that exists, there are these proliferations: "I am thus", or "I am just so", or "I am otherwise". ⤵ (2) And how is there "I am thus"? "I am a noble", or "I am a brahmin", or "I am a merchant", or "I am a worker", or "I am a householder", or "I am a renunciant", or "I am a god", or "I am a human being", or "I have material form", or "I am immaterial", or "I am percipient", or "I am non-percipient", or "I am neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "I am thus". ⤵ (3) And how is there "I am just so"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, so I am a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, so I am a brahmin", or "as he is a merchant, so I am a merchant", or "as he is a worker, so I am a worker", or "as he is a householder, so I am a householder", or "as he is a renunciant, so I am a renunciant", or "as he is a god, so I am a god", or "as he is a human being, so I am a human being", or "as he has material form, so I have material form", or "as he is immaterial, so I am immaterial", or "as he is percipient, so I am percipient", or "as he is non-percipient, so I am non-percipient", or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, so I am neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "I am just so". ⤵ (4) And how is there "I am otherwise"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, I am not so a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, I am not so a brahmin", or "as he is a merchant, I am not so a merchant", or "as he is a worker, I am not so a worker", or "as he is a householder, I am not so a householder", or "as he is a renunciant, I am not so a renunciant", or "as he is a god, I am not so a god", or "as he is a human being, I am not so a human being", or "as he has material form, I do not so have material form", or "as he is immaterial, I am not so immaterial", or "as he is percipient, I am not so percipient", or "as he is non-percipient, I am not so non-percipient", or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, I am not so neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "I am otherwise". ⤵ (5) And how is there "I shall be"? Not having discarded some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one obtains the desire "I shall be", one obtains the conceit "I shall be", one obtains the view "I shall be". When that exists, there are these proliferations: "I shall be thus", or "I shall be just so", or "I shall be otherwise". ⤵ (6) And how is there "I shall be thus"? "I shall be a noble", or "I shall be a brahmin", or "I shall be a merchant", or "I shall be a worker", or "I shall be a householder", or "I shall be a renunciant", or "I shall be a god", or "I shall be a human being", or "I shall have material form", or "I shall be immaterial", or "I shall be percipient", or "I shall be non-percipient", or "I shall be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "I shall be thus". ⤵ (7) And how is there "I shall be just so"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, so I shall be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, so I shall be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, so I shall be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "I shall be just so". ⤵ (8) And how is there "I shall be otherwise"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, I shall not so be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, I shall not so be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, I shall not so be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "I shall be otherwise". ⤵ (9) And how is there "I am lasting"? Not having discarded some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one thinks, "I am permanent, I am stable, I am eternal, I am not subject to change" — thus there is "I am lasting". ⤵ (10) And how is there "I am perishing"? Not having discarded some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one thinks, "I shall be cut off, I shall be destroyed, I shall not be" — thus there is "I am perishing". ⤵ (11) And how is there "may I be"? Not having discarded some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one obtains the desire "may I be", one obtains the conceit "may I be", one obtains the view "may I be". When that exists, there are these proliferations: "may I be thus", or "may I be just so", or "may I be otherwise". ⤵ (12) And how is there "may I be thus"? "May I be a noble", or "may I be a brahmin", or "may I be a merchant", or "may I be a worker", or "may I be a householder", or "may I be a renunciant", or "may I be a god", or "may I be a human being", or "may I have material form", or "may I be immaterial", or "may I be percipient", or "may I be non-percipient", or "may I be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "may I be thus". ⤵ (13) And how is there "may I be just so"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, so may I be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, so may I be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, so may I be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "may I be just so". ⤵ (14) And how is there "may I be otherwise"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, may I not so be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, may I not so be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, may I not so be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "may I be otherwise". ⤵ (15) And how is there "would that I might be"? Not having discarded some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one obtains the desire "would that I might be", one obtains the conceit "would that I might be", one obtains the view "would that I might be". When that exists, there are these proliferations: "would that I might be thus", or "would that I might be just so", or "would that I might be otherwise". ⤵ (16) And how is there "would that I might be thus"? "Would that I might be a noble", or "would that I might be a brahmin", or "would that I might be a merchant", or "would that I might be a worker", or "would that I might be a householder", or "would that I might be a renunciant", or "would that I might be a god", or "would that I might be a human being", or "would that I might have material form", or "would that I might be immaterial", or "would that I might be percipient", or "would that I might be non-percipient", or "would that I might be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "would that I might be thus". (17) And how is there "would that I might be just so"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, so would that I might be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, so would that I might be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, so would that I might be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "would that I might be just so". ⤵ (18) And how is there "would that I might be otherwise"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, would that I might not so be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, would that I might not so be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, would that I might not so be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "would that I might be otherwise".

Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā tathāhaṃ khattiyosmīti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇosmīti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññīsmīti vā – evaṃ iminā evasmīti hoti. ⤵ (4) Kathañca iminā aññathāsmīti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā nāhaṃ tathā khattiyosmīti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇosmīti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññīsmīti vā – evaṃ iminā aññathāsmīti hoti. ⤵ (5) Kathañca iminā bhavissanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ avakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ iminā bhavissanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā bhavissanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā bhavissanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – iminā itthaṃ bhavissanti vā, iminā evaṃ bhavissanti vā, iminā aññathā bhavissanti vā. ⤵ (6) Kathañca iminā itthaṃ bhavissanti hoti? Iminā khattiyo bhavissanti vā…pe… iminā arūpī bhavissanti vā, iminā saññī bhavissanti vā, iminā asaññī bhavissanti vā, iminā nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ iminā itthaṃ bhavissanti hoti. ⤵ (7) Kathañca iminā evaṃ bhavissanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā tathāhaṃ khattiyo bhavissanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇo bhavissanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ iminā evaṃ bhavissanti hoti. ⤵ (8) Kathañca iminā aññathā bhavissanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā nāhaṃ tathā khattiyo bhavissanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo bhavissanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ iminā aññathā bhavissanti hoti. ⤵ (9) Kathañca iminā asasmīti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ avakāriṃ [avakārī (sī.)] karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ iminā niccosmi dhuvosmi sassatosmi avipariṇāmadhammosmīti – evaṃ iminā asasmīti hoti. ⤵ (10) Kathañca iminā sātasmīti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ avakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ iminā ucchijjissāmi vinassissāmi na bhavissāmīti – evaṃ iminā sātasmīti hoti. ⤵ (11) Kathañca iminā siyanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ avakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ iminā siyanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā siyanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā siyanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – iminā itthaṃ siyanti vā, iminā evaṃ siyanti vā, iminā aññathā siyanti vā. ⤵ (12) Kathañca iminā itthaṃ siyanti hoti? Iminā khattiyo siyanti vā, iminā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā, iminā vesso siyanti vā, iminā suddo siyanti vā, iminā gahaṭṭho siyanti vā, iminā pabbajito siyanti vā, iminā devo siyanti vā, iminā manusso siyanti vā, iminā rūpī siyanti vā, iminā arūpī siyanti vā, iminā saññī siyanti vā, iminā asaññī siyanti vā, iminā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā itthaṃ siyanti hoti. ⤵ (13) Kathañca iminā evaṃ siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā tathāhaṃ khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā evaṃ siyanti hoti. ⤵ (14) Kathañca iminā aññathā siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā nāhaṃ tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā aññathā siyanti hoti. ⤵ (15) Kathañca iminā apāhaṃ siyanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ avakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ iminā apāhaṃ siyanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā apāhaṃ siyanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā apāhaṃ siyanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – iminā apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti vā. ⤵ (16) Kathañca iminā apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti? Iminā apāhaṃ khattiyo siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ brāhmaṇo siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ vesso siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ suddo siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ gahaṭṭho siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ pabbajito siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ devo siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ manusso siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ rūpī siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ arūpī siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ saññī siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ asaññī siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti. ⤵ (17) Kathañca iminā apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā apāhaṃ tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā apāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā apāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti. ⤵ (18) Kathañca iminā apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā apāhaṃ na tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā apāhaṃ na tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā apāhaṃ na tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti. ⤵ Imāni aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni bāhirassa upādāya. ⤵ Iti imāni aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni ajjhattikassa upādāya, imāni aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni bāhirassa upādāya, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni honti. Iti evarūpāni atītāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, anāgatāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, paccuppannāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā aṭṭhataṇhāvicaritasataṃ hoti.

**en** `1007193–1015074`
(1) And how is there "by this I am"? Having taken up some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one obtains the desire "by this I am", one obtains the conceit "by this I am", one obtains the view "by this I am". When that exists, there are these proliferations: "by this I am thus", or "by this I am just so", or "by this I am otherwise". ⤵ (2) And how is there "by this I am thus"? "By this I am a noble", or "by this I am a brahmin", or "by this I am a merchant", or "by this I am a worker", or "by this I am a householder", or "by this I am a renunciant", or "by this I am a god", or "by this I am a human being", or "by this I have material form", or "by this I am immaterial", or "by this I am percipient", or "by this I am non-percipient", or "by this I am neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this I am thus". ⤵ (3) And how is there "by this I am just so"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, by this so I am a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, by this so I am a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, by this so I am neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this I am just so". ⤵ (4) And how is there "by this I am otherwise"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, by this I am not so a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, by this I am not so a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, by this I am not so neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this I am otherwise". ⤵ (5) And how is there "by this I shall be"? Having taken up some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one obtains the desire "by this I shall be", one obtains the conceit "by this I shall be", one obtains the view "by this I shall be". When that exists, there are these proliferations: "by this I shall be thus", or "by this I shall be just so", or "by this I shall be otherwise". ⤵ (6) And how is there "by this I shall be thus"? "By this I shall be a noble"… or "by this I shall be immaterial", or "by this I shall be percipient", or "by this I shall be non-percipient", or "by this I shall be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this I shall be thus". ⤵ (7) And how is there "by this I shall be just so"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, by this so I shall be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, by this so I shall be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, by this so I shall be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this I shall be just so". ⤵ (8) And how is there "by this I shall be otherwise"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, by this I shall not so be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, by this I shall not so be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, by this I shall not so be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this I shall be otherwise". ⤵ (9) And how is there "by this I am lasting"? Having taken up some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one thinks, "by this I am permanent, I am stable, I am eternal, I am not subject to change" — thus there is "by this I am lasting". ⤵ (10) And how is there "by this I am perishing"? Having taken up some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one thinks, "by this I shall be cut off, I shall be destroyed, I shall not be" — thus there is "by this I am perishing". ⤵ (11) And how is there "by this may I be"? Having taken up some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one obtains the desire "by this may I be", one obtains the conceit "by this may I be", one obtains the view "by this may I be". When that exists, there are these proliferations: "by this may I be thus", or "by this may I be just so", or "by this may I be otherwise". ⤵ (12) And how is there "by this may I be thus"? "By this may I be a noble", or "by this may I be a brahmin", or "by this may I be a merchant", or "by this may I be a worker", or "by this may I be a householder", or "by this may I be a renunciant", or "by this may I be a god", or "by this may I be a human being", or "by this may I have material form", or "by this may I be immaterial", or "by this may I be percipient", or "by this may I be non-percipient", or "by this may I be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this may I be thus". ⤵ (13) And how is there "by this may I be just so"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, by this so may I be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, by this so may I be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, by this so may I be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this may I be just so". ⤵ (14) And how is there "by this may I be otherwise"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, by this may I not so be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, by this may I not so be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, by this may I not so be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this may I be otherwise". ⤵ (15) And how is there "by this would that I might be"? Having taken up some thing — material form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness — one obtains the desire "by this would that I might be", one obtains the conceit "by this would that I might be", one obtains the view "by this would that I might be". When that exists, there are these proliferations: "by this would that I might be thus", or "by this would that I might be just so", or "by this would that I might be otherwise". ⤵ (16) And how is there "by this would that I might be thus"? "By this would that I might be a noble", or "by this would that I might be a brahmin", or "by this would that I might be a merchant", or "by this would that I might be a worker", or "by this would that I might be a householder", or "by this would that I might be a renunciant", or "by this would that I might be a god", or "by this would that I might be a human being", or "by this would that I might have material form", or "by this would that I might be immaterial", or "by this would that I might be percipient", or "by this would that I might be non-percipient", or "by this would that I might be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this would that I might be thus". ⤵ (17) And how is there "by this would that I might be just so"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, by this so would that I might be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, by this so would that I might be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, by this so would that I might be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this would that I might be just so". ⤵ (18) And how is there "by this would that I might be otherwise"? Comparing oneself with another person: "As he is a noble, by this would that I might not so be a noble", or "as he is a brahmin, by this would that I might not so be a brahmin"… or "as he is neither percipient nor non-percipient, by this would that I might not so be neither percipient nor non-percipient" — thus there is "by this would that I might be otherwise". ⤵ These are the eighteen wanderings of craving concerning what is external. ⤵ So these are the eighteen wanderings of craving concerning what is internal and these are the eighteen wanderings of craving concerning what is external; gathering them together and summing them up, there are thirty-six wanderings of craving. So there are thirty-six such past wanderings of craving, thirty-six future wanderings of craving, and thirty-six present wanderings of craving; gathering them together and summing them up, there are one hundred and eight wanderings of craving.

### 1630

**pi** `693140–693525`
Tattha katamāni dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni brahmajāle veyyākaraṇe vuttāni bhagavatā? Cattāro sassatavādā, cattāro ekaccasassatikā, cattāro antānantikā, cattāro amarāvikkhepikā, dve adhiccasamuppannikā, soḷasa saññīvādā, aṭṭha asaññīvādā, aṭṭha nevasaññīnāsaññīvādā, satta ucchedavādā, pañca diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādā – imāni dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni brahmajāle veyyākaraṇe vuttāni bhagavatāti.

**en** `1015075–1015734`
Therein, what are the sixty-two grounds of views spoken of by the Blessed One in the exposition of the Brahmajāla? The four eternalist doctrines, the four partly-eternalist doctrines, the four doctrines of the finite and infinite, the four doctrines of endless equivocation, the two doctrines of chance origination, the sixteen doctrines of the percipient, the eight doctrines of the non-percipient, the eight doctrines of the neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient, the seven annihilationist doctrines, the five doctrines of Nibbāna in this very life — these are the sixty-two grounds of views spoken of by the Blessed One in the exposition of the Brahmajāla.

**en** `1015878–1016336`
How many aggregates are there, how many sense-fields, how many elements, how many truths, how many faculties, how many roots, how many nutriments, how many contacts, how many feelings, how many perceptions, how many intentions, how many minds? ⤵ There are five aggregates, twelve sense-fields, eighteen elements, four truths, twenty-two faculties, nine roots, four nutriments, seven contacts, seven feelings, seven perceptions, seven intentions, seven minds.

### 1635

**pi** `693970–694109`
Tattha katame pañcakkhandhā? Rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime vuccanti "pañcakkhandhā".

**en** `1016337–1016571`
Therein, what are the five aggregates? The aggregate of material form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness — these are called "the five aggregates".

### 1636

**pi** `694110–694348`
Tattha katamāni dvādasāyatanāni? Cakkhāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ – imāni vuccanti "dvādasāyatanāni".

**en** `1016572–1016940`
Therein, what are the twelve sense-fields? The eye sense-field, the sight sense-field, the ear sense-field, the sound sense-field, the nose sense-field, the smell sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the taste sense-field, the body sense-field, the tangible sense-field, the mind sense-field, the mental-object sense-field — these are called "the twelve sense-fields".

### 1637

Cakkhudhātu, rūpadhātu, cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotadhātu, saddadhātu, sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānadhātu , gandhadhātu, ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhādhātu, rasadhātu, jivhāviññāṇadhātu, kāyadhātu, phoṭṭhabbadhātu, kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manodhātu, dhammadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu – imā vuccanti "aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo".

**en** `1016941–1017449`
Therein, what are the eighteen elements? The eye element, the sight element, the eye-consciousness element, the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, the nose element, the smell element, the nose-consciousness element, the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, the body element, the tangible element, the body-consciousness element, the mind element, the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element — these are called "the eighteen elements".

### 1638

**pi** `694677–694802`
Tattha katamāni cattāri saccāni? Dukkhasaccaṃ, samudayasaccaṃ, nirodhasaccaṃ, maggasaccaṃ – imāni vuccanti "cattāri saccāni".

**en** `1017450–1017617`
Therein, what are the four truths? The truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, the truth of cessation, the truth of the path — these are called "the four truths".

### 1639

**en** `1017618–1018245`
Therein, what are the twenty-two faculties? The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty, the faculty of femininity, the faculty of masculinity, the life faculty, the happiness faculty, the pain faculty, the joy faculty, the grief faculty, the equanimity faculty, the faculty of confidence, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known", the faculty of final knowledge, the faculty of one who has fully known — these are called "the twenty-two faculties".

### 1640

**pi** `695211–695678`
Tattha katame nava hetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo akusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū. ⤵ Tattha katame tayo kusalahetū? Alobho kusalahetu, adoso kusalahetu, amoho kusalahetu – ime tayo kusalahetū. ⤵ Tattha katame tayo akusalahetū? Lobho akusalahetu, doso akusalahetu, moho akusalahetu – ime tayo akusalahetū. ⤵ Tattha katame tayo abyākatahetū? Kusalānaṃ vā dhammānaṃ vipākato kiriyābyākatesu vā dhammesu alobho, adoso, amoho – ime tayo abyākatahetū. Ime vuccanti "nava hetū".

**en** `1018246–1018931`
Therein, what are the nine roots? Three wholesome roots, three unwholesome roots, three neutral roots. ⤵ Therein, what are the three wholesome roots? Non-greed is a wholesome root, non-hate is a wholesome root, non-delusion is a wholesome root — these are the three wholesome roots. ⤵ Therein, what are the three unwholesome roots? Greed is an unwholesome root, hate is an unwholesome root, delusion is an unwholesome root — these are the three unwholesome roots. ⤵ Therein, what are the three neutral roots? Non-greed, non-hate, and non-delusion in the results of wholesome things or in functional neutral things — these are the three neutral roots. These are called "the nine roots".

Therein, what are the five aggregates in the material-form element? The aggregate of material form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness — these are called "the five aggregates in the material-form element". ⤵ Therein, what are the six sense-fields in the material-form element? The eye sense-field, the sight sense-field, the ear sense-field, the sound sense-field, the mind sense-field, the mental-object sense-field — these are called "the six sense-fields in the material-form element". ⤵ Therein, what are the nine elements in the material-form element? The eye element, the sight element, the eye-consciousness element, the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, the mind element, the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element — these are called "the nine elements in the material-form element". ⤵ Therein, what are the three truths in the material-form element? The truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, the truth of the path — these are called "the three truths in the material-form element". ⤵ Therein, what are the fourteen faculties in the material-form element? The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the mind faculty, the life faculty, the joy faculty, the equanimity faculty, the faculty of confidence, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known", the faculty of final knowledge, the faculty of one who has fully known — these are called "the fourteen faculties in the material-form element". ⤵ Therein, what are the eight roots in the material-form element? Three wholesome roots, two unwholesome roots, three neutral roots. ⤵ Therein, what are the three wholesome roots? Non-greed is a wholesome root, non-hate is a wholesome root, non-delusion is a wholesome root — these are the three wholesome roots. ⤵ Therein, what are the two unwholesome roots? Greed is an unwholesome root, delusion is an unwholesome root — these are the two unwholesome roots. ⤵ Therein, what are the three neutral roots? Non-greed, non-hate, and non-delusion in the results of wholesome things or in functional neutral things — these are the three neutral roots. These are called the eight roots in the material-form element. ⤵ Therein, what are the three nutriments in the material-form element? The nutriment of contact, the nutriment of mental intention, the nutriment of consciousness — these are called "the three nutriments in the material-form element". ⤵ Therein, what are the four contacts in the material-form element? Eye-contact, ear-contact, mind-element contact, mind-consciousness-element contact — these are called "the four contacts in the material-form element". ⤵ Therein, what are the four feelings in the material-form element… the four perceptions… the four intentions… the four minds? Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element — these are called "the four minds in the material-form element".

Apariyāpanne kati khandhā…pe… kati cittāni? ⤵ Apariyāpanne cattāro khandhā, dve āyatanāni, dve dhātuyo, dve saccāni, dvādasindriyāni, cha hetū, tayo āhārā, eko phasso, ekā vedanā, ekā saññā, ekā cetanā, ekaṃ cittaṃ.

**en** `1031012–1031308`
In what is not included in any sphere, how many aggregates are there… how many minds? ⤵ In what is not included there are four aggregates, two sense-fields, two elements, two truths, twelve faculties, six roots, three nutriments, one contact, one feeling, one perception, one intention, one mind.

### 1659

**pi** `703958–705467`
Tattha katame apariyāpanne cattāro khandhā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho , saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime vuccanti "apariyāpanne cattāro khandhā". ⤵ Tattha katamāni apariyāpanne dve āyatanāni? Manāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ – imāni vuccanti "apariyāpanne dve āyatanāni". ⤵ Tattha katamā apariyāpanne dve dhātuyo? Manoviññāṇadhātu, dhammadhātu – imā vuccanti "apariyāpanne dve dhātuyo". ⤵ Tattha katamāni apariyāpanne dve saccāni? Maggasaccaṃ, nirodhasaccaṃ – imāni vuccanti "apariyāpanne dve saccāni". ⤵ Tattha katamāni apariyāpanne dvādasindriyāni? Manindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ, saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ, anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ, aññindriyaṃ, aññātāvindriyaṃ – imāni vuccanti "apariyāpanne dvādasindriyāni". ⤵ Tattha katame apariyāpanne cha hetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū. ⤵ Tattha katame tayo kusalahetū? Alobho kusalahetu, adoso kusalahetu, amoho kusalahetu – ime tayo kusalahetū. ⤵ Tattha katame tayo abyākatahetū? Kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākato alobho, adoso, amoho – ime tayo abyākatahetū. Ime vuccanti "apariyāpanne cha hetū". ⤵ Tattha katame apariyāpanne tayo āhārā? Phassāhāro, manosañcetanāhāro, viññāṇāhāro – ime vuccanti "apariyāpanne tayo āhārā". ⤵ Tattha katamo apariyāpanne eko phasso? Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso – ayaṃ vuccati "apariyāpanne eko phasso". ⤵ Tattha katamā apariyāpanne ekā vedanā…pe… ekā saññā…pe… ekā cetanā…pe… ekaṃ cittaṃ? Manoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati "apariyāpanne ekaṃ cittaṃ".

**en** `1031309–1033636`
Therein, what are the four aggregates in what is not included? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness — these are called "the four aggregates in what is not included". ⤵ Therein, what are the two sense-fields in what is not included? The mind sense-field, the mental-object sense-field — these are called "the two sense-fields in what is not included". ⤵ Therein, what are the two elements in what is not included? The mind-consciousness element, the mental-object element — these are called "the two elements in what is not included". ⤵ Therein, what are the two truths in what is not included? The truth of the path, the truth of cessation — these are called "the two truths in what is not included". ⤵ Therein, what are the twelve faculties in what is not included? The mind faculty, the life faculty, the joy faculty, the equanimity faculty, the faculty of confidence, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known", the faculty of final knowledge, the faculty of one who has fully known — these are called "the twelve faculties in what is not included". ⤵ Therein, what are the six roots in what is not included? Three wholesome roots, three neutral roots. ⤵ Therein, what are the three wholesome roots? Non-greed is a wholesome root, non-hate is a wholesome root, non-delusion is a wholesome root — these are the three wholesome roots. ⤵ Therein, what are the three neutral roots? Non-greed, non-hate, and non-delusion in the results of wholesome things — these are the three neutral roots. These are called "the six roots in what is not included". ⤵ Therein, what are the three nutriments in what is not included? The nutriment of contact, the nutriment of mental intention, the nutriment of consciousness — these are called "the three nutriments in what is not included". ⤵ Therein, what is the one contact in what is not included? Mind-consciousness-element contact — this is called "the one contact in what is not included". ⤵ Therein, what is the one feeling in what is not included… the one perception… the one intention… the one mind? The mind-consciousness element — this is called "the one mind in what is not included".

Rūpakkhandho kāmadhātupariyāpanno; cattāro khandhā siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā. ⤵ Dasāyatanā kāmadhātupariyāpannā; dve āyatanā siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā. ⤵ Soḷasa dhātuyo kāmadhātupariyāpannā; dve dhātuyo siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā. ⤵ Samudayasaccaṃ kāmadhātupariyāpannaṃ; dve saccā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā; dukkhasaccaṃ siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannaṃ, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannaṃ. ⤵ Dasindriyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā; tīṇindriyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā; navindriyā siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā. ⤵ Tayo akusalahetū kāmadhātupariyāpannā; cha hetū siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā. ⤵ Kabaḷīkāro āhāro kāmadhātupariyāpanno; tayo āhārā siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā. ⤵ Cha phassā kāmadhātupariyāpannā; manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā kāmadhātu pariyāpanno, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpanno. ⤵ Cha vedanā…pe… cha saññā… cha cetanā… cha cittā kāmadhātupariyāpannā; manoviññāṇadhātu siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā.

**en** `1033993–1035835`
The aggregate of material form is included in the sense-pleasure element; four aggregates may be included in the sense-pleasure element, or may be not included in the sense-pleasure element. ⤵ Ten sense-fields are included in the sense-pleasure element; two sense-fields may be included in the sense-pleasure element, or may be not included in the sense-pleasure element. ⤵ Sixteen elements are included in the sense-pleasure element; two elements may be included in the sense-pleasure element, or may be not included in the sense-pleasure element. ⤵ The truth of the origin is included in the sense-pleasure element; two truths are not included in the sense-pleasure element; the truth of suffering may be included in the sense-pleasure element, or may be not included in the sense-pleasure element. ⤵ Ten faculties are included in the sense-pleasure element; three faculties are not included in the sense-pleasure element; nine faculties may be included in the sense-pleasure element, or may be not included in the sense-pleasure element. ⤵ Three unwholesome roots are included in the sense-pleasure element; six roots may be included in the sense-pleasure element, or may be not included in the sense-pleasure element. ⤵ The nutriment of solid food is included in the sense-pleasure element; three nutriments may be included in the sense-pleasure element, or may be not included in the sense-pleasure element. ⤵ Six contacts are included in the sense-pleasure element; mind-consciousness-element contact may be included in the sense-pleasure element, or may be not included in the sense-pleasure element. ⤵ Six feelings… six perceptions… six intentions… six minds are included in the sense-pleasure element; the mind-consciousness element may be included in the sense-pleasure element, or may be not included in the sense-pleasure element.

### 1675

**pi** `710203–711466`
Kāmadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe kati khandhā pātubhavanti…pe… kati cittāni pātubhavanti? ⤵ Kāmadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe sabbesaṃ pañcakkhandhā pātubhavanti; kassaci ekādasāyatanāni pātubhavanti; kassaci dasāyatanāni pātubhavanti; kassaci aparāni dasāyatanāni pātubhavanti; kassaci navāyatanāni pātubhavanti; kassaci sattāyatanāni pātubhavanti; kassaci ekādasa dhātuyo pātubhavanti; kassaci dasa dhātuyo pātubhavanti; kassaci aparā dasa dhātuyo pātubhavanti; kassaci nava dhātuyo pātubhavanti; kassaci satta dhātuyo pātubhavanti; sabbesaṃ ekaṃ saccaṃ pātubhavati; kassaci cuddasindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci terasindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci aparāni terasindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci dvādasindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci dasindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci navindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci aparāni navindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci aṭṭhindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci aparāni aṭṭhindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci sattindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci pañcindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci cattārindriyāni pātubhavanti; kassaci tayo hetū pātubhavanti; kassaci dve hetū pātubhavanti; kassaci [keci (syā.)] ahetukā pātubhavanti ; sabbesaṃ cattāro āhārā pātubhavanti; sabbesaṃ eko phasso pātubhavati; sabbesaṃ ekā vedanā… ekā saññā… ekā cetanā… ekaṃ cittaṃ pātubhavati.

**en** `1040960–1042204`
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-pleasure element, how many aggregates appear… how many minds appear? ⤵ At the moment of rebirth in the sense-pleasure element, for all beings five aggregates appear; for some, eleven sense-fields appear; for some, ten sense-fields appear; for some, another ten sense-fields appear; for some, nine sense-fields appear; for some, seven sense-fields appear; for some, eleven elements appear; for some, ten elements appear; for some, another ten elements appear; for some, nine elements appear; for some, seven elements appear; for all, one truth appears; for some, fourteen faculties appear; for some, thirteen faculties appear; for some, another thirteen faculties appear; for some, twelve faculties appear; for some, ten faculties appear; for some, nine faculties appear; for some, another nine faculties appear; for some, eight faculties appear; for some, another eight faculties appear; for some, seven faculties appear; for some, five faculties appear; for some, four faculties appear; for some, three roots appear; for some, two roots appear; some appear without roots; for all, four nutriments appear; for all, one contact appears; for all, one feeling… one perception… one intention… one mind appears.

### 1676

**pi** `711467–711640`
Kāmadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe sabbesaṃ katame pañcakkhandhā pātubhavanti? Rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho – kāmadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe sabbesaṃ ime pañcakkhandhā pātubhavanti.

**en** `1042205–1042457`
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-pleasure element, which five aggregates appear for all? The aggregate of material form… the aggregate of consciousness — at the moment of rebirth in the sense-pleasure element, these five aggregates appear for all.

### 1677

**pi** `711641–713695`
Kāmadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe kassa ekādasāyatanāni pātubhavanti? For womb-born beings without roots, setting aside those without sex, at the moment of rebirth five faculties appear: the body faculty, the mind faculty, the faculty of femininity or the faculty of masculinity, the life faculty, the equanimity faculty. At the moment of rebirth in the sense-pleasure element, these five faculties appear for them. ⤵ At the moment of rebirth in the sense-pleasure element, for whom do four faculties appear? For womb-born beings without roots and without sex, at the moment of rebirth four faculties appear: the body faculty, the mind faculty, the life faculty, the equanimity faculty. At the moment of rebirth in the sense-pleasure element, these four faculties appear for them.

Kāmāvacarā dhammā, na kāmāvacarā dhammā, rūpāvacarā dhammā, na rūpāvacarā dhammā, arūpāvacarā dhammā, na arūpāvacarā dhammā, pariyāpannā dhammā, apariyāpannā dhammā. ⤵ Katame dhammā kāmāvacarā? Heṭṭhato avīcinirayaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā, uparito paranimmitavasavattī deve antokaritvā, yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā khandhadhātuāyatanā; rūpaṃ, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā kāmāvacarā. ⤵ Katame dhammā na kāmāvacarā? Rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā – ime dhammā na kāmāvacarā. ⤵ Katame dhammā rūpāvacarā? Heṭṭhato brahmalokaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā, uparito akaniṭṭhe deve antokaritvā , yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa vā cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā rūpāvacarā. ⤵ Katame dhammā na rūpāvacarā? Kāmāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā – ime dhammā na rūpāvacarā. ⤵ Katame dhammā arūpāvacarā? Heṭṭhato ākāsānañcāyatanūpage deve pariyantaṃ karitvā, uparito nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpage deve antokaritvā, yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa vā cittacetasikā dhammā – ime dhammā arūpāvacarā. ⤵ Katame dhammā na arūpāvacarā? Kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, apariyāpannā – ime dhammā na arūpāvacarā. ⤵ Katame dhammā pariyāpannā? Sāsavā kusalākusalabyākatā dhammā kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime dhammā pariyāpannā. ⤵ Katame dhammā apariyāpannā? Maggā ca, maggaphalāni ca, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu – ime dhammā apariyāpannā.

**en** `1063298–1065892`
There are things of the sense sphere and things not of the sense sphere; things of the fine-material sphere and things not of the fine-material sphere; things of the immaterial sphere and things not of the immaterial sphere; things included in a sphere and things not included in any sphere. ⤵ Which things are of the sense sphere? Taking as the lower limit the Avīci hell below, and taking as the upper limit the gods who wield power over others' creations, the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields that move in this interval and are included here — material form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness — these things are of the sense sphere. ⤵ Which things are not of the sense sphere? Things of the fine-material sphere, things of the immaterial sphere, and things not included in any sphere — these things are not of the sense sphere. ⤵ Which things are of the fine-material sphere? Taking as the lower limit the Brahmā world below, and taking as the upper limit the Akaniṭṭha gods above, the mind and mental factors of one who has attained, or one who has been reborn there, or one dwelling happily in this very life, that move in this interval and are included here — these things are of the fine-material sphere. ⤵ Which things are not of the fine-material sphere? Things of the sense sphere, things of the immaterial sphere, and things not included in any sphere — these things are not of the fine-material sphere. ⤵ Which things are of the immaterial sphere? Taking as the lower limit the gods who have reached the field of infinite space below, and taking as the upper limit the gods who have reached the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception above, the mind and mental factors of one who has attained, or one who has been reborn there, or one dwelling happily in this very life, that move in this interval and are included here — these things are of the immaterial sphere. ⤵ Which things are not of the immaterial sphere? Things of the sense sphere, things of the fine-material sphere, and things not included in any sphere — these things are not of the immaterial sphere. ⤵ Which things are included? The wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral things subject to mental taints, of the sense sphere, the fine-material sphere, and the immaterial sphere: the aggregate of material form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness — these things are included. ⤵ Which things are not included? The paths, the fruits of the paths, and the unconditioned element — these things are not included.

"Gods": there are three kinds of gods — gods by convention, gods by rebirth, gods by purity. ⤵ Gods by convention are kings, queens, and princes. ⤵ Gods by rebirth are the gods from the realm of the Four Great Kings upwards. ⤵ Gods by purity are the arahants. ⤵ Having given gifts, undertaken virtue, and kept the observance day, where are beings reborn? Having given gifts, undertaken virtue, and kept the observance day, some are reborn in the company of wealthy nobles, some are reborn in the company of wealthy brahmins, some are reborn in the company of wealthy householders, some are reborn in the company of the gods of the Four Great Kings, some are reborn in the company of the gods of the Thirty-Three, some are reborn in the company of the Yāma gods, some are reborn in the company of the Tusita gods, some are reborn in the company of the gods who delight in creating, some are reborn in the company of the gods who wield power over others' creations.
