### 1700

**pi** `729445–731683`
Cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ kittakaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ? Yāni mānusakāni paññāsa vassāni, cātummahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ eso eko rattindivo [rattidivo (ka.) a. ni. 3.71]. Tāya rattiyā tiṃsa rattiyo māso. Tena māsena dvādasamāsiyo saṃvaccharo. Tena saṃvaccharena dibbāni pañca vassasatāni cātummahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ. Manussānaṃ gaṇanāya kittakaṃ hoti? Navuti vassasatasahassāni. ⤵ Tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ kittakaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ? Yaṃ mānusakaṃ vassasataṃ, tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ eso eko rattindivo. Tāya rattiyā tiṃsa rattiyo māso. Tena māsena dvādasamāsiyo saṃvaccharo. Tena saṃvaccharena dibbaṃ vassasahassaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ. Manussānaṃ gaṇanāya kittakaṃ hoti? Tisso ca vassakoṭiyo saṭṭhi ca vassasatasahassāni. ⤵ Yāmānaṃ devānaṃ kittakaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ? Yāni mānusakāni dve vassasatāni, yāmānaṃ devānaṃ eso eko rattindivo. Tāya rattiyā tiṃsarattiyo māso . Tena māsena dvādasamāsiyo saṃvaccharo. Tena saṃvaccharena dibbāni dve vassasahassāni yāmānaṃ devānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ. Manussānaṃ gaṇanāya kittakaṃ hoti? Cuddasañca vassakoṭiyo cattārīsañca vassasatasahassāni. ⤵ Tusitānaṃ devānaṃ kittakaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ? Yāni mānusakāni cattāri vassasatāni, tusitānaṃ devānaṃ eso eko rattindivo. Tāya rattiyā tiṃsarattiyo māso. Tena māsena dvādasamāsiyo saṃvaccharo. Tena saṃvaccharena dibbāni cattāri vassasahassāni tusitānaṃ devānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ. Manussānaṃ gaṇanāya kittakaṃ hoti? Sattapaññāsa vassakoṭiyo saṭṭhi ca vassasatasahassāni. ⤵ Nimmānaratīnaṃ devānaṃ kittakaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ? Yāni mānusakāni aṭṭha vassasatāni, nimmānaratīnaṃ devānaṃ eso eko rattindivo. Tāya rattiyā tiṃsarattiyo māso. Tena māsena dvādasamāsiyo saṃvaccharo. Tena saṃvaccharena dibbāni aṭṭha vassasahassāni nimmānaratīnaṃ devānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ. Manussānaṃ gaṇanāya kittakaṃ hoti? Dve vassakoṭisatāni tiṃsañca vassakoṭiyo cattārīsañca vassasatasahassāni. ⤵ Paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ kittakaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ? Yāni mānusakāni soḷasa vassasatāni, paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ eso eko rattindivo. Tāya rattiyā tiṃsarattiyo māso. Tena māsena dvādasamāsiyo saṃvaccharo. Tena saṃvaccharena dibbāni soḷasa vassasahassāni paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ. Manussānaṃ gaṇanāya kittakaṃ hoti? Nava ca vassakoṭisatāni ekavīsañca vassakoṭiyo saṭṭhi ca vassasatasahassānīti.

**en** `1067315–1069545`
What is the measure of life of the gods of the Four Great Kings? Fifty human years are one day and night of the gods of the Four Great Kings. Thirty such nights make a month; twelve such months make a year; five hundred such divine years are the measure of life of the gods of the Four Great Kings. How much is that in human reckoning? Nine million years. ⤵ What is the measure of life of the gods of the Thirty-Three? One hundred human years are one day and night of the gods of the Thirty-Three. Thirty such nights make a month; twelve such months make a year; one thousand such divine years are the measure of life of the gods of the Thirty-Three. How much is that in human reckoning? Thirty-six million years. ⤵ What is the measure of life of the Yāma gods? Two hundred human years are one day and night of the Yāma gods. Thirty such nights make a month; twelve such months make a year; two thousand such divine years are the measure of life of the Yāma gods. How much is that in human reckoning? One hundred and forty-four million years. ⤵ What is the measure of life of the Tusita gods? Four hundred human years are one day and night of the Tusita gods. Thirty such nights make a month; twelve such months make a year; four thousand such divine years are the measure of life of the Tusita gods. How much is that in human reckoning? Five hundred and seventy-six million years. ⤵ What is the measure of life of the gods who delight in creating? Eight hundred human years are one day and night of the gods who delight in creating. Thirty such nights make a month; twelve such months make a year; eight thousand such divine years are the measure of life of the gods who delight in creating. How much is that in human reckoning? Two thousand three hundred and four million years. ⤵ What is the measure of life of the gods who wield power over others' creations? Sixteen hundred human years are one day and night of the gods who wield power over others' creations. Thirty such nights make a month; twelve such months make a year; sixteen thousand such divine years are the measure of life of the gods who wield power over others' creations. How much is that in human reckoning? Nine thousand two hundred and sixteen million years.

Kappassa tatiyo bhāgo. ⤵ Paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ majjhimaṃ bhāvetvā kattha upapajjanti? Paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ majjhimaṃ bhāvetvā brahmapurohitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti. Tesaṃ kittakaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ? Kappo [eko kappo (syā.)].

**en** `1069546–1070370`
Having developed the first meditative absorption to a limited degree, where are they reborn? Having developed the first meditative absorption to a limited degree, they are reborn in the company of the gods of Brahmā's retinue. What is their measure of life? A third part of an eon. ⤵ Having developed the first meditative absorption to a middling degree, where are they reborn? Having developed the first meditative absorption to a middling degree, they are reborn in the company of the gods who are Brahmā's ministers. What is their measure of life? Half an eon. ⤵ Having developed the first meditative absorption to a refined degree, where are they reborn? Having developed the first meditative absorption to a refined degree, they are reborn in the company of the Great Brahmā gods. What is their measure of life? An eon.

Having developed the fourth meditative absorption — according to the difference of object, the difference of attention, the difference of desire, the difference of aspiration, the difference of decision, the difference of resolve, the difference of wisdom — some are reborn in the company of the non-percipient gods, some in the company of the Vehapphala gods, some in the company of the Aviha gods, some in the company of the Atappa gods, some in the company of the Sudassa gods, some in the company of the Sudassī gods, some in the company of the Akaniṭṭha gods, some in the company of the gods who have reached the field of infinite space, some in the company of the gods who have reached the field of infinite consciousness, some in the company of the gods who have reached the field of nothingness, some in the company of the gods who have reached the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. ⤵ What is the measure of life of the non-percipient gods and the Vehapphala gods? ### 1712

**pi** `735274–735592`
Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati abhiññeyyā, kati pariññeyyā, kati pahātabbā, kati bhāvetabbā, kati sacchikātabbā, kati na pahātabbā, na bhāvetabbā, na sacchikātabbā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati abhiññeyyā, kati pariññeyyā, kati pahātabbā, kati bhāvetabbā, kati sacchikātabbā, kati na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā?

**en** `1074517–1075040`
Of the five aggregates, how many are to be directly known, how many are to be fully understood, how many are to be abandoned, how many are to be developed, how many are to be realised, how many are neither to be abandoned, nor to be developed, nor to be realised… of the seven minds, how many are to be directly known, how many are to be fully understood, how many are to be abandoned, how many are to be developed, how many are to be realised, how many are neither to be abandoned, nor to be developed, nor to be realised?

### 1713

**pi** `735593–738326`
Rūpakkhandho abhiññeyyo pariññeyyo na pahātabbo na bhāvetabbo na sacchikātabbo. Cattāro khandhā abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā, siyā pahātabbā, siyā bhāvetabbā, siyā sacchikātabbā, siyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā. ⤵ Dasāyatanā abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā. Dve āyatanā abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā, siyā pahātabbā, siyā bhāvetabbā, siyā sacchikātabbā, siyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā. ⤵ Soḷasa dhātuyo abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā. Dve dhātuyo abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā, siyā pahātabbā, siyā bhāvetabbā, siyā sacchikātabbā, siyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā. ⤵ Samudayasaccaṃ abhiññeyyaṃ pariññeyyaṃ pahātabbaṃ na bhāvetabbaṃ na sacchikātabbaṃ. Maggasaccaṃ abhiññeyyaṃ pariññeyyaṃ na pahātabbaṃ bhāvetabbaṃ na sacchikātabbaṃ . Nirodhasaccaṃ abhiññeyyaṃ pariññeyyaṃ na pahātabbaṃ na bhāvetabbaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ abhiññeyyaṃ pariññeyyaṃ, siyā pahātabbaṃ, na bhāvetabbaṃ, na sacchikātabbaṃ, siyā na pahātabbaṃ. ⤵ Navindriyā abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā. Domanassindriyaṃ abhiññeyyaṃ pariññeyyaṃ pahātabbaṃ na bhāvetabbaṃ na sacchikātabbaṃ. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ abhiññeyyaṃ pariññeyyaṃ na pahātabbaṃ bhāvetabbaṃ na sacchikātabbaṃ. Aññindriyaṃ abhiññeyyaṃ pariññeyyaṃ na pahātabbaṃ, siyā bhāvetabbaṃ, siyā sacchikātabbaṃ. Aññātāvindriyaṃ abhiññeyyaṃ pariññeyyaṃ na pahātabbaṃ na bhāvetabbaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ. Tīṇindriyā abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā na pahātabbā, siyā bhāvetabbā, siyā sacchikātabbā, siyā na bhāvetabbā, sacchikātabbā. Cha indriyā abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā, siyā pahātabbā, siyā bhāvetabbā, siyā sacchikātabbā, siyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā. ⤵ Tayo akusalahetū abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā. Tayo kusalahetū abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā na pahātabbā, siyā bhāvetabbā, na sacchikātabbā, siyā na bhāvetabbā. Tayo abyākatahetū abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā, siyā sacchikātabbā , siyā na sacchikātabbā. ⤵ Kabaḷīkāro āhāro abhiññeyyo pariññeyyo na pahātabbo na bhāvetabbo na sacchikātabbo. Tayo āhārā abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā, siyā pahātabbā, siyā bhāvetabbā, siyā sacchikātabbā, siyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā. ⤵ Cha phassā abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso abhiññeyyo pariññeyyo, siyā pahātabbo, siyā bhāvetabbo, siyā sacchikātabbo, siyā na pahātabbo na bhāvetabbo na sacchikātabbo. ⤵ Cha vedanā…pe… cha saññā… cha cetanā… cha cittā abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā. Manoviññāṇadhātu abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā, siyā pahātabbā, siyā bhāvetabbā, siyā sacchikātabbā , siyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā.

**en** `1075041–1079467`
The aggregate of material form is to be directly known and fully understood; it is not to be abandoned, not to be developed, not to be realised. Four aggregates are to be directly known and fully understood; they may be to be abandoned, may be to be developed, may be to be realised, or may be neither to be abandoned, nor to be developed, nor to be realised. ⤵ Ten sense-fields are to be directly known and fully understood; they are not to be abandoned, not to be developed, not to be realised. Two sense-fields are to be directly known and fully understood; they may be to be abandoned, may be to be developed, may be to be realised, or may be neither to be abandoned, nor to be developed, nor to be realised. ⤵ Sixteen elements are to be directly known and fully understood; they are not to be abandoned, not to be developed, not to be realised. Two elements are to be directly known and fully understood; they may be to be abandoned, may be to be developed, may be to be realised, or may be neither to be abandoned, nor to be developed, nor to be realised. ⤵ The truth of the origin is to be directly known, fully understood, and abandoned; it is not to be developed, not to be realised. The truth of the path is to be directly known and fully understood; it is not to be abandoned; it is to be developed; it is not to be realised. The truth of cessation is to be directly known and fully understood; it is not to be abandoned, not to be developed; it is to be realised. The truth of suffering is to be directly known and fully understood; it may be to be abandoned, it is not to be developed, not to be realised, or it may be not to be abandoned. ⤵ Nine faculties are to be directly known and fully understood; they are not to be abandoned, not to be developed, not to be realised. The grief faculty is to be directly known, fully understood, and abandoned; it is not to be developed, not to be realised. The faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known" is to be directly known and fully understood; it is not to be abandoned; it is to be developed; it is not to be realised. The faculty of final knowledge is to be directly known and fully understood; it is not to be abandoned; it may be to be developed, or may be to be realised. The faculty of one who has fully known is to be directly known and fully understood; it is not to be abandoned, not to be developed; it is to be realised. Three faculties are to be directly known and fully understood; they are not to be abandoned; they may be to be developed, may be to be realised, or may be not to be developed but to be realised. Six faculties are to be directly known and fully understood; they may be to be abandoned, may be to be developed, may be to be realised, or may be neither to be abandoned, nor to be developed, nor to be realised. ⤵ Three unwholesome roots are to be directly known, fully understood, and abandoned; they are not to be developed, not to be realised. Three wholesome roots are to be directly known and fully understood; they are not to be abandoned; they may be to be developed, are not to be realised, or may be not to be developed. Three neutral roots are to be directly known and fully understood; they are not to be abandoned, not to be developed; they may be to be realised, or may be not to be realised. ⤵ The nutriment of solid food is to be directly known and fully understood; it is not to be abandoned, not to be developed, not to be realised. Three nutriments are to be directly known and fully understood; they may be to be abandoned, may be to be developed, may be to be realised, or may be neither to be abandoned, nor to be developed, nor to be realised. ⤵ Six contacts are to be directly known and fully understood; they are not to be abandoned, not to be developed, not to be realised. Mind-consciousness-element contact is to be directly known and fully understood; it may be to be abandoned, may be to be developed, may be to be realised, or may be neither to be abandoned, nor to be developed, nor to be realised. ⤵ Six feelings… six perceptions… six intentions… six minds are to be directly known and fully understood; they are not to be abandoned, not to be developed, not to be realised. ### 1714

**pi** `738327–738361`
<h1>8. Sārammaṇānārammaṇavāro</h1>

**en** `1079468–1079532`
<h1>8. The Section on Having Objects and Not Having Objects</h1>

### 1715

**pi** `738362–738470`
Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati sārammaṇā, kati anārammaṇā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati sārammaṇā, kati anārammaṇā?

**en** `1079533–1079682`
Of the five aggregates, how many have objects, how many are without objects… of the seven minds, how many have objects, how many are without objects?

### 1716

**pi** `738471–739065`
Rūpakkhandho anārammaṇo. Cattāro khandhā sārammaṇā. ⤵ Dasāyatanā anārammaṇā. Manāyatanaṃ sārammaṇaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā sārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇaṃ. ⤵ Dasa dhātuyo anārammaṇā. Satta dhātuyo sārammaṇā. Dhammadhātu siyā sārammaṇā, siyā anārammaṇā. ⤵ Dve saccā sārammaṇā. Nirodhasaccaṃ anārammaṇaṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā sārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇaṃ. ⤵ Sattindriyā anārammaṇā. Cuddasindriyā sārammaṇā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā sārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇaṃ. Nava hetū sārammaṇā. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro anārammaṇo. Tayo āhārā sārammaṇā. Satta phassā… satta vedanā… satta saññā… satta cetanā… satta cittā sārammaṇā.

**en** `1079683–1080543`
The aggregate of material form is without an object. Four aggregates have objects. ⤵ Ten sense-fields are without objects. The mind sense-field has an object. The mental-object sense-field may have an object, or may be without an object. ⤵ Ten elements are without objects. Seven elements have objects. The mental-object element may have an object, or may be without an object. ⤵ Two truths have objects. The truth of cessation is without an object. The truth of suffering may have an object, or may be without an object. ⤵ Seven faculties are without objects. Fourteen faculties have objects. The life faculty may have an object, or may be without an object. Nine roots have objects. The nutriment of solid food is without an object. Three nutriments have objects. Seven contacts… seven feelings… seven perceptions… seven intentions… seven minds have objects.

### 1717

**pi** `739066–739202`
Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati sārammaṇārammaṇā, kati anārammaṇārammaṇā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati sārammaṇārammaṇā, kati anārammaṇārammaṇā?

**en** `1080544–1080801`
Of the five aggregates, how many have things-with-objects as their objects, how many have things-without-objects as their objects… of the seven minds, how many have things-with-objects as their objects, how many have things-without-objects as their objects?

### 1718

**pi** `739203–740433`
Rūpakkhandho anārammaṇo. Cattāro khandhā siyā sārammaṇārammaṇā, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇā. ⤵ Dasāyatanā anārammaṇā. Manāyatanaṃ siyā sārammaṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā sārammaṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇaṃ. ⤵ Dasa dhātuyo anārammaṇā. Cha dhātuyo anārammaṇārammaṇā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā sārammaṇārammaṇā, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇā. Dhammadhātu siyā sārammaṇārammaṇā, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇā, siyā anārammaṇā. ⤵ Nirodhasaccaṃ anārammaṇaṃ. Maggasaccaṃ anārammaṇārammaṇaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ siyā sārammaṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇaṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā sārammaṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇaṃ. ⤵ Sattindriyā anārammaṇā. Pañcindriyā anārammaṇārammaṇā. Navindriyā siyā sārammaṇārammaṇā, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā sārammaṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇaṃ. ⤵ Nava hetū siyā sārammaṇārammaṇā, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇā. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro anārammaṇo. Tayo āhārā siyā sārammaṇārammaṇā, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇā. Cha phassā anārammaṇārammaṇā . Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā sārammaṇārammaṇo siyā anārammaṇārammaṇo. Cha vedanā… cha saññā… cha cetanā… cha cittā anārammaṇārammaṇā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā sārammaṇārammaṇā, siyā anārammaṇārammaṇā.

**en** `1080802–1083061`
The aggregate of material form is without an object. Four aggregates may have things-with-objects as their objects, or may have things-without-objects as their objects. ⤵ Ten sense-fields are without objects. The mind sense-field may have things-with-objects as its object, or may have things-without-objects as its object. The mental-object sense-field may have things-with-objects as its object, may have things-without-objects as its object, or may be without an object. ⤵ Ten elements are without objects. Six elements have things-without-objects as their objects. The mind-consciousness element may have things-with-objects as its object, or may have things-without-objects as its object. The mental-object element may have things-with-objects as its object, may have things-without-objects as its object, or may be without an object. ⤵ The truth of cessation is without an object. The truth of the path has things-without-objects as its object. The truth of the origin may have things-with-objects as its object, or may have things-without-objects as its object. The truth of suffering may have things-with-objects as its object, may have things-without-objects as its object, or may be without an object. ⤵ Seven faculties are without objects. Five faculties have things-without-objects as their objects. Nine faculties may have things-with-objects as their objects, or may have things-without-objects as their objects. The life faculty may have things-with-objects as its object, may have things-without-objects as its object, or may be without an object. ⤵ Nine roots may have things-with-objects as their objects, or may have things-without-objects as their objects. The nutriment of solid food is without an object. Three nutriments may have things-with-objects as their objects, or may have things-without-objects as their objects. Six contacts have things-without-objects as their objects. Mind-consciousness-element contact may have things-with-objects as its object, or may have things-without-objects as its object. Six feelings… six perceptions… six intentions… six minds have things-without-objects as their objects. The mind-consciousness element may have things-with-objects as its object, or may have things-without-objects as its object.

### 1719

**pi** `740434–740469`

### 1720

**pi** `740470–740696`
Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati diṭṭhā, kati sutā, kati mutā, kati viññātā, kati na diṭṭhā na sutā na mutā na viññātā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati diṭṭhā, kati sutā, kati mutā, kati viññātā, kati na diṭṭhā na sutā na mutā na viññātā?

**en** `1083128–1083453`
Of the five aggregates, how many are seen, how many are heard, how many are sensed, how many are known, how many are neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known… of the seven minds, how many are seen, how many are heard, how many are sensed, how many are known, how many are neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known?

### 1721

**pi** `740697–741753`
Rūpakkhandho siyā diṭṭho, siyā suto, siyā muto, siyā viññāto, siyā na diṭṭho na suto na muto, viññāto. Cattāro khandhā na diṭṭhā na sutā na mutā, viññātā. ⤵ Rūpāyatanaṃ diṭṭhaṃ, na sutaṃ na mutaṃ, viññātaṃ. Saddāyatanaṃ na diṭṭhaṃ, sutaṃ, na mutaṃ, viññātaṃ. Gandhāyatanaṃ… rasāyatanaṃ… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ na diṭṭhaṃ na sutaṃ, mutaṃ, viññātaṃ. Sattāyatanā na diṭṭhā na sutā na mutā, viññātā. ⤵ Rūpadhātu diṭṭhā, na sutā na mutā, viññātā. Saddadhātu na diṭṭhā, sutā, na mutā, viññātā. Gandhadhātu… rasadhātu… phoṭṭhabbadhātu na diṭṭhā na sutā, mutā, viññātā. Terasa dhātuyo na diṭṭhā na sutā na mutā, viññātā. ⤵ Tīṇi saccāni na diṭṭhā na sutā na mutā, viññātā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā diṭṭhaṃ, siyā sutaṃ, siyā mutaṃ, siyā viññātaṃ, siyā na diṭṭhaṃ na sutaṃ na mutaṃ, viññātaṃ. ⤵ Bāvīsatindriyā na diṭṭhā na sutā na mutā, viññātā. Nava hetū na diṭṭhā na sutā na mutā, viññātā. Cattāro āhārā na diṭṭhā na sutā na mutā, viññātā. Satta phassā na diṭṭhā na sutā na mutā, viññātā. Satta vedanā… satta saññā… satta cetanā… satta cittā na diṭṭhā na sutā na mutā, viññātā.

**en** `1083454–1084921`
The aggregate of material form may be seen, may be heard, may be sensed, may be known, or may be neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known. Four aggregates are neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known. ⤵ The sight sense-field is seen, not heard, not sensed, but known. The sound sense-field is not seen, but heard, not sensed, but known. The smell sense-field… the taste sense-field… the tangible sense-field are not seen, not heard, but sensed and known. Seven sense-fields are neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known. ⤵ The sight element is seen, not heard, not sensed, but known. The sound element is not seen, but heard, not sensed, but known. The smell element… the taste element… the tangible element are not seen, not heard, but sensed and known. Thirteen elements are neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known. ⤵ Three truths are neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known. The truth of suffering may be seen, may be heard, may be sensed, may be known, or may be neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known. ⤵ The twenty-two faculties are neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known. The nine roots are neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known. The four nutriments are neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known. The seven contacts are neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known. The seven feelings… the seven perceptions… the seven intentions… the seven minds are neither seen, nor heard, nor sensed, but known.

### 1724

**pi** `741810–742844`
Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā? ⤵ Rūpakkhandho abyākato. Cattāro khandhā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Dasāyatanā abyākatā. Dvāyatanā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Soḷasa dhātuyo abyākatā. Dve dhātuyo siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Samudayasaccaṃ akusalaṃ. Maggasaccaṃ kusalaṃ. Nirodhasaccaṃ abyākataṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā kusalaṃ, siyā akusalaṃ, siyā abyākataṃ. ⤵ Dasindriyā abyākatā. Domanassindriyaṃ akusalaṃ. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ kusalaṃ. Cattārindriyā siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Cha indriyā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. ⤵ Tayo kusalahetū kusalā. Tayo akusalahetū akusalā. Tayo abyākatahetū abyākatā. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro abyākato. Tayo āhārā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Cha phassā abyākatā. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā kusalo, siyā akusalo, siyā abyākato. Cha vedanā… cha saññā… cha cetanā… cha cittā abyākatā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā.

**en** `1085011–1086450`
Of the five aggregates, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral… of the seven minds, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral? ⤵ The aggregate of material form is neutral. Four aggregates may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be neutral. Ten sense-fields are neutral. Two sense-fields may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be neutral. Sixteen elements are neutral. Two elements may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be neutral. The truth of the origin is unwholesome. The truth of the path is wholesome. The truth of cessation is neutral. The truth of suffering may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be neutral. ⤵ Ten faculties are neutral. The grief faculty is unwholesome. The faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known" is wholesome. Four faculties may be wholesome, or may be neutral. Six faculties may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be neutral. ⤵ Three wholesome roots are wholesome. Three unwholesome roots are unwholesome. Three neutral roots are neutral. The nutriment of solid food is neutral. Three nutriments may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be neutral. Six contacts are neutral. Mind-consciousness-element contact may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be neutral. Six feelings… six perceptions… six intentions… six minds are neutral. The mind-consciousness element may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be neutral.

### 1726

**pi** `742869–746906`
Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, kati dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, kati adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, kati dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, kati adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā? ⤵ Dve khandhā na vattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi. Tayo khandhā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. ⤵ Dasāyatanā na vattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi. Manāyatanaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi. ⤵ Dasa dhātuyo na vattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi. Pañca dhātuyo adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, kāyaviññāṇadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Dhammadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā na vattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi. ⤵ Dve saccā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Nirodhasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi. ⤵ Dvādasindriyā na vattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi. Cha indriyā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Tīṇindriyā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā , siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi. ⤵ Doso akusalahetu dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto. Cuddasindriyā arūpā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā rūpaṃ, siyā arūpaṃ. Nava hetū arūpā. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro rūpaṃ. Tayo āhārā arūpā. Satta phassā arūpā. Satta vedanā… satta saññā… satta cetanā satta cittā arūpā.

**en** `1102265–1103182`
Of the five aggregates, how many are material, how many immaterial… of the seven minds, how many are material, how many immaterial? ⤵ The aggregate of material form is material. Four aggregates are immaterial. Ten sense-fields are material. The mind sense-field is immaterial. The mental-object sense-field may be material, or may be immaterial. Ten elements are material. Seven elements are immaterial. The mental-object element may be material, or may be immaterial. Three truths are immaterial. The truth of suffering may be material, or may be immaterial. Seven faculties are material. Fourteen faculties are immaterial. The life faculty may be material, or may be immaterial. The nine roots are immaterial. The nutriment of solid food is material. Three nutriments are immaterial. The seven contacts are immaterial. The seven feelings… the seven perceptions… the seven intentions… the seven minds are immaterial.

### 1735

**en** `1103183–1103212`

### 1736

**pi** `753436–753524`
Abhiññā dve sārammaṇā, diṭṭhā kusalavedanā; ⤵ Vipākā ca upādinnā, vitakkaṃ rūpalokiyāti.

**en** `1103213–1103362`
The direct knowledges, the two on objects, the seen, the wholesome, feeling; ⤵ The results and the taken-up, thought, material form, and the worldly.

### 1737

**pi** `753525–754608`
Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati lokiyā, kati lokuttarā? Dvādasannaṃ āyatanānaṃ kati lokiyā, kati lokuttarā? Aṭṭhārasannaṃ dhātūnaṃ kati lokiyā, kati lokuttarā? Catunnaṃ saccānaṃ kati lokiyā, kati lokuttarā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati lokiyā, kati lokuttarā? ⤵ Rūpakkhandho lokiyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Dasāyatanā lokiyā . Dve āyatanā siyā lokiyā , siyā lokuttarā. Soḷasa dhātuyo lokiyā. Dve dhātuyo siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Dve saccā lokiyā. Dve saccā lokuttarā. ⤵ Dasindriyā lokiyā. Tīṇindriyā lokuttarā. Navindriyā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Tayo akusalahetū lokiyā. Cha hetū siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro lokiyo. Tayo āhārā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā . Cha phassā lokiyā. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā lokiyo, siyā lokuttaro. Cha vedanā lokiyā. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā vedanā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Cha saññā lokiyā. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Cha cetanā lokiyā. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Cha cittā lokiyā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarāti.

**en** `1103363–1104959`
Of the five aggregates, how many are worldly, how many beyond the world? Of the twelve sense-fields, how many are worldly, how many beyond the world? Of the eighteen elements, how many are worldly, how many beyond the world? Of the four truths, how many are worldly, how many beyond the world… of the seven minds, how many are worldly, how many beyond the world? ⤵ The aggregate of material form is worldly. Four aggregates may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. Ten sense-fields are worldly. Two sense-fields may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. Sixteen elements are worldly. Two elements may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. Two truths are worldly. Two truths are beyond the world. ⤵ Ten faculties are worldly. Three faculties are beyond the world. Nine faculties may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. Three unwholesome roots are worldly. Six roots may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. The nutriment of solid food is worldly. Three nutriments may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. Six contacts are worldly. Mind-consciousness-element contact may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. Six feelings are worldly. Feeling born of mind-consciousness-element contact may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. Six perceptions are worldly. Perception born of mind-consciousness-element contact may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. Six intentions are worldly. Intention born of mind-consciousness-element contact may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. Six minds are worldly. The mind-consciousness element may be worldly, or may be beyond the world.
